33:1: Surah Al-Ahzab Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Hisham told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur, who said: Ubayy bin Ka’b said to me: How often do you recite Surat Al-Ahzab or how often do you count it? I said: Seventy-three verses. He said: I have seen it, and it is equivalent to Surat Al-Baqarah. We read in it: “If an old man and an old woman commit adultery, stone them both. It is a punishment from God. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Abi An-Najud, who is Ibn Bahdalah, with him. This is a good chain of transmission, and it indicates that there was a Qur’an in it, then its wording and its ruling were abrogated. And God knows best. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful This is a warning of the higher over the lower, for if God, the Almighty, commands His servant and messenger to do this, then it is even more appropriate for him to command others besides Him to do so. Talq ibn Habib said: “Taqwa is to act in obedience to God with the light from God, hoping for His reward, and to abandon disobedience to God with the light from God, fearing God’s punishment. “And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites” meaning do not listen to them or consult them. Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise meaning He is most deserving of your following His commands and obeying Him, for He is All-Knowing of the consequences of things and is Wise in His words and deeds. For this reason God, the Almighty, said: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord meaning from the Quran and Sunnah. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted meaning nothing is hidden from Him. And put your trust in God, meaning in all your affairs and conditions. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs meaning, and sufficient is He as a Disposer of affairs for whoever puts his trust in Him and turns to Him.

33:4: God Almighty says, before the moral purpose, a matter known by the senses, which is that just as one person does not have two hearts in his body, and his wife from whom he swears an oath of divorce by saying, You are to me like the back of my mother does not become his mother, likewise an adopted child does not become a man’s son if he adopts him and calls him his son. He said, God has not made for any man two hearts within him, nor has He made your wives from whom you swear an oath of divorce your mothers, like His Almighty saying, “They are not their mothers. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them.” God the Almighty said: And He has not made your adopted sons your sons. This is what is meant by the negation, as it was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him, the freed slave of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had adopted him before his prophethood, so he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. God the Almighty wanted to cut off this attachment and this relationship by saying: And He has not made your adopted sons your sons. As God the Almighty said in the middle of the surah: “Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. And God is Knowing of all things.” And He said here: That is but your statement from your mouths, meaning your adoption of them is a statement that does not require him to be a real son, as he was created from the loins of another man. It is not possible for there to be two parents, just as it is not possible for one human being to have two hearts. And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: He speaks the truth, meaning justice. Qatadah said: And He guides to the way, meaning the straight path. More than one person has mentioned that this verse was revealed about a man from Quraysh who was called Dhu al-Qalbain the one with two hearts, and that he claimed that he had two hearts, each with a great intellect, so God revealed this verse in refutation of him. This is what Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it was also said by Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah, and it was the preferred version of Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Qabus, meaning Ibn Abi Dhibyan, who said: His father told him, saying: I said to Ibn Abbas: Tell me about the statement of God, the Most High: God has not made for any man two hearts within him, what does He mean by that? He said: One day the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up to pray and a thought crossed his mind. The hypocrites who were praying with him said: Do you not see that he has two hearts: one with you and one with them? Then God, the Most High, revealed: God has not made for any man two hearts within him. This is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd Al-Rahman Al-Darimi on the authority of Sa’id Al-Harrani, on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd and on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, both on the authority of Zuhair, who is Ibn Mu’awiyah, with this chain of transmission. Then he said: This is a hasan hadith. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Hatim narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Zuhair with this chain of transmission. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Az-Zuhri regarding the verse: God has not made for any man two hearts within him, he said: It has reached us that this was about Zayd ibn Haritha, who was given an example: He says, The son of another man is not your son. Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same, that it was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him, and this is in agreement with what we have presented of the interpretation, and God knows best. And the verse: Call them by the names of their fathers; it is more just in the sight of God, is an abrogates what was permissible at the beginning of Islam, regarding claiming foreign children, who are the adopted sons. So God, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded that their lineage be traced back to their fathers in reality, and that this is justice, equity and righteousness. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: Ma’la bin Asad told us, Abdul Aziz bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Musa bin Uqba, who said: Salim told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, who said: Zayd bin Haritha, may God be pleased with him, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we did not call him anything but Zayd bin Muhammad until the Qur’an was revealed: Call them by the names of their fathers; it is more just in the sight of God. Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Musa bin Uqba. They treated them as sons in every way, in seclusion with mahrams and other things. For this reason, Sahla bint Suhayl, the wife of Abu Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with them both, said: O Messenger of God, we used to call Salim a son, but God has revealed what He has revealed, and he used to come to me, and I felt something of that in Abu Hudhayfah’s soul, so the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Breastfeed him, and you will be forbidden to him. The hadith. For this reason, when this ruling was abrogated, God Almighty permitted the wife of an adopted son, and the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the divorcee of Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him. God Almighty said: So that there will be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. And God Almighty said in the verse of prohibition: And the wives of your sons who are from your loins, as a precaution against the wife of an adopted son, because he is not from the loins. As for the son from breastfeeding, he is in the same position as the son of the loins according to the Sharia, as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said in the two Sahihs: They forbade through breastfeeding what is forbidden through lineage. As for calling someone else a son by way of Honoring and endearing, it is not among the things that are forbidden in this verse, as evidenced by what Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah narrated, except for Al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Arni, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the young boys of Banu Abd Al-Muttalib on our donkeys from Jam’a, and he began to smear our thighs and say, Abini, do not throw the pebbles at the Jamarat until the sun rises. Abu Ubaidah and others said: Abini is the diminutive of Bani, and this is the apparent meaning, for this was during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the year ten. His saying, Call them by the names of their fathers, is about Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him, who was killed on the day of Mu’tah in the year eight. Also in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu ‘Awana al-Waddah ibn ‘Abdullah al-Yashkuri, on the authority of al-Ja’d Abu ‘Uthman al-Basri, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O my son. It was narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi. God the Almighty said: But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients. God the Almighty commanded that the lineage of adopted children be traced back to their fathers if they are known. If they are not known, then they are their brothers in religion and their clients, i.e., to compensate for what they have lost of lineage. For this reason, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said on the day he left Mecca in the year of the Umrah of Compensation, and the daughter of Hamza may God be pleased with her followed them calling, O uncle, O uncle! Ali may God be pleased with him took her and said to Fatimah may God be pleased with her: Here is your cousin. So she carried her, and Ali, Zaid, and Ja’far may God be pleased with them disputed about who should take care of her, and each gave an argument. Ali may God be pleased with him said: I have more right to her, for she is my cousin. Zaid said: The daughter of my brother. Ja’far ibn Abi Talib said: The daughter of my cousin, and her maternal aunt is under me, meaning Asma’ bint Umays. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled in her favor with her maternal aunt and said: The maternal aunt is in the position of the mother. He said to Ali may God be pleased with him: You are from me and I am from you. He said to Ja’far may God be pleased with him: She resembles my creation and my character. He said to Zaid, may God be pleased with him, You are our brother and our master. The hadith contains many rulings, the best of which is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled justly and satisfied both disputing parties. He said to Zaid, may God be pleased with him, You are our brother and our master. God, the Almighty, also said, So your brothers in religion and your masters. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Uyaynah bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Bakrah, may God be pleased with him, said: God, the Almighty, said: “Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients.” So I am one of those whose fathers are not known, so I am one of your brothers in religion. My father said: By God, I think that if he knew that his father was a donkey, he would have claimed to be his father. It is stated in the hadith: Whoever claims a father other than his own, knowing that to be his, is an unbeliever. This is a severe warning and a clear threat to disavow a known lineage. For this reason, God, the Almighty, said: “Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients.” Then God the Almighty said: And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, meaning if you attribute some of them to someone other than their real father by mistake after striving and doing all you can, then God the Almighty has placed hardship on the error and lifted its sin, as He guided to in His saying the Blessed and Exalted, commanding His servants to say, Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. And it is proven in Sahih Muslim that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty said: I have done so.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Aas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a judge strives hard and gets it right, then he has two rewards, and if he strives hard and gets it wrong, then he has one reward. In another hadith, God the Blessed and Exalted has lifted from my nation mistakes, forgetfulness, and whatever they are compelled to do. And He the Blessed and Exalted said here, “There is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only] for what your hearts intended. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.” That is, the sin is upon the one who intentionally committed falsehood, as He the Almighty said, God will not hold you accountable for what your intentional oaths mean. And in the previous hadith, There is no man who knowingly claims a father other than his own, except that he has committed disbelief. And in the abrogated Qur’an, It is disbelief for you to turn away from your fathers. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Utbah ibn Mas`ud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with them, that he said: God Almighty sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the truth, and revealed with him the Book. Among what was revealed to him was the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stoned, and we stoned after him. Then he said: We used to recite, but do not turn away from your fathers, for it is disbelief on your part to turn away from your fathers. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not exaggerate in my praise as Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was exaggerated, for I am only the servant of God, so say His servant and Messenger.” And perhaps Muammar said: As the Christians exaggerated in my praise of the son of Mary. And he narrated it in another hadith: “Three things among people are disbelief: attacking lineage, wailing over the dead, and seeking rain by the stars.”

And he narrated it in another hadith: “Three things among people are disbelief: attacking lineage, wailing over the dead, and seeking rain by the stars.”
33:6: God Almighty knew the compassion and sincere advice His Messenger had for his nation, so He made him more deserving of them than they were of themselves, and his judgment of them took precedence over their own choices, as God Almighty said: “But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.” And in the Sahih: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you will truly believe until I am dearer to him than himself, his wealth, his children, and all of mankind. And in the Sahih also: “Umar may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, by God, you are dearer to me than everything except myself.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: No, O Umar, not until I am dearer to you than yourself. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Messenger of God, by God, you are dearer to me than everything, even myself. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Now, O Umar. And for this reason God Almighty said in this verse: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. Al-Bukhari said regarding this noble verse: Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir narrated to us, Muhammad bin Falih narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no believer but that I am the closest of people to him in this world and the Hereafter. Read if you wish: ‘The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.’ So any believer who leaves behind wealth, let his blood relatives inherit it, whoever they may be. But if he leaves behind a debt or a loss, let him come to me, for I am his protector.” Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it, and he also narrated it in Al-Istiqaad. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Falih with a similar wording. Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding his statement, The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who used to say, “I am closer to every believer than he is to himself. So if a man dies and leaves behind a debt, it is to me, and if someone leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs.” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with a similar wording. God the Almighty said: And their wives are their mothers meaning in sanctity, respect, reverence, honor and veneration. However, it is not permissible to be alone with them, and the prohibition does not extend to their daughters and sisters by consensus, even though some scholars called their daughters the sisters of the believers, as stated by Al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him in Al-Mukhtasar. This is a general statement, not a confirmation of the ruling. Can Mu'awiyah and his ilk be called the maternal uncle of the believers? There are two opinions from scholars may God be pleased with them, and Al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him stated that this should be said. Can they be called the mothers of the believers, so that women are included in the sound masculine plural in the absent form? There are two opinions. It was authentically reported from Aisha may God be pleased with her that she said: This should not be said, and this is the more correct of the two opinions in the school of Al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him. It was narrated from Abu Ka'b and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them that they recited: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Hasan. This is one of the two opinions of the Shafi’i school of thought may God be pleased with him. It was narrated by Al-Baghawi and others. They supported this with the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud may God have mercy on him: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad An-Nafeeli narrated to us, Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn ‘Ajlan, on the authority of Al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I am to you in the position of a father, the most knowledgeable of you. So when one of you goes to the toilet, he should neither face nor turn his back towards the qiblah, nor clean himself with his right hand.” He used to command that three stones be used and forbade the use of dung and bones. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah also narrated it on the authority of Ibn ‘Ajlan. The second opinion is that this should not be said. They used as evidence the statement of God the Almighty: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men. And the Almighty said: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God meaning in the ruling of God than the believers and the emigrants meaning the relatives are nearer to inheritance than the emigrants and the helpers. This abrogates what came before it of inheritance by oath and brotherhood that existed between them, as Ibn Abbas and others said: The emigrant used to inherit from the helper without his relatives and kin because of the brotherhood that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established between them. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair and others from the early and later generations said. Ibn Abi Hatim included a hadith on the authority of Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awam, saying: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr Al-Musabi, one of the residents of Baghdad, told us on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Al-Zinad, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awam, may God be pleased with him, who said: God Almighty revealed about us in particular, the Quraysh and the Ansar: And those of kinship are nearer to one another. That was when we, the Quraysh, came and had no money, and we found the Ansar to be the best of brothers, so we made them brothers and inherited from them. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, made Kharijah ibn Zayd a brother, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, made so-and-so a brother, and Uthman, may God be pleased with him, made a man from Banu Zuraiq ibn Sa’d Al-Zuraqi a brother, and some people say someone else. Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, said: I hid Ka’b ibn Malik and went to him and picked him up, and I found that the weapon was heavy, as he saw. By God, my son, if he had died on that day from this world, no one would have inherited it except me, until God Almighty revealed this verse about us, the Quraysh and the Ansar in particular. So we returned to our heritage. God the Almighty said: Except that you do to your relatives a kindness meaning the inheritance is gone and what remains is support, righteousness, kinship, kindness and bequest. God the Almighty said: That was written in the Book meaning this ruling, that relatives are closer to one another, is a decree from God that is predestined and written in the first Book that cannot be changed or altered. This was stated by Mujahid and others, even though God the Almighty had legislated something other than it at one time because of His profound wisdom in that, and He knows that He will abrogate it to something that is in accordance with His eternal destiny and legally determined decree. And God knows best.
33:7: God Almighty says, informing about the five resolute ones and the rest of the prophets, that He took from them a covenant and a pact to establish the religion of God Almighty, and to convey His message and to cooperate, support each other and agree, as He Almighty said: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said, ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My commitment?’ They said, ‘We have acknowledged.’ He said, ‘Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.’” So this covenant and pact was taken from them after they were sent, and likewise this one, and He mentioned from among them these five, who are the resolute ones, and this is from the category of connecting the specific to the general, and He also explicitly mentioned them in this verse, and in His Almighty saying: “He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided.” So He mentioned the two ends, the middle opening, and the closing, and those in between, in order. So this is the commandment for which He took a covenant from them, as He said God Almighty said: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary. So He began in this verse with the Seal, due to his honor, may God’s prayers be upon him, then He arranged them according to their existence, may God’s prayers be upon them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah al-Dimashqi told us, Muhammad ibn Bakkar told us, Sa’id ibn Bashir told us, Qatada told me, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding the words of God the Almighty: And [mention] when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you and from Noah [the verse]. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in mission, so I was begun before them. Sa’id ibn Bashir has a weakness. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba narrated it on the authority of Qatada as a mursal hadith, but this is more likely. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Qatada as a mawquf hadith: And God knows best. Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Amr bin Ali told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hamza Al-Zayyat told us, Adi bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The best of the children of Adam are five: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, and the best of them is Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. It is stopped and Hamza is weak. It has been said that what is meant by this covenant is the one that was taken from them when they were brought out in the form of atoms from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, as Abu Ja`far al-Razi said on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b who said: And their father Adam was raised up and looked at them, meaning his offspring, and that among them were the rich and the poor, and those of good appearance and those of lesser appearance, so he said: O Lord, if only You had made Your servants equal. So He said: I would have loved to be grateful. And he saw among them the prophets like lamps upon them was light, and they were singled out with another covenant of the message and prophethood, which is what God Almighty says: And when We took from the prophets their covenant and from you and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus, the son of Mary. This is also the saying of Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: The covenant is the firm pledge. God the Almighty says: That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. Mujahid said: Those who convey the messages of the messengers. God the Almighty says: And He has prepared for the disbelievers, meaning among their nations, a painful punishment, meaning one that is hurtful. So we bear witness that the messengers conveyed the messages of their Lord, advised the nations, and revealed to them the clear truth that is not ambiguous, doubtful, or uncertain, even if some of the ignorant, obstinate, apostate, or unjust deny them. What the messengers brought is the truth, and whoever opposes them is astray.

33:9: God Almighty says, informing us of His grace, favor, and kindness to His believing servants in turning away their enemies and defeating them in the year when they conspired against them and formed parties, which was the Year of the Trench, and that was in Shawwal of the year five after the Hijra, according to the correct and well-known opinion. Musa bin Uqbah and others said: It was in the year four, and the reason for the coming of the confederates was that a group of the Jewish nobles of Banu Nadir, whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had expelled from Medina to Khaybar, including Salam bin Abi Al-Haqiq, Salam bin Mishkam, and Kinanah bin Al-Rabi’, went out to Mecca and met with the nobles of Quraysh and incited them to fight the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), promising them victory and support, so they agreed to that. Then they went out to Ghatafan and invited them, and they agreed to them as well. Quraysh went out with their Abyssinians and those who followed them and their leader Abu Sufyan Sakhr bin Harb, and over Ghatafan was Uyaynah bin Hisn bin Badr, and all of them were close to ten thousand. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard of their march, he ordered the Muslims to dig a trench around Medina to the east, at the suggestion of Salman Al-Farsi may God be pleased with him. The Muslims worked on it and made an effort, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) carried dirt with them and dug, and in digging it there were clear signs and evident evidence. The polytheists came and camped east of Medina, near Uhud, and a group of them camped in the upper parts of Medina, as God Almighty said: When they came upon you from above you and from below you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him of the Muslims, who were about three thousand, and some say seven hundred, went out. They leaned their backs on Sal’ and their faces towards the enemy. The trench was a hole with no water between them and them, preventing the cavalry and men from reaching them. The women and children were placed in the roofs of Medina. Banu Qurayzah, who were a group of Jews, had a fortress east of Medina. They had a covenant and protection from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were about eight hundred fighters. Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri went to them and continued with them until they broke the covenant and sided with the parties against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The matter became serious, the situation became intense, and the situation became difficult, as God Almighty said: There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe earthquake. They remained besieging the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions near A month, but they did not reach them and no fighting took place between them, except that Amr bin Abd Wudd Al-Amri, who was one of the famous brave Persians in the pre-Islamic era, rode with horsemen, so they stormed the trench and reached the side of the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Muslims’ cavalry to him, and it is said that no one came forward, so he ordered Ali, may God be pleased with him, to go out to him and they fought for an hour, then Ali, may God be pleased with him, killed him, and it was a sign of victory. Then God, the Almighty, sent upon the Confederates a very strong, violent wind, until they had no tent or anything left, nor was a fire lit for them, nor was there any resting place for them, until they departed disappointed and defeated, as God, the Almighty, said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came to you armies, and We sent upon them a wind and armies. Mujahid said: It is the north wind, and this is supported by the other hadith: I was aided by the north wind, and Aad was destroyed by the south wind. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The south side said to the north side on the night of the Confederates: Go, let us aid the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The north side said: A free woman does not travel at night. He said: So the wind that was sent upon them was the north wind. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Ashja, on the authority of Hafs bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ubaidullah bin Umar told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: My maternal uncle Uthman bin Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, sent me on the night of the Battle of the Trench in intense cold and wind to Madinah, and he said: Bring us food and a blanket. He said: So I asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave me permission and said: Whoever you have brought from my companions, tell them to return. He said: So I went and the wind was blowing everything away, and I did not meet anyone except that I ordered him to return to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Not one of them turned his head. He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind was hitting it on me, and it had an edge on it. He said: The wind hit it until some of the iron fell on my hand and pushed it to the ground. And His statement, And hosts you did not see, are the angels who shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts. So the chief of each tribe would say, O sons of so-and-so, come to me. So they would gather around him, and he would say, Save! Save us for what God, the Almighty, has cast into their hearts of terror. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman may God be pleased with him: “O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and accompany him?” He said, Yes, my nephew. He said, And how did you act? He said, By God, we were struggling. The young man said, By God, if we had caught up with him, we would not have left him walking on the earth, and we would have carried him on our necks. He said: Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: O son of my brother, by God, if you had seen us with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at the Trench, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said, Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people have done? - the condition being that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return - God would admit him into Paradise. He said: So not a man stood up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said the same thing. Not a man from us stood up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said, Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people have done and then return? - the condition being that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return - I ask God Almighty to make him my companion in Paradise. So none of the people stood up because of the intensity of the fear, the intensity of the hunger, and the intensity of the cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called me, and I had no choice but to stand up when he called me. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people and see what they are doing, and do not say anything until you come to us. He said: So I went and entered among the people, and the wind and the soldiers of God, the Almighty, were doing to them what they were doing, leaving them no rest, no fire, and no building. Abu Sufyan stood up and said: O people of Quraysh, let each man look at his companion. Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: So I took the hand of the man beside me and said: Who are you? He said: So-and-so, son of so-and-so. Then Abu Sufyan said: O people of Quraysh, by God, you have not become in a place of residence. The mounts and hoofs have perished, and Banu Qurayzah have betrayed us, and we have heard from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind what you see. By God, our pots will not be reassured, our fires will not stand, and our buildings will not hold together. So depart, for I am departing. Then he stood up to his camel, which was tied up, and sat on it, then he struck it, and it leapt with it on three occasions. He did not release its halter until it was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to me that you should not do anything until you come to me, if you wished, I would have killed it with an arrow. Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: “I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing praying in a cloak belonging to one of his wives. When he saw me, he brought me between his legs and threw the edge of the cloak over me. Then he knelt and prostrated, and I was wrapped in it. When he had finished, I told him the report. Ghatafan heard what the Quraysh had done, so they turned and returned to their country.” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi on the authority of his father who said: We were with Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, and some men said to him: If you had lived in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, you would have fought with him and done well. Hudhayfah said to him: Would you have done that? I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Night of the Confederates, on a night of strong wind and cold. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there not a man who will bring report of the people and be with me on the Day of Resurrection? None of us answered him. Then the second, then the third time, likewise. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Hudhayfah, get up and bring us report of the people. I had no choice but to get up when he called me by name and said: Bring me report of the people and do not frighten them against me. So I went on as if I were walking in a bathhouse until I came to them. Then I saw Abu Sufyan praying his back by the fire, so I put an arrow in the bow of my bow and wanted to shoot it, then I remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not frighten them against me, and if I had shot it, I would have hit it. So I went back as if I were walking in a bathhouse, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the cold struck me when I had finished and settled down, so I informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he dressed me from the excess cloak he had on in which he prayed, so I continued sleeping until morning. When morning came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Peace be upon him: Get up, O Noman. It was narrated by Yunus bin Bakir on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: A man said to Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him: We complain to God about your companionship with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. You lived to see him, but we did not, and you saw him, but we did not. Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: And we complain to God about your belief in him, but you did not see him. By God, you do not know, my nephew, how you would have been if you had lived to see him. I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the Trench, on a cold, rainy night. Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above at length. Bilal bin Yahya al-Absi narrated something similar to this from Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi included in al-Dala’il from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar, from Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Du’ali, from Abdul Aziz bin Hudhayfah’s brother, who said: Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, mentioned their scenes with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions said: By God, if we had witnessed that, we would have done this and that. Hudhayfah said: Do not wish for that. I saw us on the Night of the Confederates, and we were in rows, sitting, and Abu Sufyan and those with him from the confederates were above us, and the Qurayzah of the Jews were below us, and we feared them for our children. There had never come upon us a darkness more intense or a wind more intense, and the sounds of its wind were like thunderbolts, and it was such a darkness that one of us could not see his finger. So the hypocrites began to ask permission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Our houses are exposed, but they are not exposed. No one of them asked permission except that he gave him permission, and he gave them permission so they would sneak away. We were three hundred or so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met us, man by man, until Ali came and… I have no refuge from the enemy or from the cold except a cloak for my wife that does not go beyond my knees. He said: “Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me while I was kneeling on my knees and said: Who is this? I said: Hudhayfah. He said: Hudhayfah? The ground shook and I said: Yes, O Messenger of God, for I did not want to get up. So I got up and he said: There is report about the people, so bring me report of the people. He said: And I am one of the most frightened and most oppressed people.” He said: So I went out and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, protect him from in front of him and from behind him and from his right and from his left and from above him and from below him. He said: By God, God did not create fear or coldness in my stomach except that it came out from my stomach, and I did not find anything in it. He said: When I turned away, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Hudhayfah, do not say anything to the people until you come to me. He said: So I went out and when I approached the people’s camp, I looked into the light of their lit fire and there was a huge, dark-skinned man pointing with his hand at the fire and wiping his waist, and saying: Departure, departure. I did not know Abu Sufyan before that, so I took out an arrow from my quiver with white feathers and put it in the bow of my bow to shoot him with it in the light of the fire. Then I remembered the words of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Do not say anything to them until you come to me. He said: So I held back and put my arrow back in my quiver, then I encouraged myself until I entered the camp. Then the people closest to me were Banu Amir, saying: O family of Amir, departure, departure, you have no place to stay. And when the wind was in their camp, it did not exceed their camp by a handspan. By God, I could hear the sound of stones in their saddlebags and their horses, the wind hitting them with them. Then I went out towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when I was halfway down the road or thereabouts, I saw about twenty horsemen or so wearing turban. They said: Tell your companion that God Almighty has sufficed him against the people. So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was wrapped in his cloak praying. By God, as soon as I returned, the wind came back to me, and I started to shake. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gestured to me with his hand while he was praying, so I approached him and he lowered his cloak over me. Whenever something worried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would pray. So I told him the report of the people, and I told him that I had left them to set out. And God Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came against you armies, then We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing.” Abu Dawud included in his Sunan from it: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Peace be upon him, if something worried him, he would pray, from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar. God the Almighty said: {And when they came upon you from above you} meaning the confederates, {and from below you}, it was mentioned earlier on the authority of Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him that they were Banu Qurayzah, {And when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats} meaning intense fear and panic, {And you thought about God various assumptions}, Ibn Jarir said: Some of those who were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) thought that the fate would be upon the believers, and that God would do that. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding God the Almighty’s saying: {And when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats and you thought about God various assumptions}, the believers thought every assumption and hypocrisy shone forth, to the point that Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, said: Muhammad promised us that we would eat the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, yet one of us cannot even go to the toilet. Al-Hasan said about the words of God Almighty, And you think about God various thoughts, that is, various thoughts. The hypocrites thought that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions would be exterminated, but the believers were certain that what God and His Messenger had promised was true, and that He would make Him prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists hated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Asim al-Ansari told us, Abu Amir told us, H and my father told us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi told us, al-Zubayr told us, meaning Ibn Abdullah, the client of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Rutij ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Said, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We said on the day of the Trench: O Messenger of God, is there anything we can say, for hearts have reached our throats? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, say: O God, cover our faults and make us feel safe.” He said: So he struck the faces of his enemies with the wind, and defeated them with the wind. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Amir al-Aqdi.
33:10: God Almighty says, informing us of His grace, favor, and kindness to His believing servants in turning away their enemies and defeating them in the year when they conspired against them and formed parties, which was the Year of the Trench, and that was in Shawwal of the year five after the Hijra, according to the correct and well-known opinion. Musa bin Uqbah and others said: It was in the year four, and the reason for the coming of the confederates was that a group of the Jewish nobles of Banu Nadir, whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had expelled from Medina to Khaybar, including Salam bin Abi Al-Haqiq, Salam bin Mishkam, and Kinanah bin Al-Rabi’, went out to Mecca and met with the nobles of Quraysh and incited them to fight the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), promising them victory and support, so they agreed to that. Then they went out to Ghatafan and invited them, and they agreed to them as well. Quraysh went out with their Abyssinians and those who followed them and their leader Abu Sufyan Sakhr bin Harb, and over Ghatafan was Uyaynah bin Hisn bin Badr, and all of them were close to ten thousand. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard of their march, he ordered the Muslims to dig a trench around Medina to the east, at the suggestion of Salman Al-Farsi may God be pleased with him. The Muslims worked on it and made an effort, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) carried dirt with them and dug, and in digging it there were clear signs and evident evidence. The polytheists came and camped east of Medina, near Uhud, and a group of them camped in the upper parts of Medina, as God Almighty said: When they came upon you from above you and from below you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those with him of the Muslims, who were about three thousand, and some say seven hundred, went out. They leaned their backs on Sal’ and their faces towards the enemy. The trench was a hole with no water between them and them, preventing the cavalry and men from reaching them. The women and children were placed in the roofs of Medina. Banu Qurayzah, who were a group of Jews, had a fortress east of Medina. They had a covenant and protection from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were about eight hundred fighters. Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri went to them and continued with them until they broke the covenant and sided with the parties against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The matter became serious, the situation became intense, and the situation became difficult, as God Almighty said: There the believers were tried and shaken with a severe earthquake. They remained besieging the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions near A month, but they did not reach them and no fighting took place between them, except that Amr bin Abd Wudd Al-Amri, who was one of the famous brave Persians in the pre-Islamic era, rode with horsemen, so they stormed the trench and reached the side of the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Muslims’ cavalry to him, and it is said that no one came forward, so he ordered Ali, may God be pleased with him, to go out to him and they fought for an hour, then Ali, may God be pleased with him, killed him, and it was a sign of victory. Then God, the Almighty, sent upon the Confederates a very strong, violent wind, until they had no tent or anything left, nor was a fire lit for them, nor was there any resting place for them, until they departed disappointed and defeated, as God, the Almighty, said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came to you armies, and We sent upon them a wind and armies. Mujahid said: It is the north wind, and this is supported by the other hadith: I was aided by the north wind, and Aad was destroyed by the south wind. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The south side said to the north side on the night of the Confederates: Go, let us aid the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The north side said: A free woman does not travel at night. He said: So the wind that was sent upon them was the north wind. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Ashja, on the authority of Hafs bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ubaidullah bin Umar told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: My maternal uncle Uthman bin Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, sent me on the night of the Battle of the Trench in intense cold and wind to Madinah, and he said: Bring us food and a blanket. He said: So I asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave me permission and said: Whoever you have brought from my companions, tell them to return. He said: So I went and the wind was blowing everything away, and I did not meet anyone except that I ordered him to return to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Not one of them turned his head. He said: I had a shield with me, and the wind was hitting it on me, and it had an edge on it. He said: The wind hit it until some of the iron fell on my hand and pushed it to the ground. And His statement, And hosts you did not see, are the angels who shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts. So the chief of each tribe would say, O sons of so-and-so, come to me. So they would gather around him, and he would say, Save! Save us for what God, the Almighty, has cast into their hearts of terror. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman may God be pleased with him: “O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and accompany him?” He said, Yes, my nephew. He said, And how did you act? He said, By God, we were struggling. The young man said, By God, if we had caught up with him, we would not have left him walking on the earth, and we would have carried him on our necks. He said: Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: O son of my brother, by God, if you had seen us with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at the Trench, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said, Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people have done? - the condition being that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return - God would admit him into Paradise. He said: So not a man stood up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said the same thing. Not a man from us stood up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned around and said, Who is the man who will stand and see for us what the people have done and then return? - the condition being that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return - I ask God Almighty to make him my companion in Paradise. So none of the people stood up because of the intensity of the fear, the intensity of the hunger, and the intensity of the cold. When no one stood up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called me, and I had no choice but to stand up when he called me. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, O Hudhayfah, go and enter among the people and see what they are doing, and do not say anything until you come to us. He said: So I went and entered among the people, and the wind and the soldiers of God, the Almighty, were doing to them what they were doing, leaving them no rest, no fire, and no building. Abu Sufyan stood up and said: O people of Quraysh, let each man look at his companion. Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him said: So I took the hand of the man beside me and said: Who are you? He said: So-and-so, son of so-and-so. Then Abu Sufyan said: O people of Quraysh, by God, you have not become in a place of residence. The mounts and hoofs have perished, and Banu Qurayzah have betrayed us, and we have heard from them what we dislike, and we have suffered from this wind what you see. By God, our pots will not be reassured, our fires will not stand, and our buildings will not hold together. So depart, for I am departing. Then he stood up to his camel, which was tied up, and sat on it, then he struck it, and it leapt with it on three occasions. He did not release its halter until it was standing. Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to me that you should not do anything until you come to me, if you wished, I would have killed it with an arrow. Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: “I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing praying in a cloak belonging to one of his wives. When he saw me, he brought me between his legs and threw the edge of the cloak over me. Then he knelt and prostrated, and I was wrapped in it. When he had finished, I told him the report. Ghatafan heard what the Quraysh had done, so they turned and returned to their country.” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi on the authority of his father who said: We were with Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, and some men said to him: If you had lived in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, you would have fought with him and done well. Hudhayfah said to him: Would you have done that? I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Night of the Confederates, on a night of strong wind and cold. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there not a man who will bring report of the people and be with me on the Day of Resurrection? None of us answered him. Then the second, then the third time, likewise. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Hudhayfah, get up and bring us report of the people. I had no choice but to get up when he called me by name and said: Bring me report of the people and do not frighten them against me. So I went on as if I were walking in a bathhouse until I came to them. Then I saw Abu Sufyan praying his back by the fire, so I put an arrow in the bow of my bow and wanted to shoot it, then I remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not frighten them against me, and if I had shot it, I would have hit it. So I went back as if I were walking in a bathhouse, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the cold struck me when I had finished and settled down, so I informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he dressed me from the excess cloak he had on in which he prayed, so I continued sleeping until morning. When morning came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Peace be upon him: Get up, O Noman. It was narrated by Yunus bin Bakir on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, who said: A man said to Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him: We complain to God about your companionship with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. You lived to see him, but we did not, and you saw him, but we did not. Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: And we complain to God about your belief in him, but you did not see him. By God, you do not know, my nephew, how you would have been if you had lived to see him. I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the Trench, on a cold, rainy night. Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above at length. Bilal bin Yahya al-Absi narrated something similar to this from Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi included in al-Dala’il from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar, from Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Du’ali, from Abdul Aziz bin Hudhayfah’s brother, who said: Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, mentioned their scenes with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions said: By God, if we had witnessed that, we would have done this and that. Hudhayfah said: Do not wish for that. I saw us on the Night of the Confederates, and we were in rows, sitting, and Abu Sufyan and those with him from the confederates were above us, and the Qurayzah of the Jews were below us, and we feared them for our children. There had never come upon us a darkness more intense or a wind more intense, and the sounds of its wind were like thunderbolts, and it was such a darkness that one of us could not see his finger. So the hypocrites began to ask permission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Our houses are exposed, but they are not exposed. No one of them asked permission except that he gave him permission, and he gave them permission so they would sneak away. We were three hundred or so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met us, man by man, until Ali came and… I have no refuge from the enemy or from the cold except a cloak for my wife that does not go beyond my knees. He said: “Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me while I was kneeling on my knees and said: Who is this? I said: Hudhayfah. He said: Hudhayfah? The ground shook and I said: Yes, O Messenger of God, for I did not want to get up. So I got up and he said: There is report about the people, so bring me report of the people. He said: And I am one of the most frightened and most oppressed people.” He said: So I went out and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, protect him from in front of him and from behind him and from his right and from his left and from above him and from below him. He said: By God, God did not create fear or coldness in my stomach except that it came out from my stomach, and I did not find anything in it. He said: When I turned away, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Hudhayfah, do not say anything to the people until you come to me. He said: So I went out and when I approached the people’s camp, I looked into the light of their lit fire and there was a huge, dark-skinned man pointing with his hand at the fire and wiping his waist, and saying: Departure, departure. I did not know Abu Sufyan before that, so I took out an arrow from my quiver with white feathers and put it in the bow of my bow to shoot him with it in the light of the fire. Then I remembered the words of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Do not say anything to them until you come to me. He said: So I held back and put my arrow back in my quiver, then I encouraged myself until I entered the camp. Then the people closest to me were Banu Amir, saying: O family of Amir, departure, departure, you have no place to stay. And when the wind was in their camp, it did not exceed their camp by a handspan. By God, I could hear the sound of stones in their saddlebags and their horses, the wind hitting them with them. Then I went out towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when I was halfway down the road or thereabouts, I saw about twenty horsemen or so wearing turban. They said: Tell your companion that God Almighty has sufficed him against the people. So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was wrapped in his cloak praying. By God, as soon as I returned, the wind came back to me, and I started to shake. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gestured to me with his hand while he was praying, so I approached him and he lowered his cloak over me. Whenever something worried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would pray. So I told him the report of the people, and I told him that I had left them to set out. And God Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came against you armies, then We sent against them a wind and armies you did not see. And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing.” Abu Dawud included in his Sunan from it: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Peace be upon him, if something worried him, he would pray, from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar. God the Almighty said: {And when they came upon you from above you} meaning the confederates, {and from below you}, it was mentioned earlier on the authority of Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him that they were Banu Qurayzah, {And when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats} meaning intense fear and panic, {And you thought about God various assumptions}, Ibn Jarir said: Some of those who were with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) thought that the fate would be upon the believers, and that God would do that. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding God the Almighty’s saying: {And when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats and you thought about God various assumptions}, the believers thought every assumption and hypocrisy shone forth, to the point that Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, said: Muhammad promised us that we would eat the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, yet one of us cannot even go to the toilet. Al-Hasan said about the words of God Almighty, And you think about God various thoughts, that is, various thoughts. The hypocrites thought that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions would be exterminated, but the believers were certain that what God and His Messenger had promised was true, and that He would make Him prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists hated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Asim al-Ansari told us, Abu Amir told us, H and my father told us, Abu Amir al-Aqdi told us, al-Zubayr told us, meaning Ibn Abdullah, the client of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Rutij ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Said, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We said on the day of the Trench: O Messenger of God, is there anything we can say, for hearts have reached our throats? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, say: O God, cover our faults and make us feel safe.” He said: So he struck the faces of his enemies with the wind, and defeated them with the wind. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Amir al-Aqdi.
33:11: God the Most High says, informing us of that situation when the confederates encamped around Medina, and the Muslims were besieged in extreme hardship and distress, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was among them, that they were afflicted, tested, and shaken severely. Then hypocrisy appeared, and those in whose hearts was disease spoke of what was in their souls: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease said, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’ As for the hypocrite, his hypocrisy became apparent, and the one in whose heart was doubt or doubt due to his weak state, so he vented what he found of whispers in himself due to the weakness of his faith and the severity of his condition. Other people said as God the Most High said: And when a party of them said, ‘O people of Yathrib,’ meaning Medina. As it came in the Sahih, “I was shown in a dream the place of your migration, a land between two lava fields. My family thought it was Yathrib, but it was Medina.” In another version: Medina. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ibrahim bin Mahdi told us, Saleh bin Omar told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever calls Madinah Yathrib, let him seek forgiveness from God, for it is Tayyiba, it is Tayyiba. Imam Ahmad is the only one who narrated it, and there is a weakness in its chain of transmission, and God knows best. It is said that the origin of its name Yathrib was due to a man who settled there from the Amalekites, whose name was Yathrib bin Ubayd bin Mahlayl bin Aws bin Amlaq bin Lawdh bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, as Al-Suhayli said. He said: It was narrated from some of them that he said: It has eleven names in the Torah: Al-Madinah, Tayyiba, Tayyiba, Al-Muskeenah, Al-Jabirah, Al-Muhabba, Al-Mahbouba, Al-Qasimah, Al-Majburah, Al-Adhra’, and Al-Marhuma. Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: We find in the Torah that God the Almighty says to Madinah: O Tayyiba, O Tayyiba, O Poor One, do not carry treasures. I will raise your stones above the stones of the villages. And his saying, You have no place to stay, meaning here they mean with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the place of guarding. So return, meaning to your homes and dwellings. And a group of them should ask the Prophet’s permission. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They are Banu Haritha. They said: We fear thieves from our homes. And more than one said the same. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the one who said that was Aws ibn Qayzi, meaning they excused themselves from returning to their homes by saying that they were exposed, meaning there was nothing to screen them from the enemy, so they feared them. God Almighty said: And it is not exposed, meaning it is not as they claim. They only want to flee, meaning to escape from the advance.

33:13: God the Most High says, informing us of that situation when the confederates encamped around Medina, and the Muslims were besieged in extreme hardship and distress, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was among them, that they were afflicted, tested, and shaken severely. Then hypocrisy appeared, and those in whose hearts was disease spoke of what was in their souls: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts was disease said, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’ As for the hypocrite, his hypocrisy became apparent, and the one in whose heart was doubt or doubt due to his weak state, so he vented what he found of whispers in himself due to the weakness of his faith and the severity of his condition. Other people said as God the Most High said: And when a party of them said, ‘O people of Yathrib,’ meaning Medina. As it came in the Sahih, “I was shown in a dream the place of your migration, a land between two lava fields. My family thought it was Yathrib, but it was Medina.” In another version: Medina. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ibrahim bin Mahdi told us, Saleh bin Omar told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdur Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Bara’ may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever calls Madinah Yathrib, let him seek forgiveness from God, for it is Tayyiba, it is Tayyiba. Imam Ahmad is the only one who narrated it, and there is a weakness in its chain of transmission, and God knows best. It is said that the origin of its name Yathrib was due to a man who settled there from the Amalekites, whose name was Yathrib bin Ubayd bin Mahlayl bin Aws bin Amlaq bin Lawdh bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, as Al-Suhayli said. He said: It was narrated from some of them that he said: It has eleven names in the Torah: Al-Madinah, Tayyiba, Tayyiba, Al-Muskeenah, Al-Jabirah, Al-Muhabba, Al-Mahbouba, Al-Qasimah, Al-Majburah, Al-Adhra’, and Al-Marhuma. Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: We find in the Torah that God the Almighty says to Madinah: O Tayyiba, O Tayyiba, O Poor One, do not carry treasures. I will raise your stones above the stones of the villages. And his saying, You have no place to stay, meaning here they mean with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the place of guarding. So return, meaning to your homes and dwellings. And a group of them should ask the Prophet’s permission. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They are Banu Haritha. They said: We fear thieves from our homes. And more than one person said the same. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the one who said that was Aws ibn Qayzi, meaning they excused themselves from returning to their homes by saying that they were exposed, meaning there was nothing to screen them from the enemy, so they feared them. God Almighty said: And it is not exposed, meaning it is not as they claim. They only want to flee, meaning to escape from the advance.
33:14: The Almighty tells us about those who “say, ‘Our houses are exposed,’ but they are not exposed. They only want to flee.” That if the enemies entered upon them from every side of the city and any of its regions, and then they were asked about the trial, which is entering into disbelief, they would quickly disbelieve. They do not maintain faith nor hold fast to it with the slightest fear or panic. This is how Qatada, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and Ibn Jarir explained it. This is a severe condemnation of them. Then the Almighty said, reminding them of what they had pledged to God before this fear, that they would not turn their backs or flee from the battle. And the pledge of God will be questioned, meaning that God Almighty will inevitably question them about that pledge. Then He informed them that their fleeing would not delay their appointed times or lengthen their lives, but rather it might have been a reason for their being taken by surprise. For this reason, the Almighty said: And then you would not enjoy [yourselves] except for a little, meaning after your flight and escape. Say, ‘The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears God.’ Then the Almighty said: Say, ‘Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends to harm you or intends to have mercy upon you?’ And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper. That is, they and others have no protector or helper besides God.

33:18: God the Almighty informs us of His comprehensive knowledge of those who prevent others from witnessing war and who say to their brothers, companions, friends, and acquaintances, Come to us, to where we are staying in the shade and fruits. Yet, they "come only a little to battle. Stingy with you," meaning miserly with affection and compassion. Al-Suddi said, Stingy with you, meaning with spoils. But when fear comes, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who has fainted from death, meaning from the intensity of his fear and alarm. This is how these cowards fear fighting. But when the fear has departed, they lash out at you with sharp tongues, meaning when there is security, they speak eloquent, lofty words, and claim for themselves high positions in bravery and courage, while they lie about that. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said, They lash out at you, meaning they greet you. Qatada said: As for the spoils, they are the most miserly people and the worst at sharing: Give us, give us, we have witnessed with you. As for the battle, they are the most cowardly people and abandon the truth, and yet they are miserly with good, meaning there is no good in them, they have combined cowardice, lying and lack of good, so they are as the poet said about their proverbs: Are they harsh and rude in peace, and in war like the shameless women? That is, in the case of peace, they are like donkeys, and the word ayyar is the plural of ayr, which is a donkey. And in war, they are like menstruating women. That is why God Almighty said: Those did not believe, so God rendered worthless their deeds, and that, for God, is easy. That is, it is easy and simple for Him.

33:20: This is also one of their ugly traits of cowardice, weakness and fear. They think that the confederates have not gone away, but rather they are close to them and will return to them. But if the confederates come, they wish that they were nomads among the desert dwellers, asking about your report. That is, if the confederates come, they wish that they were not present with you in the city, but rather in the desert, asking about your report and what happened with your enemy. And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little. That is, if they had been among you, they would not have fought with you except a little, due to their great cowardice, humiliation and weak faith. And God, the Most High, the Most Great, knows them.
33:21: This noble verse is a great foundation for following the example of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his words, actions, and conditions. For this reason, God, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded people to follow the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of the Confederates in his patience, perseverance, steadfastness, struggle, and awaiting relief from his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. For this reason, God, the Almighty, said to those who were anxious, impatient, shaken, and disturbed in their affairs on the Day of the Confederates, Indeed, in the Messenger of God you have an excellent pattern to follow. That is, why did you not follow his example and follow his characteristics, may God bless him and grant him peace? For this reason, God, the Almighty, said, For whoever hopes in God and the Last Day and remembers God much. Then God the Almighty said, informing about His believing servants who believed in God’s promise to them and made it their outcome in this world and the hereafter, God the Almighty said: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, ‘This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth.’ Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and Qatadah said: They meant God the Almighty’s statement in Surat Al-Baqarah 2: “Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trials and tribulations] have not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken until [even] the Messenger and those who believed with him said, ‘When is the help of God?’ Unquestionably, the help of God is near.” That is, this is what God and His Messenger promised us of trials, tests, and examinations that will be followed by imminent victory. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And God and His Messenger spoke the truth. The Almighty’s statement: And it only increased them in faith and submission is evidence of the increase and strength of faith in relation to people and their conditions, as the majority of the imams said: it increases and decreases, and we have established that at the beginning of the explanation of Al-Bukhari, praise and thanks be to God. The meaning of His statement, may His Majesty be glorified, And it only increased them is that condition, distress and hardship except in faith in God and submission meaning obedience to His commands and obedience to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
