33:23: When God the Almighty mentioned about the hypocrites that they broke the covenant they had pledged to God not to turn their backs, He described the believers as having adhered to the covenant and the pact. “They were true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his pledge.” Some of them said: his appointed time. Al-Bukhari said: his covenant, and it refers back to the first one. And among them is he who awaits [his end] and has not altered [his end] by any alteration. That is, they did not change the covenant of God, nor did they break it, nor did they alter it. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu`ayb told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit told me, on the authority of his father, who said: When we made copies of the Qur’an, a verse from Surat Al-Ahzab was missing. I used to hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite it. I did not find it except with Khuzaymah bin Thabit Al-Ansari may God be pleased with him, whose testimony the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made equivalent to the testimony of two men. Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to God. This was narrated only by Al-Bukhari, not by Muslim. Ahmad included it in his Musnad, and by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in their Tafsir from their Sunans, on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. Al-Bukhari also said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari told us, my father told me, on the authority of Thamamah, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: We see that this verse was revealed about Anas ibn an-Nadr may God be pleased with him: Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. This verse is unique to al-Bukhari from this chain of narration, but it has corroborating evidence from other chains of narration. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, who said: Anas said: My uncle Anas ibn an-Nadr may God be pleased with him, I was named after him. He did not witness the Battle of Badr with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so it was difficult for him, and he said: The first battle that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) witnessed, I was absent from it. If God lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) after that, God will see what I will do. He said: He was afraid to say anything else, so he was present with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud. He met Sa`d ibn Mu`adh may God be pleased with him. Anas may God be pleased with him said to him: O Abu `Amr, where is the fragrance of Paradise? I smell it before Uhud. He fought them until he was killed may God be pleased with him. Eighty-two wounds were found on his body, between blows, stab wounds, and arrow wounds. His sister, my aunt Ar-Rabi` bint An-Nadr, said: I did not recognize my brother except by his fingertips. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance] and they have not changed [their covenant] by any change.” He said: They thought that it was revealed about him and his companions may God be pleased with them. Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Al-Mughira with this chain of transmission. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah from Thabit from Anas may God be pleased with him with a similar chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: His uncle, meaning Anas bin An-Nadr, may God be pleased with him, was absent from the Battle of Badr. He said: I was absent from the first battle in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought the polytheists. If God lets me witness a fight against the polytheists, God Almighty will see what I will do. He said: When the Day of Uhud came, the Muslims fled, so he said: O God, I apologize to You for what these people did - meaning his companions - and I disavow before You what these people did - meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced and Sa`d bin Mu`adh, may God be pleased with him, met him before Uhud, and he said: I am with you. Saad may God be pleased with him said: “I could not do what he did. When he was killed, eighty-odd sword wounds, spear wounds, and arrow wounds were found on him. They used to say: ‘Among them and his companions was revealed: “And among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await [their fate].”’ At-Tirmidhi included it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd, and An-Nasa’i also included it on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, both on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun on his authority. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Al-Bukhari included it in Al-Maghāzī on the authority of Hassan ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talhah, on the authority of Masraf, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, on his authority. He did not mention the revelation of the verse. Ibn Jarir included it on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Asqalani told us, Sulayman ibn Ayyub ibn Isa ibn Musa ibn Talhah ibn Ubaydullah told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Musa ibn Talhah, on the authority of his father Talhah may God be pleased with him, who said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned from Uhud, he ascended the pulpit, praised and glorified God, and consoled the Muslims for what had befallen them, and informed them of the reward and provision for them in it. Then he recited this verse: ‘Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his pledge’…” the entire verse. A Muslim man stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, who are these?’ I came wearing two green Hadrami garments. He said: ‘O questioner, this is one of them.’” Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Ayyub al-Talhi. At-Tirmidhi also included it in his Tafsir and Manaqib, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Talhah ibn Yahya, on the authority of Musa and Isa, the sons of Talhah, on the authority of their father may God be pleased with them. He said: It is a strange hadith, we do not know it except from the hadith of Yunus. He also said: Ahmad bin Issam Al-Ansari told us, Abu Amir told us - meaning Al-Aqdi - Ishaq told me - meaning Ibn Talha bin Ubaidullah - on the authority of Musa bin Talha who said: I entered upon Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, and when I left he called me and said: Shall I not tell you, O son of my brother, a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Talha is among those who have fulfilled their vow. Narrated by Ibn Jarir: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Talhi, on the authority of Musa bin Talhah, who said: Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan may God be pleased with him stood up and said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: Talhah is among those who have fulfilled their vow. This is why Mujahid said about the words of God the Almighty: And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, meaning his covenant. And among them is he who awaits, he said: a day when there will be fighting and he will be truthful in the encounter. Al-Hasan said: And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, meaning his death while being truthful and loyal. Some of them are awaiting death in the same manner, and some of them have not changed at all. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. Some of them said: We love him and vow him. And the Almighty said: And they did not change at all meaning they did not change their covenant and exchange loyalty for treachery, rather they continued to adhere to what they had pledged and did not break it, like the actions of the hypocrites who said, “Indeed, our houses are exposed, but they are not exposed. They only desire to flee. And if they were to enter upon them from its regions and then they were asked for temptation, they would come to it and they would not remain in it except a little. And they had already made a covenant with God before that they would not turn their backs.” And the Almighty’s saying: That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. That is, He only tests His servants with fear and earthquakes to distinguish the wicked from the good, so that the matter of one becomes apparent in action and the matter of the other in action, even though He, the Almighty, knows a thing before it comes into being. However, He does not punish creation with His knowledge of them until they act upon what He knows of them, as He, the Almighty, said: And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the steadfast, and We will make evident your report. This is knowledge of a thing after it comes into being, even though previous knowledge of it was obtained before its existence. Likewise, God, the Almighty, said: “It is not for God to leave the believers in that state you are upon until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Nor is it for God to inform you of the unseen.” For this reason, the Almighty said here: That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, that is, for their patience in what they pledged to God, their adherence to it, and their adherence to it. And He may punish the hypocrites, who are the ones who break the covenant of God and disobey His commands, and thus deserve His punishment and torment. But they are under His will in this world, if He wills. He will continue with them in what they did until they meet Him, and He will punish them for it. If He wills, He will forgive them by guiding them to abandon hypocrisy and turn to faith and righteous deeds after their immorality and disobedience. And since His mercy and compassion, blessed and exalted be He, for His creation prevail over His wrath, He said, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.

If God lets me witness a battle with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) after that, God will see what I will do. He said: He was afraid to say anything else, so he was present with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on the day of Uhud. He met Sa`d ibn Mu`adh may God be pleased with him. Anas may God be pleased with him said to him: O Abu `Amr, where is the fragrance of Paradise? I smell it before Uhud. He fought them until he was killed may God be pleased with him. Eighty-two wounds were found on his body, between blows, stab wounds, and arrow wounds. His sister, my aunt Ar-Rabi` bint An-Nadr, said: I did not recognize my brother except by his fingertips. He said: Then this verse was revealed: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow [to the death], and among them is he who awaits [his chance] and they have not changed [their covenant] by any change.” He said: They thought that it was revealed about him and his companions may God be pleased with them. Muslim, At-Tirmidhi, and An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Al-Mughira with this same chain of transmission. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah from Thabit from Anas may God be pleased with him with a similar chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: His uncle, meaning Anas bin An-Nadr, may God be pleased with him, was absent from the Battle of Badr. He said: I was absent from the first battle in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought the polytheists. If God lets me witness a fight against the polytheists, God Almighty will see what I will do. He said: When the Day of Uhud came, the Muslims fled, so he said: O God, I apologize to You for what these people did - meaning his companions - and I disavow before You what these people did - meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced and Sa`d bin Mu`adh, may God be pleased with him, met him before Uhud, and he said: I am with you. Saad may God be pleased with him said: “I could not do what he did. When he was killed, eighty-odd sword wounds, spear wounds, and arrow wounds were found on him. They used to say: ‘Among them and his companions was revealed: “And among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who await [their fate].”’ At-Tirmidhi included it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd ibn Humayd, and An-Nasa’i also included it on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, both on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun on his authority. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan. Al-Bukhari included it in Al-Maghāzī on the authority of Hassan ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talhah, on the authority of Masraf, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, on his authority. He did not mention the revelation of the verse. Ibn Jarir included it on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Asqalani told us, Sulayman ibn Ayyub ibn Isa ibn Musa ibn Talhah ibn Ubaydullah told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Musa ibn Talhah, on the authority of his father Talhah may God be pleased with him, who said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned from Uhud, he ascended the pulpit, praised and glorified God, and consoled the Muslims for what had befallen them, and informed them of the reward and provision for them in it. Then he recited this verse: ‘Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his pledge’…” the entire verse. A Muslim man stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, who are these?’ I came wearing two green Hadrami garments. He said: ‘O questioner, this is one of them.’” Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Ayyub al-Talhi. At-Tirmidhi also included it in his Tafsir and Manaqib, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Talhah ibn Yahya, on the authority of Musa and Isa, the sons of Talhah, on the authority of their father may God be pleased with them. He said: It is a strange hadith, we do not know it except from the hadith of Yunus. He also said: Ahmad bin Issam Al-Ansari told us, Abu Amir told us - meaning Al-Aqdi - Ishaq told me - meaning Ibn Talha bin Ubaidullah - on the authority of Musa bin Talha who said: I entered upon Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, and when I left he called me and said: Shall I not tell you, O son of my brother, a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Talha is among those who have fulfilled their vow. Narrated by Ibn Jarir: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Talhi, on the authority of Musa bin Talhah, who said: Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan may God be pleased with him stood up and said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: Talhah is among those who have fulfilled their vow. This is why Mujahid said about the words of God the Almighty: And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, meaning his covenant. And among them is he who awaits, he said: a day when there will be fighting and he will be truthful in the encounter. Al-Hasan said: And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, meaning his death while being truthful and loyal. Some of them are awaiting death in the same manner, and some of them have not changed at all. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said the same. Some of them said: We love him and vow him. And the Almighty said: And they did not change at all meaning they did not change their covenant and exchange loyalty for treachery, rather they continued to adhere to what they had pledged and did not break it, like the actions of the hypocrites who said, “Indeed, our houses are exposed, but they are not exposed. They only desire to flee. And if they were to enter upon them from its regions and then they were asked for temptation, they would come to it and they would not remain in it except a little. And they had already made a covenant with God before that they would not turn their backs.” And the Almighty’s saying: That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. That is, He only tests His servants with fear and earthquakes to distinguish the wicked from the good, so that the matter of one becomes apparent in action and the matter of the other in action, even though He, the Almighty, knows a thing before it comes into being. However, He does not punish creation with His knowledge of them until they act upon what He knows of them, as He, the Almighty, said: And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the steadfast, and We will make evident your report. This is knowledge of a thing after it comes into being, even though previous knowledge of it was obtained before its existence. Likewise, God, the Almighty, said: “It is not for God to leave the believers in that state you are upon until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Nor is it for God to inform you of the unseen.” For this reason, the Almighty said here: That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, that is, for their patience in what they pledged to God, their adherence to it, and their adherence to it. And He may punish the hypocrites, who are the ones who break the covenant of God and disobey His commands, and thus deserve His punishment and torment. But they are under His will in this world, if He wills. He will continue with them in what they did until they meet Him, and He will punish them for it. If He wills, He will forgive them by guiding them to abandon hypocrisy and turn to faith and righteous deeds after their immorality and disobedience. And since His mercy and compassion, blessed and exalted be He, for His creation prevail over His wrath, He said, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
33:25: God Almighty says, informing about the parties when He expelled them from the city with the wind and divine soldiers He sent upon them. And if God had not made His Messenger a mercy to the worlds, this wind would have been more severe upon them than the barren wind He sent upon Aad. But God Almighty said: And God would not punish them while you are among them. So He unleashed upon them a wind that divided them, just as the reason for their gathering was passion. They were a mixture of different tribes, parties, and opinions. So it was appropriate to send upon them a wind that divided their groups and returned them disappointed and losers due to their anger and resentment. They did not attain any good in this world because of the victory and spoils they had in their souls, nor in the Hereafter because of the sins they bore in their confrontation with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with hostility and their intention to kill him and exterminate his army. And whoever intends something and his intention is true in his action, then he is in reality like the one who did it. God the Almighty said: And God spared the believers in fighting meaning they did not need to fight them or duel them until they expelled them from their land, rather God alone sufficed and granted victory to His servant and honored His soldiers. That is why the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: “There is no god but God alone. He fulfilled His promise, granted victory to His servant, honored His soldiers, and defeated the confederates alone, so there is nothing after Him.” Both of them narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated against the confederates and said: “O God, Sender down of the Book, Swift in account, defeat the confederates. O God, defeat them and shake them.” In His Almighty saying: And God spared the believers in fighting refers to the cessation of war between them and the Quraysh, and this is what happened after that. The polytheists did not invade them, but the Muslims invaded them in their own land. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, “When the people of the Trench left the Trench, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, as we have been informed, ‘The Quraysh will not attack you after this year, but you will attack them.’” So the Quraysh did not attack you after that, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued to attack them after that until God, the Most High, conquered Mecca. This hadith mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq is an authentic hadith, as Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Sufyan, Abu Ishaq told me: I heard Sulayman ibn Sard may God be pleased with him say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said on the Day of the Confederates, ‘Now we will attack them, and they will not attack us.’” This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Ath-Thawri, and Isra’il on the authority of Abu Ishaq with it. The Almighty’s statement, And God is All-Powerful, All-Mighty, means that by His power and might He sent them back disappointed, having achieved no good, and God honored Islam and its people, fulfilled His promise, and aided His Messenger and His servant, so to Him be praise and thanks.
33:26: It was mentioned that when the Banu Qurayzah troops arrived and descended upon Medina, they broke the treaty that had been between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was due to the embassy of Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, may God curse him. He entered their fortress and remained with their master Ka’b ibn Asad until he broke the treaty, and said to him, among other things: Woe to you, I have come to you with the glory of the age. I have come to you with the Quraysh and their Abyssinians, and Ghatafan and their followers, and they will not cease here until they exterminate Muhammad and his companions. Ka’b said to him: Rather, by God, you have come to me with the humiliation of the age. Woe to you, Huyayy, you are ill-omened, so leave us alone. He continued to twist from top to bottom until he agreed. Huyayy stipulated that if the Confederates went and nothing happened, he would enter the fortress with them, so he would be like them. When Qurayzah broke the treaty and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of this, it upset him and made it very difficult for him and for the Muslims. When God supported him God the Almighty granted him victory and subdued the enemies and sent them back disappointed in the most lost deal. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina supported and victorious, and the people laid down their weapons. “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was washing himself from the fatigue of that battle in the house of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, Gabriel, peace be upon him, appeared to him wearing a turban of brocade, riding a mule with a velvet of brocade on it. He said: Have you laid down your weapons, O Messenger of God? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. He said: But the angels did not lay down their weapons, and now I am returning from pursuing the people. Then he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, commands you to rise up against Banu Qurayzah.” In another narration, he said to him: Is it your excuse to fight? Have you laid down your weapons? He said: Yes. He said: But we have not laid down our weapons yet. Rise up against these people. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where?” He said: Banu Qurayzah, for God Almighty has commanded me to shake them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up immediately and ordered the people to march to Banu Qurayzah, which was miles from Madinah, after the noon prayer. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. So the people marched and the prayer caught up with them on the way. Some of them prayed on the way and said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want us to do anything except hasten the march.” Others said: We will not pray it except in Banu Qurayzah. He did not rebuke either group, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed them. He had appointed Ibn Umm Maktum, may God be pleased with him, as his successor in Madinah, and given the banner to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When the situation became too long for him, they submitted to the rule of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, the leader of the Aws, may God be pleased with him, because they had been their allies in the pre-Islamic period, and they believed that he would treat them well in that, as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had done with his clients. Banu Qaynuqa`, when he released them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they thought that Sa`d would do to them what Ibn Abi did to those people, and they did not know that Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, had been struck by an arrow in his ankle during the Battle of the Trench, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cauterized his ankle and brought him down to the dome of the mosque to visit him soon, and Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said in his supplication: O God, if You have left anything of the war against the Quraysh, then keep me for it, and if You have put the war between us and them, then start it, and do not let me die until my eyes are comforted by Banu Qurayzah. So God, the Most High, answered his supplication, and decreed that they submit to his judgment of their own free will, requesting it of their own accord. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned him from Medina to judge them, and when he arrived riding on a donkey that they had trampled on, the Aws began to seek refuge with him and say: O Sa`d, they are your clients, so treat them well, and they were gentle with him and kind to him, but he remained silent and did not respond to them. When they complained to him, he, may God be pleased with him, said: It was time for Sa'd not to be blamed for the sake of God. They knew that he would not outstrip them, so when he approached the tent in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rise and go to your master. The Muslims rose and made him stay there out of respect, reverence and honour in his place of authority so that his judgment over them would be more effective. When he sat down, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: These people - and he pointed to them - have submitted to your judgment, so rule over them as you wish. The man may God be pleased with him said: Is my judgment valid over them? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. He said: And over those in this tent? He said: Yes. He said: And over those over here - and he pointed to the side where the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was, but he was turning his face away from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) out of reverence, honour and respect. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Yes. He may God be pleased with him said: I rule that their fighters should be killed and their children and wealth should be taken captive. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: You have ruled with the ruling of God the Most High from above seven heavens. In another narration: You have ruled with the ruling of the King. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered that trenches be dug in the ground, and they were brought bound, and their necks were struck off. They were between seven and eight hundred, and those who had not yet grown hair were taken captive, along with their women and wealth. All of this is established in detail with its evidence and hadiths and its expansion in the book of the biography, which we have devoted briefly and simply, praise and thanks be to God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And He sent down those who supported them meaning those who aided the parties and helped them in fighting the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), of the People of the Scripture meaning Banu Qurayzah of the Jews from some of the tribes of the Children of Israel. Their fathers had settled in the Hijaz long ago, hoping to follow the unlettered Prophet, whom they found written about in the Torah and the Gospel. But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So they Damn it. God the Almighty said: from their strongholds meaning their fortresses, as Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata', Qatadah, As-Suddi and others among the Salaf said. The horns of cows are called so because they are the highest part of them, and He cast terror into their hearts meaning fear, because they had sided with the polytheists in fighting the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). And one who knows is not like one who does not know. They frightened the Muslims and sought to fight them so that they would gain honor in this world, but the situation was reversed and the situation was reversed for them. The polytheists rolled up their sleeves and won a deal that was lost to them. Just as they sought honor, they were humiliated, and they wanted to eradicate the Muslims, but they were eradicated. Added to that was the misery of the Hereafter, so the sentence became that this is the losing deal. For this reason God the Almighty said: A party you kill and a party you take captive Those who were killed are the fighters, and the captives are the young ones and the women. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham bin Bashir narrated to us, Abdul Malik bin Umair narrated to us, on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Qurazi, who said: I was presented to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Qurayzah, and they had doubts about me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered me to see if I had grown any hair yet. They looked but did not find any hair, so he released me and included me among the captives. This is how all the scholars of Sunan narrated it, through various chains of narration on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. An-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Atiyyah, in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: And He made you inherit their land and their homes and their wealth means He made them yours because you killed them. And a land which you have not trodden It was said: Khaybar, and it was said: Mecca. Malik narrated it on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, and it was said: Persia and Rome. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that all of them are meant: And God is over all things competent. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Alqamah bin Waqqas, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told me: I went out on the day of the Trench and made the people stand back. I heard the earth rumbling behind me, and there I saw Saad bin Muadh, may God be pleased with him, and with him was his nephew Al-Harith bin Aws carrying a shield. She said: So I sat on the ground, and Saad, may God be pleased with him, passed by, wearing an iron shield with its edges sticking out, and I was afraid for Saad’s edges. She said: Saad, may God be pleased with him, was one of the greatest and tallest people, and he passed by while he was chanting: He stayed a little while witnessing the battle. Death is better when the time comes. She said: So I got up and went into the garden, and there were a group of Muslims in it, and there was Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and among them was a man wearing a tasbihah headgear, so Umar may God be pleased with him said: What brought you? By God, you are indeed bold, and what guarantees that this is not a calamity or that you will flee? She said: He kept blaming me until I wished that the earth would split open under me at that moment, so I entered it, and the man removed the tasbihah from his face, and it was Talha ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, so he said: O Umar, woe to you, you have spoken too much since today, and where is the fleeing or protection except to God the Most High? She said: A man from Quraysh called Ibn al-Arqa shot Sa`d may God be pleased with him with an arrow and said to him: Take it, for I am Ibn al-Arqa. It hit his ankle and cut it off. Sa`d may God be pleased with him supplicated to God, saying: O God, do not let me die until you have relieved my eyes from Banu Qurayzah. She said: They were his allies and clients in the pre-Islamic period. She said: So his words were broken and God sent a wind against the polytheists: And God sufficed the believers in fighting, and God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. So Abu Sufyan and those with him fled to Tihamah, and `Uyaynah ibn Badr and those with him fled to Najd. Banu Qurayzah returned and fortified themselves in their fortresses. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned to Medina and ordered that a leather tent be pitched over Sa`d may God be pleased with him in the mosque. She said: “Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him while there was dust on his front teeth. He said: Have you laid down your weapons? No, by God, the angels have not laid down their weapons yet. Go out to Banu Qurayzah and fight them.” She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dressed for his nation and gave the people permission to leave. He passed by Banu Tamim, who were neighbors of the mosque, and said: Who passed by you? They said: Dihya al-Kalbi passed by us. Dihya al-Kalbi’s beard, age, and face resembled Gabriel (peace be upon him) in his age, age, and face. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When their siege intensified and the affliction intensified, it was said to them: Submit to the judgment of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They consulted Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir, and he indicated to them that it was slaughter. They said: We will submit to the judgment of Sa’d ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Submit to the judgment of Sa’d ibn Mu’adh. So they submitted. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for Sa’d ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. He brought him on a donkey with a saddlebag of palm fibers that he had loaded onto. His people surrounded him and said: O Abu Amr, they are your allies and your clients, and the people of calamity and those you know. She said: He does not return to them with anything and does not pay attention. To them, until when he approached their homes, he turned to his people and said: It is time for me not to care about the blame of the blamers for the sake of God. He said: Abu Saeed said: When he came out, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stand up for your master and bring him down. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Our master is God. He said: Bring him down. So they brought him down. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Judge concerning them. Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said: Then I judge concerning them by the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger. Then Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, supplicated and said: O God, if You have spared anything of the war between Your Prophet and the Quraysh, then keep me for it, and if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You. His words burst out and he had been freed from it except for something like a speck, and he returned to his tent that the Messenger of God had pitched over him. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar, may God be pleased with them, attended him. She said: “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I recognize the weeping of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, from the weeping of Umar, may God be pleased with him, and I was in my room, and they were as God the Almighty said: “Compassionate among themselves.” Alqamah said: I said, “O mother, how did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, act?” She said: “His eyes would not shed tears for anyone, but when he felt distressed, he would take hold of his beard, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, something similar to this, but shorter, and in it he supplicated Sa`d, may God be pleased with him.

He did not rebuke either group, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed them. He had appointed Ibn Umm Maktum, may God be pleased with him, as his successor in Madinah, and given the banner to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When the situation became too long for him, they submitted to the rule of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, the leader of the Aws, may God be pleased with him, because they had been their allies in the pre-Islamic period, and they believed that he would treat them well in that, as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had done with his clients. Banu Qaynuqa`, when he released them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they thought that Sa`d would do to them what Ibn Abi did to those people, and they did not know that Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, had been struck by an arrow in his ankle during the Battle of the Trench, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cauterized his ankle and brought him down to the dome of the mosque to visit him soon, and Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said in his supplication: O God, if You have left anything of the war against the Quraysh, then keep me for it, and if You have put the war between us and them, then start it, and do not let me die until my eyes are comforted by Banu Qurayzah. So God, the Most High, answered his supplication, and decreed that they submit to his judgment of their own free will, requesting it of their own accord. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned him from Medina to judge them, and when he arrived riding on a donkey that they had trampled on, the Aws began to seek refuge with him and say: O Sa`d, they are your clients, so treat them well, and they were gentle with him and kind to him, but he remained silent and did not respond to them. When they complained to him, he, may God be pleased with him, said: It was time for Sa'd not to be blamed for the sake of God. They knew that he would not outstrip them, so when he approached the tent in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rise and go to your master. The Muslims rose and made him stay there out of respect, reverence and honour in his place of authority so that his judgment over them would be more effective. When he sat down, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: These people - and he pointed to them - have submitted to your judgment, so rule over them as you wish. The man may God be pleased with him said: Is my judgment valid over them? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. He said: And over those in this tent? He said: Yes. He said: And over those over here - and he pointed to the side where the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was, but he was turning his face away from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) out of reverence, honour and respect. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Yes. He may God be pleased with him said: I rule that their fighters should be killed and their children and wealth should be taken captive. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: You have ruled with the ruling of God the Most High from above seven heavens. In another narration: You have ruled with the ruling of the King. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered that trenches be dug in the ground, and they were brought bound, and their necks were struck off. They were between seven and eight hundred, and those who had not yet grown hair were taken captive, along with their women and wealth. All of this is established in detail with its evidence and hadiths and its expansion in the book of the biography, which we have devoted briefly and simply, praise and thanks be to God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And He sent down those who supported them meaning those who aided the parties and helped them in fighting the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), of the People of the Scripture meaning Banu Qurayzah of the Jews from some of the tribes of the Children of Israel. Their fathers had settled in the Hijaz long ago, hoping to follow the unlettered Prophet, whom they found written about in the Torah and the Gospel. But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So they Damn it. God the Almighty said: from their strongholds meaning their fortresses, as Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata', Qatadah, As-Suddi and others among the Salaf said. The horns of cows are called so because they are the highest part of them, and He cast terror into their hearts meaning fear, because they had sided with the polytheists in fighting the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). And one who knows is not like one who does not know. They frightened the Muslims and sought to fight them so that they would gain honor in this world, but the situation was reversed and the situation was reversed for them. The polytheists rolled up their sleeves and won a deal that was lost to them. Just as they sought honor, they were humiliated, and they wanted to eradicate the Muslims, but they were eradicated. Added to that was the misery of the Hereafter, so the sentence became that this is the losing deal. For this reason God the Almighty said: A party you kill and a party you take captive Those who were killed are the fighters, and the captives are the young ones and the women. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham bin Bashir narrated to us, Abdul Malik bin Umair narrated to us, on the authority of Atiyyah Al-Qurazi, who said: I was presented to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Qurayzah, and they had doubts about me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered me to see if I had grown any hair yet. They looked but did not find any hair, so he released me and included me among the captives. This is how all the scholars of Sunan narrated it, through various chains of narration on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. An-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Atiyyah, in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: And He made you inherit their land and their homes and their wealth means He made them yours because you killed them. And a land which you have not trodden It was said: Khaybar, and it was said: Mecca. Malik narrated it on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, and it was said: Persia and Rome. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that all of them are meant: And God is over all things competent. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Alqamah bin Waqqas, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told me: I went out on the day of the Trench and made the people stand back. I heard the earth rumbling behind me, and there I saw Saad bin Muadh, may God be pleased with him, and with him was his nephew Al-Harith bin Aws carrying a shield. She said: So I sat on the ground, and Saad, may God be pleased with him, passed by, wearing an iron shield with its edges sticking out, and I was afraid for Saad’s edges. She said: Saad, may God be pleased with him, was one of the greatest and tallest people, and he passed by while he was chanting: He stayed a little while witnessing the battle. Death is better when the time comes. She said: So I got up and went into the garden, and there were a group of Muslims in it, and there was Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and among them was a man wearing a tasbihah headgear, so Umar may God be pleased with him said: What brought you? By God, you are indeed bold, and what guarantees that this is not a calamity or that you will flee? She said: He kept blaming me until I wished that the earth would split open under me at that moment, so I entered it, and the man removed the tasbihah from his face, and it was Talha ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, so he said: O Umar, woe to you, you have spoken too much since today, and where is the fleeing or protection except to God the Most High? She said: A man from Quraysh called Ibn al-Arqa shot Sa`d may God be pleased with him with an arrow and said to him: Take it, for I am Ibn al-Arqa. It hit his ankle and cut it off. Sa`d may God be pleased with him supplicated to God, saying: O God, do not let me die until you have relieved my eyes from Banu Qurayzah. She said: They were his allies and clients in the pre-Islamic period. She said: So his words were broken and God sent a wind against the polytheists: And God sufficed the believers in fighting, and God is Powerful and Exalted in Might. So Abu Sufyan and those with him fled to Tihamah, and `Uyaynah ibn Badr and those with him fled to Najd. Banu Qurayzah returned and fortified themselves in their fortresses. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned to Medina and ordered that a leather tent be pitched over Sa`d may God be pleased with him in the mosque. She said: “Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him while there was dust on his front teeth. He said: Have you laid down your weapons? No, by God, the angels have not laid down their weapons yet. Go out to Banu Qurayzah and fight them.” She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dressed for his nation and gave the people permission to leave. He passed by Banu Tamim, who were neighbors of the mosque, and said: Who passed by you? They said: Dihya al-Kalbi passed by us. Dihya al-Kalbi’s beard, age, and face resembled Gabriel (peace be upon him) in his age, age, and face. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them and besieged them for twenty-five nights. When their siege intensified and the affliction intensified, it was said to them: Submit to the judgment of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They consulted Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir, and he indicated to them that it was slaughter. They said: We will submit to the judgment of Sa’d ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Submit to the judgment of Sa’d ibn Mu’adh. So they submitted. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for Sa’d ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. He brought him on a donkey with a saddlebag of palm fibers that he had loaded onto. His people surrounded him and said: O Abu Amr, they are your allies and your clients, and the people of calamity and those you know. She said: He does not return to them with anything and does not pay attention. To them, until when he approached their homes, he turned to his people and said: It is time for me not to care about the blame of the blamers for the sake of God. He said: Abu Saeed said: When he came out, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stand up for your master and bring him down. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Our master is God. He said: Bring him down. So they brought him down. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Judge concerning them. Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said: Then I judge concerning them by the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger. Then Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, supplicated and said: O God, if You have spared anything of the war between Your Prophet and the Quraysh, then keep me for it, and if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You. His words burst out and he had been freed from it except for something like a speck, and he returned to his tent that the Messenger of God had pitched over him. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar, may God be pleased with them, attended him. She said: “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I recognize the weeping of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, from the weeping of Umar, may God be pleased with him, and I was in my room, and they were as God the Almighty said: “Compassionate among themselves.” Alqamah said: I said, “O mother, how did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, act?” She said: “His eyes would not shed tears for anyone, but when he felt distressed, he would take hold of his beard, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, something similar to this, but shorter, and in it he supplicated Sa`d, may God be pleased with him.
33:28: This is an order from God, the Blessed and Exalted, to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give his wives the choice between him leaving them and going to someone else with whom they can obtain the life of this world and its adornments, or being patient with the hardship of his situation, for they will have a great reward from God, the Most High, for that. So they chose, may God be pleased with them and may God and His Messenger be pleased with them, the Hereafter. So God, the Most High, then combined for them the good of this world and the happiness of the Hereafter. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu`ayb told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah bin `Abd Al-Rahman told me that `Aishah, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to her when God, the Most High, commanded him to give his wives a choice. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with me and said: I am going to mention to you a matter, so do not be hasty until you consult your parents, for he knows that my parents did not command me to leave him. She said: Then he said: God, the Most High, said: O Prophet, tell your wives to the end of the two verses. I said to him: In which of these should I consult my parents? For I want God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter? And he narrated it in a suspended chain of transmission from Al-Layth. Yunus told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of `Aishah, may God be pleased with her, and he mentioned it, and he added: She said: Then the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did as I did. Al-Bukhari narrated that Mu`ammar was confused about it, sometimes narrating it on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Salamah, and sometimes Narrated by Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dhabi told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: When the choice was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: I want to mention a matter to you, so do not decide anything about it until you consult your parents. She said: I said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: He repeated it to her. She said: What is it, O Messenger of God? She said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to her: ‘O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment…’ to the end of the verse.” She said: “I said: ‘Rather, we choose God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter.’” She said: “Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejoiced at that.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: When the verse of choice was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) started with me and said: “Aisha, I am presenting a matter to you, so do not give a decision about it until you have presented it to your parents: Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman may God be pleased with them. She said: “O Messenger of God, what is it?” He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God, the Almighty, said: ‘O Prophet, tell your wives: If you should desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release. But if you should desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, God has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward.’” She said: “I desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, and I do not consult my parents, Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman may God be pleased with them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed, then he asked the stone to recite it and said: ‘Aisha may God be pleased with her said such and such.’ They said: ‘And we say what Aisha may God be pleased with them all said.’” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ on the authority of Abu Usama on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Amr on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, my father told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to give them a choice, he came to me and said: I will mention to you a matter, but do not be hasty until you consult your father. I said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: I have been commanded to give you a choice, and he recited to her the verse of choice until the end of the two verses. She said: “I said: What is it that you say, ‘Do not be hasty until you consult your father?’ For I choose God and His Messenger.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with that, and he presented it to his wives, and they all followed one another, and they chose God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid ibn Sinan al-Basri narrated to us, Abu Salih Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me, Uqayl narrated to me on the authority of al-Zuhri, Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr informed me on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both who said: Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The verse of choice was revealed, and he began with me, the first of his wives, and the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: I am going to mention to you something, but do not worry if you hasten until you consult your parents. She said: He knew that my parents would not order me to leave him. She said: Then he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: O Prophet, tell your wives (al-Masjid al-Haram 2:17), the two verses. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: I said: Is it in this that I consult my parents? Indeed, I want God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. Then he gave all his wives the choice, and they said what Aisha may God be pleased with them had said. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a choice, so we chose him, and he did not promise us anything.” They both narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Zakariya bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came to ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the people were sitting at his door, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, but he was not given permission. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, came and asked permission, but he was not given permission. Then Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, were given permission, and they entered while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with his wives around him, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I will speak to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perhaps he will laugh. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, if you had seen the daughter of Zayd - the wife of Umar - who asked me for maintenance just now, so I struck her neck, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed. And he the Prophet made peace until his molars were visible and said: They are all around me asking me for support. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him went to Aisha to beat her, and Umar may God be pleased with him went to Hafsa, both of them saying: “You are asking the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for something he does not have.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them. They said: “By God, we will not ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after this meeting for something he does not have.” God the Almighty revealed the choice, and he began with Aisha may God be pleased with her and said: I am mentioning to you a matter which I do not like you to hasten until you consult your parents. She said: What is it? He recited to her: O Prophet, tell your wives the verse. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: Is it you that I should consult my parents about? Rather, I have chosen God Almighty and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to any of your wives what I have chosen. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty did not send me to be harsh, but He sent me as a teacher and a facilitator. No woman among them asks me about what I have chosen except that I will tell her. Muslim alone transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. He and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Zakariya ibn Ishaq Al-Makki. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: Surayj bin Yunus told us, Ali bin Hisham bin Al-Barid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ubaid God bin Ali bin Abi Rafi, on the authority of Uthman bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave his wives the choice of this world and the Hereafter, but he did not give them the choice of divorce.” This is an interrupted chain of narration. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Qatada and others, but it is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse, for he said: Then come, I will provide for you and set you free with gracious freedom, meaning, I will give you your rights and set you free. The scholars differed over the permissibility of someone else marrying them if he divorced them. There are two opinions, the more correct of which is: Yes, if that happens in order to achieve the purpose of the release, and God knows best. Ikrimah said: He had nine wives at that time: five from Quraysh 106:Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habib, Sawda, and Umm Salama, may God be pleased with them. He also had Safiyya bint Huyayy al-Nadiriyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyah, may God be pleased with them all.

Then he gave all his wives the choice, and they said what Aisha may God be pleased with them had said. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a choice, so we chose him, and he did not promise us anything.” They both narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Zakariya bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came to ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the people were sitting at his door, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, but he was not given permission. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, came and asked permission, but he was not given permission. Then Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, were given permission, and they entered while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with his wives around him, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I will speak to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, perhaps he will laugh. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, if you had seen the daughter of Zayd - the wife of Umar - who asked me for maintenance just now, so I struck her neck, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed. And he the Prophet made peace until his molars were visible and said: They are all around me asking me for support. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him went to Aisha to beat her, and Umar may God be pleased with him went to Hafsa, both of them saying: “You are asking the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for something he does not have.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them. They said: “By God, we will not ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after this meeting for something he does not have.” God the Almighty revealed the choice, and he began with Aisha may God be pleased with her and said: I am mentioning to you a matter which I do not like you to hasten until you consult your parents. She said: What is it? He recited to her: O Prophet, tell your wives the verse. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: Is it you that I should consult my parents about? Rather, I have chosen God Almighty and His Messenger, and I ask you not to mention to any of your wives what I have chosen. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty did not send me to be harsh, but He sent me as a teacher and a facilitator. No woman among them asks me about what I have chosen except that I will tell her. Muslim alone transmitted it, not Al-Bukhari. He and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Zakariya ibn Ishaq Al-Makki. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: Surayj bin Yunus told us, Ali bin Hisham bin Al-Barid told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ubaid God bin Ali bin Abi Rafi, on the authority of Uthman bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave his wives the choice of this world and the Hereafter, but he did not give them the choice of divorce.” This is an interrupted chain of narration. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Qatada and others, but it is contrary to the apparent meaning of the verse, for he said: Then come, I will provide for you and set you free with gracious freedom, meaning, I will give you your rights and set you free. The scholars differed over the permissibility of someone else marrying them if he divorced them. There are two opinions, the more correct of which is: Yes, if that happens in order to achieve the purpose of the release, and God knows best. Ikrimah said: He had nine wives at that time: five from Quraysh 106:Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habib, Sawda, and Umm Salama, may God be pleased with them. He also had Safiyya bint Huyayy al-Nadiriyah, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyah, may God be pleased with them all.
33:30: God Almighty says, admonishing the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who chose God, His Messenger, and the other world, and whose affair was settled under the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was appropriate for him to inform them of their ruling and to single them out from among the other women, that whoever among them commits a clear indecency... Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It is rebellion and bad character, and in any case it is a condition, and a condition does not necessarily occur, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And it has already been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and to those before you, ‘If you should associate [anything] with God, your work would surely become worthless.’ And in the saying of God the Almighty: And if they had associated [anything] with God, all that they used to do would surely become worthless for them. “Say, ‘If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.’” “If God had willed to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Glory be to Him! He is God, the One, the Prevailing.” Since their status was high, it was appropriate to make the sin, if committed by them, severe, in order to protect their honor and their high veil. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Whoever among you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her twice. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, The punishment will be doubled for her twice. He said: In this world and the hereafter. And on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, And that is easy for God. That is, easy and simple. Then He mentioned His justice and grace in His saying: And whoever among you is obedient to God… And His Messenger,” meaning, and He responds, “We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision,” meaning in Paradise, for they are in the stations of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the highest of the highest, above the stations of all creation in the intermediary, which is the closest station in Paradise to the Throne.
33:31: God Almighty says, admonishing the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who chose God, His Messenger, and the other world, and whose affair was settled under the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was appropriate for him to inform them of their ruling and to single them out from among the other women, that whoever among them commits a clear indecency... Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It is rebellion and bad character. In any case, it is a condition, and a condition does not necessarily occur, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And it has already been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and to those before you, ‘If you should associate [anything] with God, your work would surely become worthless.’ And in the saying of God the Almighty: And if they had associated [anything] with God, all that they used to do would surely become worthless. “Say, ‘If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers.’” “If God had willed to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Glory be to Him! He is God, the One, the Prevailing.” Since their status was high, it was appropriate to make the sin, if committed by them, severe, in order to protect their honor and their high veil. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Whoever among you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her twice. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, The punishment will be doubled for her twice. He said: In this world and the hereafter. And on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. And that is easy for God. That is, easy and simple. Then He mentioned His justice and grace in His saying: And whoever among you is obedient to God… And His Messenger,” meaning, and He responds, “We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision,” meaning in Paradise, for they are in the stations of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the highest of the highest, above the stations of all creation in the intermediary, which is the closest station in Paradise to the Throne.
33:32: These are the manners that God the Most High commanded the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to follow, and the women of the ummah follow them in that. So God the Most High said, addressing the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if they fear God the Almighty as He commanded them, then no other woman will be like them or reach them in virtue and status. Then God the Most High said: So do not speak in a soft voice. Al-Suddi and others said: By that, he means softening the speech when addressing men. For this reason, God the Most High said: lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet meaning deceit. And speak in appropriate speech. Ibn Zayd said: Good, beautiful, and well-known words of goodness. The meaning of this is that she should address strangers with speech that is not softened, meaning that a woman should not address strangers as she addresses her husband. God the Almighty said: And abide in your houses meaning the time, so do not go out except for a need. Among the legitimate needs is praying in the mosque, provided that it is permissible, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not prevent the female servants of God from the mosques of God, and let them go out without decency. In another narration: And their homes are better for them. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Hamid ibn Mas’adah told us, Abu Raja’ al-Kalbi told us, Ruh ibn al-Musayyab is trustworthy, Thabit al-Banani told us, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, who said: “Women came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, the men have taken the virtue and jihad in the cause of God, so what work do we have that will equal the work of those who strive in the cause of God? The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever among you stays in her house - or a word similar to that - will attain the work of those who strive in the cause of God.” Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it from Thabit except Ruh ibn al-Musayyab, and he is a well-known man from Basra. Al-Bazzar also said: Muhammad Al-Muthanna told us, Amr bin Asim told me, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Mawariq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “A woman is ‘awrah, and when she goes out, Satan makes her look suspiciously. She is closest to the spirit of her Lord when she is in the depths of her home.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Amr bin Asim, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Bazzar narrated with his chain of transmission mentioned above, and Abu Dawud also narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: A woman’s prayer in her bedroom is better than her prayer in her house, and her prayer in her house is better than her prayer in her room. This is a good chain of transmission. God the Almighty said: {And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance}. Mujahid said: A woman would go out walking in front of men, and that was the display of the times of ignorance. Qatada said: {And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance} meaning: If you go out of your houses and they walk gracefully and flirtatiously, then God the Almighty forbade that. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: {And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance}. Displaying yourselves means that she puts the veil over her head and does not tighten it, so that it covers her necklaces, earrings and neck, and all of that is visible from her, and that is the display of her beauty. Then the women of the believers became widespread in display of their beauty. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Zuhair told me, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat told us, Ali ibn Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: He recited this verse: And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance. He said: It was between Noah and Idris, and it was a thousand years, and there were two clans of the children of Adam, one of them lived in the plain and the other lived in the mountains, and the men of the mountains were beautiful, but the women were ugly. The women of the plain were beautiful in the morning, while the men were ugly. Satan, may God curse him, came to a man from the plain in the form of a boy, and hired himself out to him, so he served him. Satan took something like the symbolism of the shepherds, and he came in it with a voice that people had never heard the like of. This reached those around him, so they came back to listen to him, and they made a festival to which they would gather throughout the year, so the women would display themselves for the men, and the men would adorn themselves for them. A man from the mountain attacked them on their festival, and he saw the women and their beauty, so he came to his companions and informed them of that, so they turned to them and descended with them, and indecency appeared among them, as is the saying of God Almighty: And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance. God the Almighty said: {And establish prayer and give zakat and obey God and His Messenger} He first forbade them from evil and then ordered them to do good, such as establishing prayer, which is the worship of God alone with no partner, and giving zakat, which is kindness to creation. And obey God and His Messenger This is a case of linking the general to the specific. God the Almighty said: {God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household, and to purify you with a thorough purification} This is a clear statement that the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) are included among the people of the household here, because they are the reason for the revelation of this verse, and the reason for revelation is included in it according to one opinion, either on its own according to one opinion, or with something else according to the correct opinion. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he used to call out in the marketplace: {God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the Household, and to purify you with a thorough purification} It was revealed specifically about the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Thus, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Ali bin Harb Al-Mawsili told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Hussain bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the verse: God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, he said: It was revealed specifically regarding the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah said: Whoever wants to know about his family, it was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If what is meant is that they were the reason for the revelation and not others, then it is correct.
