He said: His women are among his household, but the people of his household are those for whom charity is forbidden. He said: And who are they? He said: They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Jaafar, and the family of Abbas, may God be pleased with them. He said: Is charity forbidden to all of these after them? He said: Yes. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Bakkar bin Al-Rayyan on the authority of Hassan bin Ibrahim on the authority of Saeed bin Masrouq on the authority of Yazid bin Hayyan on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned the hadith similar to what was mentioned above, and in it I said to him: Are his women from the people of his house? He said: No, by God, a woman may be with a man for an age, then he divorces her and she returns to her father. The people of his house are his origin and his clan who forbade charity after him. This is how it happened in this narration, and the first is better and more appropriate to take it. This second possibility suggests that he wanted to explain the family mentioned in the hadith he narrated, that what is meant by them is his family who were forbidden from charity, or that what is meant by family is not only the wives, but they are with his family, and this possibility is more likely to reconcile them with the narration before it, and also to reconcile the Qur’an and the hadiths that came before it if they are authentic, because there is a problem with some of their chains of transmission, and God knows best. Then what is not in doubt from contemplating the Qur’an is that the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are included in the words of God Almighty: God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the household, and to purify you with a thorough purification, because the context of the speech is with them, and for this reason God Almighty said after all of this: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom, meaning, act according to what God Almighty sends down to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in your houses from the Book and the Sunnah, as Qatadah and more than one said, and remember this blessing that you were singled out from among the people, that the revelation is sent down in your houses without the rest of the people, and Aisha, the truthful daughter of the truthful, may God be pleased with them both, is the first of them to receive this blessing. And the most fortunate of them in this bounty, and the most special of them in this universal mercy, is that the revelation did not come down to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the bed of any other woman, as stated by God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Some scholars may God have mercy on him said: Because he did not marry a virgin other than her, and no man slept with her in her bed other than him (peace and blessings of God be upon him and may God be pleased with her), it was appropriate that she be singled out for this privilege and this high rank. However, if his wives were from his household, then his relatives are more deserving of this name, as mentioned in the hadith: And my household is more deserving. This is similar to what was proven in Sahih Muslim: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day, he said: It is this mosque of mine.” This is of this type, for the verse was revealed regarding the mosque of Quba’, as mentioned in other hadiths. However, if that was founded on piety from the first day, then the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more deserving of this name, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Walid told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Hisain bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Jamila, who said: Al-Hasan bin Ali may God be pleased with them both was appointed caliph when Ali may God be pleased with them both was killed. He said: While he was praying, a man jumped on him and stabbed him with his dagger. Hisain claimed that he had heard that the one who stabbed him was a man from Banu Asad, and Al-Hasan may God be pleased with him was prostrating. He said: They claim that the stab wound was in his hip, and he was sick for months and then recovered. He sat on the pulpit and said: O people of Iraq, fear God in our regard, for we are your leaders and your guests, and we are the people of the house about whom God the Most High said: God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the house, and to purify you with a thorough purification. He said: He kept saying this until there was no one in the mosque who did not cry and wail. Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam that he said: Ali bin Al-Hussein may God be pleased with him said to a man from Ash-Sham: Have you not read in al-Ahzab 33:God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification? He said: Yes, and you are them? He said: Yes. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is ever Kind and Aware means that it is through His kindness to you that you have attained this status, and through His knowledge of you and that you are worthy of that, He gave that to you and singled you out for it. Ibn Jarir may God have mercy on him said: And remember the blessing of God upon you by placing you in homes in which the verses of God and wisdom are recited, so thank God for that and praise Him. Indeed, God is ever Kind and Aware meaning that He was kind to you, as He placed you in homes in which the verses of God and wisdom are recited, and this is the Sunnah. He is Aware of you as He chose you for His Messenger. Qatada said: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom He said: He bestows that favor upon them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Atiyah Al-Awfi said about the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is Kind and All-Knowing, meaning that He is Kind in extracting it and All-Knowing in its location. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: And it was also narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas on the authority of Qatada.
33:35: Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us: Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Uthman bin Hakim told us, Abdul Rahman bin Shaibah told us: I heard Umm Salamah may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), say: I said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), why are we not mentioned in the Qur’an as men are? She said: One day, I was startled by him when I heard him calling out from the pulpit while I was combing my hair. So I wrapped my hair and went out to my room, the room of my house, and I listened by the palm frond. Then I heard him saying from the pulpit, “O people, God the Most High says: ‘Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women,’” to the end of the verse. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Jarir narrated it in this way from the hadith of Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad, with a similar chain of transmission. Another chain of transmission from her Al-Nasa’i also said: Muhammad ibn Hatim told us, Suwayd told us, Abdullah ibn Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, that she said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Prophet of God, why do I hear men mentioned in the Qur’an and women not? So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, that Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib told him on the authority of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, that she said: I said: O Messenger of God, men are mentioned and we are not, so God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women. Another way Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid who said: Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, said: O Messenger of God, men are mentioned and we are not. So God Almighty revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women the verse. Another Hadith Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us: Sayyar bin Muzahir Al-Anzi told us: Abu Kudayna Yahya bin Al-Muhallab told us, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The women said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Why does he mention the believing men and not the believing women? So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women (al-Baqarah 2:17). Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Some women entered upon the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: God, the Most High, has mentioned you in the Qur’an but has not mentioned us at all. Is there not in us something that is mentioned? So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women (al-Baqarah 2:17). God, the Most High, said: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women (al-Baqarah 2:17) is evidence that faith is not Islam, and it is more specific than it, because God, the Most High, said: The desert Arabs say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed; but say, “We have submitted, for faith has not yet entered your hearts.’” (al-Baqarah 2:17) In the two Sahihs, it says: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer. This takes away his faith, but this does not necessarily mean that he is an unbeliever, according to the consensus of the Muslims. This indicates that it is more specific than it, as we stated first in the explanation of Al-Bukhari. And the Almighty said: And the men who are obedient, men and women. Obedience is to obey in tranquility. Is he who is obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? And the Almighty said: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth? All are obedient to Him. “O Mary, be obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow.” And stand before God, devoutly obedient. Islam comes after it as a level to which it ascends, which is faith, then obedience arises from them. And the truthful men and truthful women. This is in the sayings, for truthfulness is a praiseworthy characteristic, and for this reason some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, were never found to have lied, neither in the pre-Islamic period nor in Islam. It is a sign of faith, just as lying is a sign of hypocrisy, and whoever is truthful will be saved. “You must be truthful, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. And beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to Hell. A man continues to be truthful and seeks to be truthful until he is recorded with God as truthful, and a man continues to…” He lies and seeks to lie until he is recorded before God as a liar. There are many hadiths about this. The patient men and the patient women This is the characteristic of the steadfast, which is patience in the face of calamities, and the knowledge that what is destined will inevitably happen and accepting that with patience at the first shock, meaning the most difficult at first glance, then what comes after it is easier than it, which is the sincerity and steadfastness of the nature. The humble men and the humble women Humility: tranquility and reassurance, deliberation and dignity, and modesty, and what motivates it is the fear of God Almighty and His observation, as in the hadith Worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. “The charitable men and charitable women” Charity is doing good to the needy, weak people who have no income and no one to earn it. They give from the excess money in obedience to God and as kindness to His creation. It has been proven in the two Sahihs, “Seven whom God will shade in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His shade - and he mentioned among them - a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand is spending.” And in another hadith, Charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire. There are many hadiths urging this, each with its own topic: and the fasting men and fasting women. In the hadith narrated by Ibn Majah, it says: Fasting is the zakat of the body, meaning it purifies and cleanses it of bad humors, both by nature and by the Shari’ah. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: “Whoever fasts Ramadan and three days of every month is included in the words of God the Almighty: ‘and the fasting men and fasting women.’” And since fasting is one of the greatest aids in curbing desire, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “O young men, whoever among you can afford to get married, let him get married, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and guarding one’s chastity. And whoever cannot afford it, let him fast, for it will be a restraint for him.” It is appropriate to mention after it: and the men and women who guard their private parts, meaning from forbidden things and sins, except for permissible things, as God the Almighty said: “And those who guard their private parts, * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed. * But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors.” And the Almighty said: And the men who remember God often, men and women. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ubaidullah told us, Muhammad bin Jabir told us, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Al-Agharr Abu Muslim, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man wakes his wife at night and they pray two rak’ahs, they will be recorded that night among the men who remember God often, men and women. Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Agharr Abu Muslim, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, which of the servants will have the highest degree before God on the Day of Resurrection?’ He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: ‘Those who remember God frequently, both men and women.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, and who fights in the cause of God?’ He said: ‘If he were to strike with his sword among the infidels and polytheists until it breaks and is covered in blood, those who remember God would be better than him.’” Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim told us, on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was traveling on the road to Mecca when he came to Jamdan. He said: ‘This is Jamdan. Go, for the single men have already gone ahead.’ They said: ‘And who are the single men?’ He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Those who remember God often, men and women.’ Then he (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘O God, forgive those who shave their heads.’ They said: ‘And those who cut their hair short?’ He... said: ‘And those who cut their hair short.’” This is the only version of this hadith narrated by Muslim, but not the end of it. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjin bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Ziyad, the freed slave of Abdullah bin Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, who said: It reached me on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No human being has ever done a deed that will save him from the punishment of God, the Most High, than the remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic.’” Muadh, may God be pleased with him, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Shall I not tell you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them before your Lord, the highest of them in your degrees, and better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy tomorrow and striking their necks and they striking your necks?’ They said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic.’” Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, Zaban bin Fa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Sahl bin Mu’adh bin Anas Al-Juhani, on the authority of his father may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “A man asked him, ‘Which of the mujahideen has the greatest reward, O Messenger of God?’ He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Those who remember God the most.’ He said, ‘Which of the fasting ones has the greatest reward?’ He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Those who remember God the most.’ Then he mentioned prayer, zakat, pilgrimage, and charity. ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘Those who remember God the most.’” Abu Bakr said to Umar may God be pleased with them both: Those who remember God have gone with all good. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Yes. And we will mention, God willing, the rest of the hadiths that have been narrated about frequent remembrance of God, when God says in this surah, ‘O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance * And glorify Him morning and evening.’” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], God willing. God Almighty says: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward, which is report about all of those mentioned, meaning that God Almighty has prepared for them, that is, made ready for them, forgiveness from Him for their sins and a great reward, which is Paradise.
33:36: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the Almighty’s statement: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their wives or children (al-Baqarah 2:17). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to propose marriage to his young lady Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him. He entered upon Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, may God be pleased with her, and proposed marriage to her. She said: I will not marry him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, then marry him. She said: O Messenger of God, am I being commanded to do so in my own soul? While they were talking, God revealed this verse to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice about their wives or children. She said: O Messenger of God, have you approved him for me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. She said: “Then I will not disobey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I have married him to myself.” Ibn Lahi’ah said, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umrah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to Zaynab bint Jahsh for Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him, but she refused him and said: I am better than him in lineage. She was a woman who had a sharp temper, so God Almighty revealed: ‘And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman…’” The entire verse. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same, and it was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh, may God be pleased with her, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her for his freedman, Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him, and she refused, then she accepted. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It was revealed about Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, may God be pleased with her, and she was the first woman to emigrate, meaning after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. She offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I accept. So Zayd ibn Haritha, may God be pleased with him, married her after he had separated from Zaynab. She and her brother were angry and said: We only wanted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so we married his slave. He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter to the end of the verse. He said: And a more comprehensive command came than this: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. He said: That is specific and this is more comprehensive. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed marriage to a woman from the Ansar on behalf of her father, and he said: ‘Until I consult her mother.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then yes.’ The man went to his wife and mentioned that to her. She said: ‘By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, found no one but Julaybib, and we have prevented her from so-and-so and so-and-so.’ The slave girl was listening in her seclusion. The man went to inform the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, but the slave girl said: ‘Do you want to return the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? If he has accepted him for you, then marry him.’ It was as if she had left her parents, and they said: ‘You have spoken the truth.’ Her father went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘If you are pleased with him, then we are pleased with him.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then I am pleased with him.’ He said: ‘So he married her.’ Then the people of Medina were alarmed, and Julaybib rode out, and they found him killed, with people around him.” From the polytheists he killed, Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: I saw it and it was from the most generous house in Medina. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, meaning Ibn Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Kinanah ibn Nu`aym al-`Adawi, on the authority of Abu Barzah al-Aslami, who said: “Julaibib was a man who would enter upon women, pass by them, and play with them. So I said to my wife: ‘Do not let Julaybib enter upon you today, for if he enters upon you, I will do this and that.’ She said: ‘And among the Ansar, if one of them had a widow, he would not marry her off until he knew whether the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a need for her or not.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man from the Ansar: ‘Marry me your daughter.’ He said: ‘Yes, and with honor, O Messenger of God, and with the blessing of my eye.’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not want her for myself.’ He said: ‘For whom, O Messenger of God?’ He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘For Julaybib.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, shall I consult her mother?’ So he went to her mother and said: ‘Is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposing marriage to your daughter?’ She said: ‘Yes, and with the blessing of my eye.’ He said: ‘He is not proposing marriage to her for himself, but rather for Julaybib.’ She said: ‘Julaibib.’ Is it Jalibib? Is it Jalibib? By God, we will not marry him. So when he wanted to go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and tell him what her mother had said, the slave girl said: Who proposed to you for me? So her mother told her. She said: Do you refuse the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) his matter? Hand me over to him, for he will not let me down. So her father went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Do as you wish with her. So he married her to Jalibib. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out on a military expedition, and when God had bestowed upon him the spoils of war, he said to his companions may God be pleased with them: Are you missing anyone? They said: We are missing so-and-so and we are missing so-and-so. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Look, are you missing anyone? They said: No. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: But I miss Julaybib. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So look for him among the dead. So they looked for him and found him beside seven people whom he had killed and then killed him. They said: O Messenger of God, here he is beside seven people whom he had killed and then killed him. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to him and stood over him and said: He killed seven and they killed him. This is from me and I am from him, two or three times. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) placed him on his forearms and dug a grave for him. He had no bed except the forearm of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he placed him in his grave and did not mention that he washed him, may God be pleased with him. Thabit may God be pleased with him said: There was no widow among the Ansar who spent more than her. And the hadith of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah is confirmed: Do you know what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed for her? He said: He said: “O God, pour goodness upon her abundantly and do not make her life a struggle.” And that is how it was. There was no widow among the Ansar who spent more than her. This is how Imam Ahmad reported it in full. Muslim and al-Nasa’i included in al-Fada’il the story of his killing from it. Al-Hafiz Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr mentioned in al-Isti’ab that When the slave girl said in her chamber: Do you reject the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? This verse was revealed: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. Ibn Jurayj said: Aamer bin Mus`ab informed me on the authority of Tawus who said: He asked Ibn `Abbas about two rak`ahs after the `Asr prayer and he forbade him. Ibn `Abbas may God be pleased with him recited: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. This verse is general and applies to all matters. That is because when God and His Messenger rule on something, no one has the right to disobey Him. No one has a choice here, no opinion or statement, as God the Most High said: “But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.” And in the hadith: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you truly believes until his inclination is subservient to what you have brought. For this reason, He was strict in opposing that, saying: And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error. Like His statement: “So let those beware who oppose the Prophet’s (blessings and peace of God be upon him) order, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment be inflicted upon them.”
33:37: The Almighty says, informing us about His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to his freed slave Zaid bin Haritha, may God be pleased with him, who was the one upon whom God bestowed His blessings, that is, Islam and following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, And bestowed His blessings upon him, that is, freedom from slavery. He was a great and noble master, beloved to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was called Al-Hab, and his son Usama was called Al-Hab bin Al-Hab. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never sent him on a military expedition except that he appointed him over them, and if he had lived after him, he would have appointed him as his successor. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Saeed bin Muhammad Al-Warraq and Muhammad bin Ubaid on the authority of Wael bin Dawud on the authority of Abdullah Al-Bahi on her authority. Al-Bazzar said: Khalid bin Yusuf told us, Abu Awana told us, Muhammad bin Muammar told us, Abu Dawud told us, Abu Awana told us, Umar bin Abi Salamah told me on the authority of his father, who said: Usamah bin Zaid, may God be pleased with them both, told me: I was in the mosque when Al-Abbas and Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them both, came to me and said: O Usamah, ask permission for us to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, saying: Ali and Al-Abbas are asking permission. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what their need is? I said: No, O Messenger of God. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But I know. He said: So he gave them permission. They said: O Messenger of God, we have come to you so that you may tell us which of your family is dearest to you? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dearest of my family to me is Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad. They said: O Messenger of God, we are not asking you about Fatimah. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then Usamah bin Zaid bin Haritha, upon whom God has bestowed His blessings and upon whom I have bestowed His blessings. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had… He married his cousin Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah may God be pleased with her, and her mother was Umaimah bint Abdul Muttalib. Her dowry was ten dinars and sixty dirhams, a veil, a sheet, a coat of mail, fifty mudds of food and ten mudds of dates, as stated by Muqatil ibn Hayyan. He stayed with him for nearly a year or more, then something happened between them. Zayd came to complain about her to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) kept saying to him: Keep your wife and fear God. God the Most High said: And you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal, and you fear people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir mentioned here narrations from some of the early generations may God be pleased with them, but we would like to ignore them due to their lack of authenticity, so we will not cite them. Imam Ahmad also narrated here a hadith narrated by Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, which contains a strange issue, so we have also omitted its context. Al-Bukhari also narrated part of it in an abbreviated form, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Raheem told us, Ma’la ibn Mansur told us on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, Thabit told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: This verse, And you concealed within yourself that which God was going to bring to light, was revealed about Zayd. Thabit told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: This verse, And you concealed within yourself that which God was going to bring to light, was revealed about Zayd bint Jahsh and Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with them both. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Hashim Marzuq told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn may God be pleased with them both asked me what al-Hasan had to say about the verse: "And you concealed within yourself that which God was to bring to light." So I mentioned it to him, and he said: "No, but God informed His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that she would be one of his wives before he married her. So when Zayd may God be pleased with him came to him to complain about her, he said: 'Fear God and keep your wife.' He said: 'I have informed you that I will marry her to you, and you concealed within yourself that which God was to bring to light.'" And it was narrated from al-Suddi that he said something similar. Ibn Jarir said: Ishaq bin Shaheen told us, Khalid told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: If Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything of what was revealed to him from the Book of God Almighty, he would have concealed: And you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal, and you fear the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. And the Almighty’s saying: And when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you. Want means need and desire, meaning when he finished with her and left her, We married her to you. And the One who was in charge of marrying her to him was God Almighty, meaning that He revealed to him that he should consummate the marriage with her without a guardian, a contract, a dowry, or human witnesses. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim, meaning Ibn Al-Qasim, told us, Al-Nadr told us, Sulayman Ibn Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: When Zaynab’s waiting period ended, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Zayd Ibn Haritha, Go and mention her to me. So he went until he came to her while she was fermenting her dough. He said: When I saw her, she became so great in my heart that I could not look at her and say that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned her. So I turned my back on her and turned back on my heels, and I said: “O Zaynab, be of good cheer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has sent me to mention you.” She said: I will not do anything until I consult my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. So she stood up to go to her place of prayer, and the Qur’an was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered upon her without permission. I saw us when she entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we fed her bread and meat. The people went out, and some men remained talking in the house after the meal. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, and I followed him. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept following the rooms of his wives, greeting them. And they said: O Messenger of God, how did you find your family? I do not know whether I told him that the people had left or he was told. So he went until he entered the house, so I went to enter with him, but he threw a curtain between me and him. Then the veil was revealed and the people were admonished with what they were admonished with: Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission, the entire verse. Muslim and An-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Sulayman ibn Al-Mughira. Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him who said: Zainab bint Jahsh may God be pleased with her used to boast to the wives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), saying: Your families married you, but God married me from above the seven heavens. We have already mentioned in Surat An-Nur on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jahsh who said: Zainab and Aisha may God be pleased with them were boasting, and Zainab may God be pleased with her said: I am the one whose marriage was sent down from the heavens. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: I am the one whose excuse was sent down from the heavens. Zainab may God be pleased with her acknowledged her. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Zainab may God be pleased with her used to say to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), “I am more inclined towards you in three ways, and none of your wives can claim them all: My grandfather and your grandfather are one, and God, the Almighty, married me to you from the heavens, and the ambassador is Gabriel (peace be upon him).” God the Almighty said: So that there will be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need of them. That is, We have only permitted you to marry her, and We did that so that there would be no blame upon the believers in marrying the divorced women of their adopted sons. This is because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had adopted Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him before his prophethood, and he used to call him Zayd ibn Muhammad. Then God the Almighty cut off this relationship with His saying: “And He has not made your adopted sons your sons. That is your statement from your mouths, and God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God.” Then He added to that clarification and confirmation by the marriage of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to Zaynab bint Jahsh may God be pleased with her, when Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him divorced her. For this reason, God the Almighty said in the verse of prohibition: and the wives of your sons who are from your loins, to beware of the adopted son, as that was common among them. God Almighty says: And the command of God was to be carried out. That is, this matter that occurred was decreed and determined by God Almighty, and it will inevitably happen. Zainab, may God be pleased with her, was known by God to have become one of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
33:38: God the Almighty says: There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has enjoined upon him meaning in what He has permitted him and commanded him to do, such as marrying Zaynab may God be pleased with her who was divorced by his adopted son, Zayd ibn Haritha may God be pleased with him. And His statement: The way of God with those who passed on before means this is the ruling of God the Almighty regarding the prophets before him. He would not command them to do anything, and there would be blame upon them for doing so. This is a refutation of those hypocrites who imagined a deficiency in his marrying her to the wife of Zayd, his freed slave and adopted son whom he had adopted. And the command of God is a decree decreed meaning that His command that He decrees will inevitably come to pass and will not be avoided or changed. Whatever He wills will happen, and whatever He does not will will not happen.
33:39: God Almighty praises those who convey the messages of God that is, to His creation and deliver them faithfully and fear Him that is, they fear Him and do not fear anyone other than Him, so no one’s power prevents them from conveying the messages of God Almighty, and sufficient is God as a Reckoner that is, God is sufficient as a supporter and helper, and the master of people in this position, and in every position, is Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he carried out the message and conveyed it to the people of the East and the West, to all types of the children of Adam, and God Almighty made His word, religion, and law prevail over all religions and laws, for the prophet before him was only sent to his people specifically, but as for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was sent to all of creation, Arabs and non-Arabs, Say, ‘O people, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all’ Then his nation inherited the position of conveying from him after him, so the highest of those who carried it out after him were his companions, may God be pleased with them, they conveyed it from him as he commanded them in all his sayings and actions And his conditions, during his night and day, his presence and his travels, his secret and his public actions, so may God be pleased with them and satisfy them, and then every successor inherited it from their predecessors until our time, so by their light the guided are followed, and on their path the successful walk, so we ask God the Generous, the Giver of Grace to make us among their successors. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numair told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “None of you should belittle himself by seeing something said about God and not saying it, for God says, ‘What is preventing you from saying it?’ He says, ‘O Lord, I feared the people.’ He says, ‘So I am more deserving of being feared.’” It was also narrated by Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numair and Abu Mu’awiyah, both of them on the authority of Al-A’mash, with this chain of transmission. God the Almighty said: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, forbidding anyone to say after this, Zayd ibn Muhammad, meaning he was not his father, even though he had adopted him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not have any male children who lived to reach puberty. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had Al-Qasim, Al-Tayyib, and Al-Tahir from Khadija, may God be pleased with her, but they died young. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had Ibrahim from Mariyah Al-Qibtiyya, but he also died as an infant. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had four daughters from Khadija: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah, may God be pleased with them all. Three died during his lifetime, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Fatimah may God be pleased with her was delayed until she was afflicted by him, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and then she died six months after him. And the Almighty’s saying: But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, and God is Knowing of all things, is like His saying: God knows best where to place His message. This verse is a clear statement that there is no prophet after him, and if there is no prophet after him, then there is no messenger after him, by the foremost and most appropriate way, because the status of messengership is more specific than the status of prophethood, since every messenger is a prophet, but not vice versa. And thus the successive hadiths were reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of a group of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Al-Azdi told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My example among the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, made it beautiful and perfect, but left a space for a brick without putting it in. The people went around the building, amazed by it, and said: If only the place of this brick were completed, then I would be among the prophets in the place of that brick.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Amir Al-Aqdi, with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Mukhtar bin Falfel told us, Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him told us that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The message and prophethood have come to an end, so there is no messenger or prophet after that. The people were upset by that, so he said: But the good tidings. They said: O Messenger of God, what are the good tidings? He said: The dream of a Muslim man, and it is a part of the parts of prophethood. And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za’farani on the authority of Affan bin Muslim, and he said: It is a sahih gharib hadith from Al-Mukhtar bin Falfel. Another hadith Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Salim ibn Hayyan told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Mina’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and the example of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, completing it and making it beautiful except for the space of one brick. Whoever entered it and looked at it would say: ‘How beautiful it is except for the space of this brick.’ So I am the space of that brick, and with me the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, were sealed.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Salim ibn Hayyan, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is authentic but ghareeb from this source. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and that of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house and completed it except for one brick. So I came and completed that brick.” Muslim alone transmitted it from the narration of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Uthman bin Ubaid Al-Rasibi told us: I heard Abu Al-Tayyib, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no prophethood after me except good tidings. It was said: What are good tidings, O Messenger of God? He said: A good dream - or he said - a righteous dream. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him told us, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built houses and completed them, made them beautiful and perfect, except for the space of one brick in one of their corners. The people would go around them and admire the building and say: Why did you not place a brick here so that your building would be completed? The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: So I was that brick.” Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, Imam Muslim said: Yahya bin Ayoub, Qutaybah, and Ali bin Hajar told us, they said: Ismail bin Ja’far told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given six things superior to the prophets: I was given concise speech, I was aided by terror, spoils of war were made lawful for me, the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, I was sent to all of creation, and the prophets were sealed with me.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Ismail bin Ja’far, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built a house and completed it except for the place of one brick. Then I came and completed that brick.” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb, both of them on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, with the same chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told us, Saeed ibn Suwaid al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Hilal al-Salami, on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Indeed, I am the Seal of the Prophets in the sight of God, while Adam was still kneaded in his clay. Another hadith Al-Zuhri said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im told me on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi through whom God Almighty will erase disbelief, I am Al-Hashir at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib after whom there will be no prophet.” They both included it in the two Sahihs. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us one day as if bidding farewell and said: I am Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet - three times - “and there is no prophet after me. I have been given the openings of speech, its conciseness, and its endings, and I have been taught how many are the keepers of Hell and the bearers of the Throne, and I have been granted well-being and my nation has been granted well-being, so listen and obey as long as I am among you. But when I go, then adhere to the Book of God, the Most High, and make lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids.” This is narrated only by Imam Ahmad. And Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hubayrah Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Surayj Al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Qais, the client of Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned something similar, and the hadiths on this are many. It is from the mercy of God Almighty to the servants that He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, then from His honor for them that He sealed the prophets and messengers with him and completed the true religion for him. God Almighty informed in His Book and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the continuous Sunnah from him that there is no prophet after him, so that they may know that everyone who claims this position after him is a liar, a lying, misguided charlatan who leads astray. Even if he were to practice magic and sorcery and come up with various types of magic, talismans and incantations, all of them are impossible and misguidance to those with understanding, just as God Almighty caused corrupt conditions and cold sayings to occur at the hands of Al-Aswad Al-Ansi in Yemen and Musaylimah the Liar in Al-Yamamah, so that every person of understanding, understanding and reason would know that they are liars. They are two astrays, may God curse them, and so is every claimant of this until the Day of Judgment, until they are sealed with the false Messiah. God creates with each one of these liars such things that scholars and believers testify that the one who brought them was a liar. This is from the perfection of God’s kindness to His creation, for they do not necessarily command what is right or forbid what is wrong except by agreement or because they have ulterior motives, etc., and their words and actions are at the height of slander and immorality, as God the Almighty said: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying, sinful person. This is in contrast to the state of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, for they are at the height of righteousness, truthfulness, guidance, uprightness, and justice in what they say, do, command, and forbid, along with what they support with miracles, clear evidence, and dazzling proofs. May God’s prayers and peace be upon them always and forever as long as the earth and heavens remain.

The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not have any male children who lived to reach puberty. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had Al-Qasim, Al-Tayyib, and Al-Tahir from Khadija, may God be pleased with her, but they died young. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had Ibrahim from Mariyah Al-Qibtiyya, but he also died as an infant. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had four daughters from Khadija: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah, may God be pleased with them all. Three died during his lifetime, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Fatimah may God be pleased with her was delayed until she was afflicted by him, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and then she died six months after him. And the Almighty’s saying: But he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, and God is Knowing of all things, is like His saying: God knows best where to place His message. This verse is a clear statement that there is no prophet after him, and if there is no prophet after him, then there is no messenger after him, by the foremost and most appropriate way, because the status of messengership is more specific than the status of prophethood, since every messenger is a prophet, but not vice versa. And thus the successive hadiths were reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of a group of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Amir Al-Azdi told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “My example among the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, made it beautiful and perfect, but left a space for a brick without putting it in. The people went around the building, amazed by it, and said: If only the place of this brick were completed, then I would be among the prophets in the place of that brick.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Amir Al-Aqdi, with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Al-Mukhtar bin Falfel told us, Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him told us that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The message and prophethood have come to an end, so there is no messenger or prophet after that. The people were upset by that, so he said: But the good tidings. They said: O Messenger of God, what are the good tidings? He said: The dream of a Muslim man, and it is a part of the parts of prophethood. And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Za’farani on the authority of Affan bin Muslim, and he said: It is a sahih gharib hadith from Al-Mukhtar bin Falfel. Another hadith Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Salim ibn Hayyan told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Mina’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and the example of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, completing it and making it beautiful except for the space of one brick. Whoever entered it and looked at it would say: ‘How beautiful it is except for the space of this brick.’ So I am the space of that brick, and with me the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, were sealed.” Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Salim ibn Hayyan, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is authentic but ghareeb from this source. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and that of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house and completed it except for one brick. So I came and completed that brick.” Muslim alone transmitted it from the narration of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Uthman bin Ubaid Al-Rasibi told us: I heard Abu Al-Tayyib, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no prophethood after me except good tidings. It was said: What are good tidings, O Messenger of God? He said: A good dream - or he said - a righteous dream. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him told us, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built houses and completed them, made them beautiful and perfect, except for the space of one brick in one of their corners. The people would go around them and admire the building and say: Why did you not place a brick here so that your building would be completed? The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: So I was that brick.” Both of them narrated it from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq. Another hadith On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, Imam Muslim said: Yahya bin Ayoub, Qutaybah, and Ali bin Hajar told us, they said: Ismail bin Ja’far told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given six things superior to the prophets: I was given concise speech, I was aided by terror, spoils of war were made lawful for me, the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, I was sent to all of creation, and the prophets were sealed with me.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Ismail bin Ja’far, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and the example of the prophets before me is like that of a man who built a house and completed it except for the place of one brick. Then I came and completed that brick.” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb, both of them on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, with the same chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told us, Saeed ibn Suwaid al-Kalbi told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Hilal al-Salami, on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Indeed, I am the Seal of the Prophets in the sight of God, while Adam was still kneaded in his clay. Another hadith Al-Zuhri said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im told me on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi through whom God Almighty will erase disbelief, I am Al-Hashir at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib after whom there will be no prophet.” They both included it in the two Sahihs. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us one day as if bidding farewell and said: I am Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet - three times - “and there is no prophet after me. I have been given the openings of speech, its conciseness, and its endings, and I have been taught how many are the keepers of Hell and the bearers of the Throne, and I have been granted well-being and my nation has been granted well-being, so listen and obey as long as I am among you. But when I go, then adhere to the Book of God, the Most High, and make lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids.” This is narrated only by Imam Ahmad. And Imam Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hubayrah Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Surayj Al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Qais, the client of Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned something similar, and the hadiths on this are many. It is from the mercy of God Almighty to the servants that He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, then from His honor for them that He sealed the prophets and messengers with him and completed the true religion for him. God Almighty informed in His Book and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the continuous Sunnah from him that there is no prophet after him, so that they may know that everyone who claims this position after him is a liar, a lying, a deceitful, misguiding charlatan. Even if he burns himself and practices magic and comes with various types of magic, talismans and incantations, all of them are impossible and misguidance to those with understanding, just as God Almighty caused corrupt conditions and cold sayings to occur at the hands of Al-Aswad Al-Ansi in Yemen and Musaylimah the Liar in Al-Yamamah, so that every person of understanding, understanding and reason knows that they are liars. They are two astrays, may God curse them, and so is every claimant of this until the Day of Judgment, until they are sealed with the false Messiah. God creates with each one of these liars such things that scholars and believers testify that the one who brought them was a liar. This is from the perfection of God’s kindness to His creation, for they do not necessarily command what is right or forbid what is wrong except by agreement or because they have ulterior motives, etc., and their words and actions are at the height of slander and immorality, as God the Almighty said: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying, sinful person. This is in contrast to the state of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, for they are at the height of righteousness, truthfulness, guidance, uprightness, and justice in what they say, do, command, and forbid, along with what they support with miracles, clear evidence, and dazzling proofs. May God’s prayers and peace be upon them always and forever as long as the earth and heavens remain.
33:41: God Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to frequently remember their Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, who has bestowed upon them various blessings and types of favors, because of the great reward and beautiful destination they will receive for that. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Saeed, the freedman of Ibn Ayyash narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bahriya, on the authority of Abu Darda’ may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Lord, the highest of them in your degrees, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours.” They said: What is that, O Messenger of God? He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic. This is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abdullah bin Saeed bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ziyad, the freedman of Ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Bahriya, whose name was Abdullah bin Qais Al-Baraghami, on the authority of Abu Darda’ may God be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: Some of them narrated it from him but he sent it without a chain of transmission. I said: This hadith was presented in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, in relation to the words of God Almighty: And men who remember God often, men and women who remember Him, in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, the client of Abdullah ibn Ayyash, that he heard from Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. So God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ narrated to us, Faraj bin Fadala narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Himsi, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: A supplication that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which I will never abandon: O God, make me the greatest in thanking You, following Your advice, remembering You often, and heeding Your advice. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Musa, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Abu Fadala Al-Faraj bin Fadala, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Himsi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar, and he said: It is strange. Imam Ahmad also narrated it in this way, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr Hashim bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Faraj bin Fadala, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Murri, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned it. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Salih on the authority of Amr ibn Qays who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Busr say: “Two Bedouins came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and one of them said: ‘O Messenger of God, who is the best of people?’ He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘He who lives long and does good deeds.’ The other said: ‘O Messenger of God, the laws of Islam have become too many for us, so instruct me to do something that I may hold fast to.’ He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of God Almighty.’” At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated the second chapter of the hadith of Muawiyah ibn Salih with this chain of transmission. At-Tirmidhi said: It is a hasan ghareeb hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, who said: Diraj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Remember God often until they say you are crazy.’” At-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad told us, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Makram al-Ami, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Sufyan al-Juhdari, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Abi Thabib al-Rasibi, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Remember God often until the hypocrites say you are showing off. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed, a client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Shaddad Abu Talha al-Rasibi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Waze’ Jabir ibn Amr narrating on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: There are no people who sit in a gathering in which they do not remember God except that they will see it as a cause of regret on the Day of Resurrection. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both regarding the words of God the Almighty: Remember God with much remembrance, that God the Almighty did not impose an obligation on His servants except that He set a known limit for it, then He excused its people in cases where they had an excuse other than remembrance. God the Almighty did not set a limit for it, and He did not excuse anyone for abandoning it except one who was forced to abandon it. He said: They remember God standing, sitting, and lying on their sides by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, rich and poor, sick and healthy, secretly and openly, and in every situation. God the Almighty said: And glorify Him morning and evening. So if you do that, He and His angels will send blessings upon you. There are many hadiths, verses and traditions that encourage remembering God the Almighty, and this noble verse encourages us to do so often. People have written books on the remembrances of God related to the times of the night and day, such as An-Nasa’i, Al-Ma’mari and others. One of the best books written on this topic is The Book of Remembrances by Sheikh Muhyi Al-Din An-Nawawi may God have mercy on him. God the Almighty said: And glorify Him in the morning and the evening, meaning in the morning and the evening, as He the Almighty said: “So exalt God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. To Him be praise in the heavens and the earth and in the evening and when you reach the noon.” And He the Almighty said: It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels do. This is an encouragement to remember Him, meaning that He the Almighty remembers you, so remember Him, as He the Almighty said: “Just as We have sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know. So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.” And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God the Almighty says: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I will remember him in Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I will remember him in an assembly better than it.” And the blessing from God the Almighty is His praise of the servant before the angels, as narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, and narrated by Abu Ja`far Al-Razi on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas on his authority. And others said: The blessing from God the Almighty is mercy. It may be said: There is no contradiction between the two statements, and God knows best. As for the prayer of the angels, it means supplication for people and seeking forgiveness, as God Almighty says: “Those who bear the Throne and those around it exalt [God] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], ‘Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and to whoever was righteous among their fathers and their spouses and their descendants. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.’ And protect them from evil.” And the Almighty’s saying: That He may bring you out from darkness into the light means, because of His mercy towards you, His praise of you, and the supplication of His angels for you, He brings you out from the darkness of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and certainty. And He is ever Merciful to the believers meaning in this world and the hereafter. As for in this world, He guided them to the truth that others were ignorant of, and He showed them the path that others who called to disbelief or innovation and their followers among the tyrants had strayed from and turned away from. As for His mercy towards them in the hereafter, He secured them from the greatest terror and commanded His angels to meet them with the good report of winning Paradise and being saved from the Fire. This is only because of His love for them and His compassion for them. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Uday narrated to us on the authority of Humayd on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by with a group of his companions may God be pleased with them, and there was a child on the road. When the child’s mother saw the people, she feared that her child would be trampled on, so she ran and said: My son, my son! She ran and caught him. The people said: O Messenger of God, this woman would not throw her son into the Fire. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) calmed them down and said: No, by God, He will not throw His beloved into the Fire. Its chain of transmission meets the criteria of the two Sahihs, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it, but in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw a woman from among the captives who had taken her child, held him close to her chest and breastfed him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you think that this woman would throw her child into the Fire when she is able to do so? They said: No. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By God, God is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child. God the Almighty says: “Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, ‘Peace.’” It appears that what is meant - and God knows best - is their greeting, that is, from God the Almighty on the Day they meet Him, “Peace,” meaning the Day He greets them, as He the Almighty says: “Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.” Qatadah claimed that what is meant is that they will greet one another with peace on the Day they meet God in the Hereafter, and Ibn Jarir preferred this view. I say This can be proven by God’s statement: “Their call therein will be, ‘Glory be to You, O God,’ and their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’ And their final call will be, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” God the Almighty says: And has prepared for them a noble reward, meaning Paradise and what is in it of food, drink, clothing, dwellings, marriages, refuges, and sights, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man.

He (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Al-Tirmidhi said: Some of them narrated it from him but he sent it without a chain of transmission. I said: This hadith was presented in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, in relation to the words of God Almighty: And men who remember God often, men and women who remember Him, in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, the client of Abdullah ibn Ayyash, that he heard from Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. So God knows best. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Musa, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Abu Fadala Al-Faraj bin Fadala, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Himsi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar, and he said: It is strange. Imam Ahmad also narrated it in this way, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr Hashim bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Faraj bin Fadala, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Murri, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned it.
