33:45: Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Falih bin Sulaiman told us, Hilal bin Ali told us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, who said: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, may God be pleased with them both, and I said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur’an: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner and a protection for the illiterate. You are My servant and Messenger, I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. You are not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets. He does not repel evil with evil, but he pardons, forgives, and pardons. God will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion, by which they say, There is no god but God, and thereby he opens blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts. Al-Bukhari narrated it in Al-Buyu’ on the authority of Muhammad bin Sinan on the authority of Falih bin Sulaiman on the authority of Hilal bin Ali on his authority. It was narrated in Tafsir on the authority of Abdullah, it was said Ibn Raja, and it was said Ibn Salih, on the authority of Abdul Aziz Ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Ata’ Ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, with it. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Raja’, on the authority of Abdul Aziz Ibn Abi Salamah Al-Majshun with it. Al-Bukhari said in Al-Buyu’: Saeed said on the authority of Hilal on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, may God be pleased with him, and Wahb bin Munabbih said: God Almighty revealed to a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel, whose name was Isaiah: “Rise among your people, the Children of Israel, for I will speak with your tongue a revelation, and I will send an illiterate person from among the illiterate. I will send him who is neither rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets. If he passes by a lamp, he will not extinguish it due to his tranquility, and if he walks on reeds, he will not hear what is beneath his feet. I will send him as a bringer of good tidings and a warner who will not speak obscenities. I will open through him blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts. I will guide him to every beautiful matter and bestow upon him every noble characteristic. I will make tranquility his clothing, righteousness his slogan, piety his conscience, wisdom his speech, truthfulness and loyalty his nature, forgiveness and goodness his character, truth his law, justice his way of life, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad is his name by which he is guided after misguidance, and I will teach…” Through him, I will raise people after their ignorance, raise them after their insignificance, make them more numerous after their fewness, enrich them after their poverty, unite them after their division, bring together scattered nations, different hearts, and scattered desires, and rescue great groups of people from destruction, and make his nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, monotheistic, faithful, sincere, and believing in what My Messengers brought. I will inspire them with glorification, praise, exaltation, magnification, and monotheism in their mosques, their assemblies, their beds, their resting places, and their resting places. They will pray to Me while singing and sitting, and they will fight in the way of God in ranks and groups. They will go out from their homes seeking My pleasure in thousands, purifying their faces and limbs and tightening their garments in half. Their sacrifices will be their blood, and their Gospels will be in their chests. They will be monks by night and lions by day. I will make among his family and his descendants the forerunners and the truthful. And the martyrs and the righteous, his nation after him, they guide with the truth and with it they act justly. I will honor those who support them and support those who call to them. I will turn the circle of evil on those who oppose them, or transgress against them, or want to snatch anything of what is in their hands. I will make them inheritors of their Prophet, and the callers to their Lord. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, establish prayer, give zakat, and fulfill their covenant. 33:49: This noble verse contains many rulings, including the application of marriage to the contract alone, and there is no verse in the Quran that is more explicit about that than it. They differed about marriage: Is it really in the contract alone, or in intercourse, or in both? There are three opinions. The Quran uses the term in the contract and intercourse after it, except in this verse, as it is used in the contract alone, based on the saying of God the Most High: If you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, and in it is evidence for the permissibility of divorcing a woman before consummating the marriage. God's statement: The believing women is based on the most common view, as there is no difference in the ruling between a believing woman and a woman of the People of the Book in this regard, by consensus. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin, and a group of the early Muslims used this verse as evidence that divorce does not take place unless it is preceded by marriage, because God SWT said: When you marry believing women and then divorce them, so the marriage is followed by divorce, which indicates that it is not valid and does not take place before it. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and a large group of the early Muslims and later Muslims may God have mercy on them. Malik and Abu Hanifah may God have mercy on them held that divorce before marriage is valid if a person says: If I marry so-and-so, she is divorced. According to them, whenever he marries her, she is divorced from him. They differed regarding the case in which a person says: Every woman I marry is divorced. Malik said: She is not divorced until he specifies the woman. Abu Hanifah may God have mercy on him said: Every woman he marries after this statement is divorced from him. As for the majority, they cited this verse as evidence that divorce does not take place. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi told us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl told us, Yunus, meaning Ibn Abi Ishaq, told us: I heard Adam, the client of Khalid, from Saeed ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: If he says: Every woman I marry is divorced, he said: It is nothing, because God Almighty says: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them (al-Baqarah 2:170). Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, from Matar, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanaq, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God Almighty said: When you marry believing women and then divorce them (al-Baqarah 2:170). Don’t you see that the divorce comes after the marriage? Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God Almighty said: When you marry believing women and then divorce them (al-Baqarah 2:170). So there is no divorce before the marriage. This hadith was narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no divorce for the son of Adam regarding that which he does not possess. Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith, and it is the best hadith narrated on this topic. Ibn Majah also narrated it on the authority of Ali and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no divorce before marriage. God the Almighty said: And you have no waiting period to count for them. This is a matter agreed upon by scholars, that if a woman is divorced before consummation of the marriage, there is no waiting period for her, so she may go and marry whomever she wants immediately. The only exception to this is the woman whose husband has died, as she must observe a waiting period of four months and ten days, even if he has not consummated the marriage with her, according to consensus. God the Almighty said: Then give them a provision and release them with gracious release. The provision here is more general than it being half the specified dowry or a specific provision if none has been specified for her. God the Almighty said: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and have already specified for them a dowry, then give them half of what you specified. And He the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dowry. But give them a provision, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d and Abu Usayd may God be pleased with them they said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) married Umaymah bint Shuraheel, and when she entered upon him (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he extended his hand to her, and it was as if she disliked that, so he ordered Abu Usayd to prepare her and clothe her in two Raziq garments. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them that if he specified a dowry for her, then she is only entitled to half, and if he did not specify a dowry, then he should give her a provision according to his ease and difficulty, and this is the beautiful release.
33:50: God the Almighty says, addressing His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that He has made lawful for him from among the women his wives to whom he has given their dowries, which are wages here, as stated by Mujahid and others. His dowry for his wives was twelve ounces and a nash, which is half an ounce, so the total was five hundred dirhams, except for Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, for the Negus may God have mercy on him gave her a dowry of four hundred dinars on his behalf. Except for Safiyyah bint Huyayy, for he chose her from the captives of Khaybar, then freed her and made her freedom her dowry. Similarly, Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyah, for whom he paid her a freed slave contract to Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, and he married her - may God be pleased with them all. And the Almighty said: And what your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you meaning He permitted you to take concubines from what you took from the spoils. He took possession of Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, so he freed them and married them, and he took possession of Rayhana bint Sham’un al-Nadriyyah and Maria al-Qibtiyyah, the mother of his son Ibrahim, peace be upon them, and they were among the concubines, may God be pleased with them. And the Almighty’s saying: And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts the verse, this is a middle ground between excess and neglect, as the Christians do not marry a woman unless there are seven grandfathers or more between them, and the Jews marry one of them the daughter of his brother and the daughter of his sister. So this complete and pure Sharia came to demolish the excess of the Christians, so it permitted the daughter of the paternal uncle and the aunt, and the daughter of the maternal uncle and the aunt, and prohibited what the Jews neglected in permitting the daughter of the brother and the sister, and this is heinous and terrible. Rather, He said: And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, so He used the male form singular for its honor and used the female form plural for their deficiency, as He said: on the right and the left, “He brings them out from darkness into the light,” and And He made darkness and light. And there are many similar examples. God the Almighty said: Those who emigrated with you. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn al-Harith al-Razi narrated to us, Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Umm Hani’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed marriage to me, and I apologized to him, but he excused me. Then God the Almighty revealed: “Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation, and those your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles, and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you.” She said: I was not lawful to him, and I was not among those who emigrated with him. I was among those who were freed. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, with this chain of transmission. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, on her authority, in a similar manner. At-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Jami’. Abu Razin and Qatadah said the same, and what is meant is those who emigrated with him to Madinah. In a narration on the authority of Qatada, those who migrated with you means those who converted to Islam. Al-Dahhak said: Ibn Masoud read those who migrated with you. And the Almighty’s saying: And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet if the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you (al-Baqarah 2:170), meaning, it is lawful for you, O Prophet, to marry a believing woman if she offers herself to you without a dowry if you wish. This verse contains two conditions, like the Almighty’s saying, informing us about Noah, peace be upon him, that he said to his al-Nas 114:And my advice will not benefit you, if I intend to advise you, if God intends to mislead you (al-Baqarah 2:170) and the saying of Moses, peace be upon him: O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely on Him, if you should be Muslims (al-Baqarah 2:170). And He said here: And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet (al-Baqarah 2:170). Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi, “A woman came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have given myself to you.’ She stood for a long time, and a man stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, marry her to me if you have no need for her.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do you have anything as a dowry for her?’ He said: ‘I have nothing but this lower garment of mine.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘If you give her your lower garment, you will have no lower garment.’ He looked for something, but he said: ‘I cannot find anything.’ He said: ‘Look for even an iron ring.’ He looked but did not find anything, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘Do you know anything of the Qur’an?’ He said: ‘Yes, Surah such and such and Surah such and such’ - he named the surahs. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘I marry her to you for what you know of the Qur’an.’” Both of them narrated from the hadith of Malik. Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Marhum narrated to us, I heard Thabit say: I was sitting with Anas and his daughter was with him, so Anas said: A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Prophet of God, do you have a need? His daughter said: How little modesty she had. He said: She is better than you. She desired the Prophet and offered herself to him. Al-Bukhari alone narrated it from the hadith of Marhum ibn Abd al-Aziz from Thabit al-Bunani from Anas. Ahmad also said: Abdullah ibn Bakir narrated to us, Sinan ibn Rabi’ah from al-Hadrami from Anas ibn Malik, “A woman came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, I have such and such a daughter, and I mentioned her beauty and loveliness, so I preferred her to you. He said: I have kissed her. She continued praising her until she remembered that she never had a headache or any complaint at all. He said: I have no need of your daughter.” They did not narrate it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim told us, Ibn Abi al-Wadah, meaning Muhammad ibn Muslim, told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The one who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Khawlah bint Hakim. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman and Ibn Abi al-Zinad, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father: Khawlah bint Hakim ibn al-Awqas from Banu Sulaym was among those who offered themselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In a narration of his, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father: We used to say that Khawlah bint Hakim offered herself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was a righteous woman. So it is possible that Umm Sulaym was Khawlah bint Hakim or she was another woman. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Wakee’ told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Umar ibn al-Hakam, and Abdullah ibn Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married thirteen women, six from the Quraysh 106:Khadija, Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba, Sawda, and Umm Salama; three from Banu Amir ibn Sa’sa’a; two from Banu Hilal ibn Amir: Maymunah bint al-Harith, who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace; Zaynab, the mother of the poor; a woman from Banu Bakr ibn Kilab from the Qurashiyyat, who chose the world; a woman from Banu al-Jun, who sought refuge from him; Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah; and the two captives: Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith ibn Amr ibn al-Mustaliq al-Khuza’iyya. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet, he said: She is Maymunah bint al-Harith. There is an interruption in the chain of transmission, this is mursal. The well-known view is that Zaynab, who was called Umm al-Masakin, is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Ansariyyah, and she died while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was alive. And God knows best. The point of this is that those who offered themselves to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were many, as al-Bukhari said: Zakariya bin Yahya told us, Abu Usamah told us, he said: Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: I used to be jealous of those who offered themselves to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I would say: Does a woman offer herself? Then when God revealed the verse: “You may defer to God whom you will of them, and you may take to yourself whom you will. And from those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you,” I said: I do not think that your Lord will except hasten to fulfil your desires. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Mansour Al-Ja’fi told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Anbasa bin Al-Azhar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not have a woman who offered herself to him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir, meaning that he did not accept a single woman who offered herself to him, even though that was permissible for him and specific to him, because it was up to his will, as God the Most High said: If the Prophet wishes to marry her, meaning if he chooses that. And the Almighty’s saying: Purely for you, not for the believers. Ikrimah said: This means that the gifted woman is not permissible for anyone else. If a woman gives herself to a man, she is not permissible for him until he gives her something. This is what Mujahid, Ash-Sha’bi and others said. This means that if a woman gives herself to a man, then when he consummates the marriage with her, he is obligated to give her a dowry similar to that of her peers, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ruled in the case of Baru’ bint Washiq when she was given the gift. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ruled that she be given a dowry similar to that of her peers when her husband died. Death and consummation are the same in determining the dowry and establishing the dowry similar to that of the woman who is given the gift to someone other than the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). As for him (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he is not obligated to give the woman she is given the gift to, even if he consummated the marriage with her, because he has the right to marry without a dowry, guardian, or witnesses, as in the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh may God be pleased with her. For this reason, Qatadah said regarding His saying: Purely for you, not for the believers, that he means that no woman gives herself to a man without a guardian or dowry except to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). And the Almighty said: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess. Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jarir said regarding His statement: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives meaning limiting them to four free women, and whatever they wish of female slaves, and stipulating a guardian, dowry, and witnesses over them, and they are the female slaves. We have given you permission to do that, so we have not obligated you to do anything of it “so that there will be no hardship upon you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
33:51: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that she was jealous of the women who had offered themselves to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: Isn't a woman ashamed to offer herself without a dowry? Then God the Almighty revealed: You may postpone whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish 2:17. She said: I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill your desires. It was previously narrated by Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Abu Usamah on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah. This indicates that what is meant by his saying: You may postpone is to delay whoever you wish of them meaning of the donors and take to yourself whomever you wish meaning of the donors "you may accept whomever you wish and reject whomever you wish, and whomever you reject, you also have the choice regarding her after that if you wish to go back to her and take her in. For this reason, He said: "And if you desire among those whom you have set aside, there is no blame upon you." Aamer Al-Shaabi said about the verse: You may postpone any of them you wish verse, they were women who had offered themselves to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he had intercourse with some of them and postponed others, and they did not marry again after that, including Umm Sharik. Others said: Rather, what is meant by His saying: You may postpone any of them you wish verse, is the verse, meaning from among your wives there is no blame on you for not dividing your time with them, so you may bring forward whomever you wish and delay whomever you wish, and have intercourse with whomever you wish and leave whomever you wish. This is how it is narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Razin, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and others. Despite this, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would divide his time with them, and for this reason a group of jurists from the Shafi’i school and others went to the view that dividing time was not obligatory upon him (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they used this noble verse as evidence. Al-Bukhari said: Habban bin Musa told us, Abdullah - he is Ibn Al-Mubarak - told us, and Asim Al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Muadh, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to ask permission from any woman among us every day after this verse was revealed: “You may defer whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish. And if you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you.” So I said to her: What did you say? She said: I used to say, If that is up to me, then I do not want, O Messenger of God, to give preference to anyone over you. This hadith about her indicates that what is meant by that is the absence of division. Her first hadith requires that the verse was revealed about the donors. From here, Ibn Jarir chose that the verse is general regarding the donors and women, who, according to him, he has the choice regarding them: if he wishes, he may divide or if he wishes, he may not divide. This which he chose is good, good, and strong, and in it he reconciles the hadiths. For this reason, God the Almighty said: That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted and they will not grieve and will be satisfied with what You have given them all. That is, if they know that God has removed from you the difficulty in dividing, then if you wish, you may divide, and if you wish, you may not divide. There is no blame on you for whichever of these you do. Then, with this, you divide for them by choice from you, not that it is obligatory. They rejoiced at that and were pleased with it, and they took your kindness in that, and they acknowledged your favor upon them in dividing for them and your equality between them and your fairness to them and your justice with them. God the Almighty said: And God knows what is in your hearts meaning the inclination towards some of them over others, which cannot be warded off, as Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to divide his time equally among his wives, then he would say: ‘O God, this is my action in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not.’” It was narrated by the four scholars of Sunan on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, and Abu Dawud added after his statement: So do not blame me for what You control and I do not, meaning the heart. Its chain of transmission is saheeh, and all of its men are trustworthy. That is why God followed that with His statement: And God is All-Knowing, meaning of the secrets of the hearts, Forbearing, meaning He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
33:52: More than one scholar, such as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, Ibn Jarir, and others, mentioned that this verse was revealed as a reward for the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as a sign of his approval of them for their good deeds in choosing God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them the choice, as mentioned in the verse. When they chose the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, their reward was that God Almighty restricted him to them, and forbade him from marrying anyone other than them or replacing them with other husbands, even if he liked their beauty, except for female slaves and concubines, in which case there is no blame on him. Then God Almighty lifted the blame from him for that and abrogated the ruling of this verse, and permitted him to marry, but he did not marry after that so that the favor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be upon them. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not die until God made women lawful for him. He also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, on the authority of Aisha. At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa’i narrated it in their Sunans. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abdur-Rahman ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Shaybah told us, Umar ibn Abi Bakr told me, Al-Mughirah ibn Abdur-Rahman Al-Khuza’i told me, on the authority of Abu An-Nadr, the freed slave of Umar ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb ibn Zam’ah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not die until God made it lawful for him to marry as many women as he wished, except for a mahram. This is the statement of God, the Most High: You may defer from them whomever you wish (al-Baqarah 2:174). This abrogates the next in recitation, just as the two verses about the waiting period for death in Surah Al-Baqarah abrogate the next. And God knows best. Others said: Rather, the meaning of the verse It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that is after what we have mentioned to you of the description of the women whom We have made lawful for you from your wives, those to whom you have given their due compensation, those whom your right hand possesses, the daughters of paternal uncles and aunts, the maternal uncles and aunts, the female aunts who give as a gift, and other types of women are not lawful for you. This is what was narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Mujahid in one narration from him, and Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak in one narration, and Abu Razin in one narration from him, and Abu Salih, Al-Hasan and Qatadah in one narration, and As-Suddi and others. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, Muhammad ibn Abi Musa told me, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Tell me, if the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died, would he not have the right to marry? He said: What prevents him from doing that? He said: I said, God’s statement, ‘It is not lawful for you to take other women after that.’ He said: God only made lawful for him a type of women, as God, the Most High, said: “O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation and those your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet.” Then it was said to him, It is not lawful for you to take other women after that. Abdullah bin Ahmad narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Dawud. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade all kinds of women except those who were believing emigrants, as God Almighty said: It is not lawful for you to take other women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses. So God made permissible your believing girls and a believing woman if she offered herself to the Prophet, and He forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam. Then He said: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless. God the Almighty said: “O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries, and those your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you [as booty] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet - if the Prophet wishes to marry her - exclusively for you, not including the believers.” And He forbade all other types of women. Mujahid said, It is not lawful for you to marry women after that, meaning after what has been named for you of Muslim, Jewish, Christian, or infidel women. Abu Salih said, It is not lawful for you to marry women after that, meaning that a man is commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman, male or female, and to marry after that from the women of Tihamah and whatever he wishes of the daughters of his paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles, and maternal aunts, if he wishes, up to three hundred. Ikrimah said, It is not lawful for you to marry women after that, meaning those whom God has named. Ibn Jarir may God have mercy on him said: The verse is general and includes all the women mentioned, including the nine women he married. What he said is good, and perhaps what was meant by many of the salaf we have narrated from them, as many of them narrated this and that from him, and there is no contradiction, and God knows best. Then Ibn Jarir brought up against himself what was narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) divorced Hafsah and then took her back! He resolved to separate from Sawda until she gave her day to Aisha. Then he replied that this was before the revelation of the verse: It is not lawful for you to take other women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives (al-Baqarah 2:17). What he said about this being before the revelation of the verse is correct, but there is no need for that, because the verse only indicates that he will not marry anyone other than those under his protection and that he will not replace them with anyone else. It does not indicate that he will not divorce one of them without replacing them, and God knows best. As for the case of Sawda, it is in the Sahih on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and it is the reason for the revelation of the verse: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves (al-Baqarah 2:17). As for the case of Hafsah, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban narrated in his Sahih, through various chains of narration on the authority of Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayyi, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of ‘Umar, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsah and then took her back. This is a strong chain of narration. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: ‘Umar entered upon Hafsah while she was crying. He said: What makes you cry? Perhaps the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced you. He divorced you once and then took you back because of me. By God, if he divorces you a second time, I will never speak to you again.’ The men of the narration meet the criteria of the two Sahihs. And the Almighty said: Nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you. So He forbade him from increasing them if he divorced one of them, and replacing her with another, except for what his right hand possesses. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated a suitable hadith that he mentioned here, and he said: Ibrahim bin Nasr told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Abd al-Salam bin Harb told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah al-Qurashi, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The exchange in the pre-Islamic era was for a man to say to another man: Exchange your wife for me, and I will exchange my wife for you, meaning you give up your wife for me and I will give up my wife for you. So God revealed: Nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you. He said: “So Uyaynah bin Hisn al-Fazari entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Aisha was with him, so he entered without permission, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Where is the permission? He said: O Messenger of God, I have not asked permission to enter upon a man from Mudar since I became an adult.” Then he said: Who is this red-skinned woman next to you? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is Aisha, the Mother of the Believers. He said: Shall I not give you the best of creation? He said: O Uyaynah, God has forbidden that. When he left, Aisha said: Who is this? He said: This is an obeyed fool, and as you see, he is the master of his people. Then Al-Bazzar said: Ishaq ibn Abdullah is very weak in hadith, and we only mentioned him because we did not memorize him except from this source and we explained the defect in it.
33:53: This is the verse on hijab, and it contains legal rulings and etiquette. Among the things that were revealed in accordance with the words of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, as was proven in the two Sahihs on his authority that he said: I agreed with my Lord, the Almighty, in three matters. I said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer? So God, the Almighty, revealed: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. I said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives, so why don’t you veil them? So God, the Almighty, revealed the verse on hijab. I said to marry the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when they conspired against him out of jealousy: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. So it was revealed likewise. In a narration by Muslim, the prisoners of Badr were mentioned, and it is a fourth matter. Al-Bukhari said: Musaddad narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so why don’t you order the Mothers of the Believers to wear the hijab? So God revealed the verse of the hijab, and the time of its revelation was on the morning of the wedding of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, whose marriage God Himself had undertaken. That was in Dhul-Qi’dah of the fifth year, according to Qatada, al-Waqidi, and others. Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna and Khalifah ibn Khayyat claimed that it was in the third year, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi narrated to us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, I heard my father, Abu Majlaz narrated to us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people and they ate, then they sat talking. He was getting ready to stand up, but they did not stand up. When he saw that, he stood up. When he stood up, those who stood stood up and three people sat down. Then the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came to enter, and the people were sitting. Then they stood up and left. I came and told the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that they had left, so he came and entered. I went to enter, but he threw a veil between me and him. Then God the Most High revealed: “O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, without awaiting its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter, and when you have eaten, disperse.” This has also been narrated in another place, and Muslim and al-Nasa’i have chains of transmission on the authority of Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman with it. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it alone from the hadith of Ayoub on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, in a similar manner. Then he said: Abu Muammar told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Abdul-Aziz bin Suhaib told us on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought Zainab bint Jahsh bread and meat, and sent someone to bring the food. Some people would come, eat, and leave, then some people would come, eat, and leave. I called until I could not find anyone to invite. I said: O Messenger of God, I cannot find anyone to invite. He said: Take away your food. Three men remained talking in the house, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and went to the room of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and said: Peace be upon you, people of the house, and the mercy and blessings of God. She said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God. How did you find your family, O Messenger of God? May God bless you. So he went to the room of all his wives, saying to them what he said to Aisha, and they said to him what Aisha said, then…” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned and found three men in the house talking. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was very shy, so he went out towards Aisha’s room. I do not know whether I told him or he was told that the people had left. He returned and when he had put one foot inside the door and the other outside, he lowered the curtain between me and him and revealed the verse of hijab. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it from among the authors of the six books of hadith, except for al-Nasa’i, in Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah from the hadith of Abd al-Warith. Then he narrated it from Ishaq, who is Ibn Mansur, from Abdullah Ibn Bakr al-Sahmi, from Humayd, from Anas, in a similar manner. Two men said: He is the only one who narrated it from this source. It was mentioned before in the individuals of Muslim from the hadith of Sulayman Ibn al-Mughira, from Thabit, from Anas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Muzaffar told us, Ja`far ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of al-Ja`d Abu Uthman al-Yashkuri, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married one of his wives. Umm Sulaym made a hais a stew and put it in a bowl. She said: ‘Take this to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and convey my greetings to him and tell him that this is a small favor from us for him.’ Anas said: ‘The people were in difficulty at that time, so I brought it and said: ‘O Messenger of God, Umm Sulaym sent this to you, and she conveys my greetings to you and says: Tell him that this is a small favor from us for him.’ He looked at it and said: ‘Put it on.’ So I put it in a corner of the house. Then he said: ‘Go and invite for me so-and-so and so-and-so.’ He named many men and said: ‘And whoever you meet from the Muslims.’ So I invited whoever I met from the Muslims. I came and the house, the porch, and the room were full of people. I said: ‘O Abu Uthman, how many were there?’ He said: ‘They were about three hundred.’ Anas said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought it to me, so I brought it to him. He placed his hand on it and supplicated, saying: “Whatever God wills.” Then he said: Let ten by ten sit in a circle, and say Bismillah, and let each person eat from what is closest to him. So they began to say Bismillah and eat until they had all eaten, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Lift it up. So I came and took the bowl and looked at it. I do not know whether it was more when I put it down or when I took it up? He said: Some men stayed behind talking in the house of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the wife of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), with whom he had entered, was with them, turning her face to the wall. They talked for a long time, and this made it difficult for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he was the shyest of people. If they had known, it would have been difficult for them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up and went out and greeted his lap and his wives. When they saw him come, they thought that they had burdened him, so they rushed to the door and went out. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and lowered the curtain and entered the house, and I was in the room. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stayed in his house for a while, and God revealed the Qur’an to him. He came out reciting this verse: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet [al-Ansari]. Anas said: He recited them to me before the people, and I am the most recent of people to have heard them. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i all narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Ja’far ibn Sulayman. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. Al-Bukhari included it in the Book of Marriage, and he said: Ibrahim said: Ibn Tahman, on the authority of al-Ja`d Abi Uthman, on the authority of Anas, and he mentioned something similar. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rafi`, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of al-Ja`d, with this chain of narration. This hadith was also narrated by Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Bayan ibn Bishr, on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of narration. Al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through two other chains of narration on the authority of Bayan ibn Bishr al-Ahmasi al-Kufi, on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of narration. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Nadrah al-`Abdi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, with a similar chain of narration, but they did not include it in their collections. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of `Amr ibn Sa`id and from the hadith of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas, with a similar chain of narration. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz and Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated to us: Sulayman bin Al-Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: When Zaynab’s waiting period was over, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Zayd: Go and mention her to me. So Zayd went until he came to her while she was kneading her dough. When I saw her, I felt great in my heart. He mentioned the rest of the hadith as we presented it in the statement of God the Almighty: And when Zayd had no longer any need of her, and he added at the end of it after His statement: And he admonished the people with what they had been admonished with. Hashim said in his hadith: Do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission, and the verse. Muslim and An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman bin Al-Mughira. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, told me, my uncle Abdullah bin Wahb told me, Yunus told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out at night when they wanted to defecate to the open plains - which were hot ground - and Umar would say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Veil your women, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not do so. So Sawdah bint Zam’ah, the wife of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, and she was a tall woman, and Umar called to her in his loudest voice: We know you, O Sawdah, out of eagerness for the veil to be revealed. She said: So God revealed the veil. This is how it appears in this narration, and it is well known that this was after the veil was revealed. As narrated by Imam Ahmad, Al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “Sawda went out after the veil was imposed for her needs. She was a large woman, not hidden from those who knew her. Umar bin Al-Khattab saw her and said: O Sawda, by God, you are not hidden from us, so watch how you go out.” She said: “So I turned back and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in my house, and he was eating dinner and in his hand was a vessel. She entered and said: O Messenger of God, I went out for some of my needs, and Umar said to me: Such and such.” She said: “So God revealed to him, then lifted him from it, and the vessel was still in his hand, and he said: ‘You have been given permission to go out for your needs.’” The wording of Al-Bukhari. So God’s statement: Do not enter the houses of the Prophet prohibits the believers from entering the homes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, without permission, as they used to do before that in their homes during the pre-Islamic period and the beginning of Islam, until God was jealous for this nation and commanded them to do so. This is from His honoring this nation, and for this reason the Messenger of God said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Beware of entering upon women, the hadith. Then he made an exception from that, saying: Unless permission is given to you for a meal, without waiting for its preparation. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: That is, without waiting for it to be cooked. That is, do not wait for the food to be cooked until it is almost cooked before you enter, because this is something that God hates and condemns. This is evidence of the prohibition of parasitism, which is what the Arabs call daifun. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi wrote a book on this subject, condemning parasites, and he mentioned things about them that would take too long to cite. Then God the Almighty said: “But when you are invited, enter. And when you have eaten, disperse.” And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If one of you invites his brother, let him accept, whether it is a wedding or something else.’” Its origin is in the two Sahihs, and in Sahih also: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If I were invited to a forearm, I would accept, and if a leg were offered as a gift, I would accept. So when you have finished what you were invited to, make things easy for the people of the house and disperse throughout the land.” And for this reason God the Almighty said: nor seeking entertainment for conversation, meaning as happened to those three people who were carried away by the conversation, and they forgot themselves until it was difficult for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, that used to annoy the Prophet, and he would be shy of you. And it was said that what is meant is that your entering his house without his permission was difficult for him and he would be annoyed by it, but he hated to forbid them from that due to the intensity of his shyness, peace be upon him, until God revealed to him the prohibition against that. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And God is not shy of the truth, meaning that is why He forbade you from that. And he warned you against it. Then God the Almighty said: {And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition} meaning, just as I have forbidden you from entering upon them, do not look at them at all. And if one of you needs something from them, he should not look at them or ask them for anything except from behind a partition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I was eating with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, hais in a bowl. Umar passed by and he called him to eat, and his finger touched my finger. He said, ‘Good! Oh! If he had obeyed concerning you, no eye would have seen you!’ So the verse about the hijab was revealed: ‘That is purer for your hearts and their hearts’ meaning, what I have commanded you to do and prescribed for you regarding the hijab is purer and better.” And the Almighty said: “And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, he said: It was revealed about a man who intended to marry one of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after him. A man said to Sufyan: Is it Aisha? He said: They have mentioned that, and so did Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. He mentioned on the authority of al-Suddi that the one who decided to do that was Talhah ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, until the warning was revealed about the prohibition of that. For this reason, all scholars agreed that if a wife of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) dies and leaves behind him, it is forbidden for anyone else to marry her after him, because they are his wives in this world and the hereafter and the mothers of the believers, as mentioned above. They differed regarding a woman who had intercourse with him and then divorced him during his lifetime: Is it permissible for anyone else to marry her? There are two opinions based on whether she is included in the generality of his statement after him or not. As for one who married her and then divorced her before consummating the marriage, we do not know of any dispute about her being permissible for anyone else in this case, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamir, that the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, died and Qaylah bint al-Ash’ath - meaning Ibn Qays - had become his wife. After that, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her. This was very difficult for Abu Bakr, so Umar said to him: O Caliph of the Messenger of God, she is not one of his wives. The Messenger of God did not give her a choice or conceal her, and God has cleared her of him by apostasy with her people. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was reassured and calmed down. God, the Blessed and Exalted, greatly magnified this and emphasized it and threatened with it by saying: Indeed, that is in the sight of God a great thing. Then His, the Most High, saying: Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed, God is ever, of all things, Knowing. That is, whatever your hearts conceal and what your secrets conceal, God knows it, for nothing is hidden from Him. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.

I said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon your wives, so why don’t you veil them? So God, the Almighty, revealed the verse on hijab. I said to marry the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when they conspired against him out of jealousy: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. And it was said that what is meant is that your entering his house without his permission was difficult for him and he would be annoyed by it, but he hated to forbid them from that due to the intensity of his shyness, peace be upon him, until God revealed to him the prohibition against that. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And God is not shy of the truth, meaning that is why He forbade you from that. And he warned you against it. Then God the Almighty said: {And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition} meaning, just as I have forbidden you from entering upon them, do not look at them at all. And if one of you needs something from them, he should not look at them or ask them for anything except from behind a partition. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I was eating with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, hais in a bowl. Umar passed by and he called him to eat, and his finger touched my finger. He said, ‘Good! Oh! If he had obeyed concerning you, no eye would have seen you!’ So the verse about the hijab was revealed: ‘That is purer for your hearts and their hearts’ meaning, what I have commanded you to do and prescribed for you regarding the hijab is purer and better.” And the Almighty said: “And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God an enormity.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, he said: It was revealed about a man who intended to marry one of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after him. A man said to Sufyan: Is it Aisha? He said: They have mentioned that, and so did Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. He mentioned on the authority of al-Suddi that the one who decided to do that was Talhah ibn Ubaydullah may God be pleased with him, until the warning was revealed about the prohibition of that. For this reason, all scholars agreed that if a wife of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) dies and leaves behind him, it is forbidden for anyone else to marry her after him, because they are his wives in this world and the hereafter and the mothers of the believers, as mentioned above. They differed regarding a woman who had intercourse with him and then divorced him during his lifetime: Is it permissible for anyone else to marry her? There are two opinions based on whether she is included in the generality of his statement after him or not. As for one who married her and then divorced her before consummating the marriage, we do not know of any dispute about her being permissible for anyone else in this case, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamir, that the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, died and Qaylah bint al-Ash’ath - meaning Ibn Qays - had become his wife. After that, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl married her. This was very difficult for Abu Bakr, so Umar said to him: O Caliph of the Messenger of God, she is not one of his wives. The Messenger of God did not give her a choice or conceal her, and God has cleared her of him by apostasy with her people. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was reassured and calmed down. God, the Blessed and Exalted, greatly magnified this and emphasized it and threatened with it by saying: Indeed, that is in the sight of God a great thing. Then His, the Most High, saying: Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed, God is ever, of all things, Knowing. That is, whatever your hearts conceal and what your secrets conceal, God knows it, for nothing is hidden from Him. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
33:55: When God Almighty commanded women to veil themselves from strangers, He made it clear that they should not be veiled from these relatives, as He made an exception for them in Surat An-Nur when He Almighty said: “And not to reveal their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husbands’ fathers, or their sons, or their husbands’ sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or those their right hands possess, or male attendants who have no desire, or children who have no knowledge of the private parts of women.” There are additions to this, and their explanation and discussion have already been presented, so there is no need to repeat it here. Some of the Salaf asked: Why are the paternal uncle and maternal uncle not mentioned in these two verses? Ikrimah and Ash-Sha'bi replied that they were not mentioned because they might describe that to their sons. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj ibn Munhal told us, Hammad told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ash-Sha'bi and Ikrimah, regarding the verse: There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers 2:17. I said: Why are the paternal uncle and maternal uncle not mentioned? He said: Because they describe them to their sons and it is disliked for her to remove her veil in front of her maternal uncle and paternal uncle. The verse: nor their women means not covering herself in front of believing women. The verse: nor those their right hands possess means their male and female slaves, as was previously pointed out and the hadith related in this regard was cited. Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab said: It only refers to female slaves. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God Almighty says: “And fear God. Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a Witness.” That is, fear Him in private and in public, for He is a Witness over all things. Nothing is hidden from Him, so be watchful of the Watcher.
33:56: Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The prayer of God Almighty is His praise of him before the angels, and the prayer of the angels is supplication. Ibn Abbas said: They pray and bless. This is how Al-Bukhari connected it to both of them. Abu Ja`far Al-Razi narrated it on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah in the same way, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi` as well. `Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas as he said, both of them are the same. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them both. Abu `Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri and more than one of the people of knowledge. They said: The prayer of the Lord is mercy, and the prayer of the angels is seeking forgiveness. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr Al-Awdi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah. Al-A’mash said, I think it was on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah: Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. He said: His blessings, Blessed and Exalted be He, are glorious and holy. My mercy has preceded My wrath. The intended meaning of this verse is that God, the Most High, the Most Great, informed His servants of the status of His servant and prophet with Him in the highest assembly, that he is praised by the angels brought near, and that the angels send blessings on him. Then God, the Most High, commanded the people of the lower world to send blessings on him and salute him, so that praise of him would come together from the people of both worlds: the upper and the lower. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash'ath bin Ishaq, on the authority of Ja'far, meaning Ibn Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa'id bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Children of Israel said to Moses, peace be upon him: Does your Lord pray? So his Lord, the Almighty, called to him: O Moses, they asked you, does your Lord pray? Say: Yes, I, and My angels, pray for My prophets and messengers. Then God, the Almighty, revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation.” God the Almighty has informed us that He sends blessings upon His believing servants, as He says: “O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance. And exalt Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, and so do His angels.” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] And He also says: And give good tidings to the patient, Who, when disaster strikes them, say, “Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return. Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord.” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] And in the hadith: Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon those on the right side of the rows. And in another hadith: O God, send blessings upon the family of Abu Awfa. And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to the wife of Jabir when she asked him to send blessings upon her and her husband: May God send blessings upon you and your husband. There are many hadiths from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) commanding us to send blessings upon him and how to send blessings upon him. We will mention from them, God willing, what is easy, and God is the source of help. Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Sa`id ibn Yahya ibn Sa`id narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Mis`ar, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ka`b ibn `Ujrah, who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, ‘As for peace upon you, we know it, but how is the prayer?’ He said: ‘Say, “O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Laila say: Ka`b ibn `Ujrah met me and said: Shall I not give you a gift? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us and we said: O Messenger of God, we know how to greet you, but how do we pray? He said: Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham, You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Abraham, You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. This hadith has been narrated by the group in their books through various chains of narration on the authority of al-Hakam, who is Ibn `Utaybah. Al-Bukhari and `Abdullah ibn `Isa both added it on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, so he mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arfa told us, Hisham bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Ka’b bin Ujrah, who said: When the verse, “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation,” was revealed, we said, “O Messenger of God, we have learned how to say ‘peace be upon you’, but how should we send blessings upon you?” He said, “Say: ‘O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” Abdur-Rahman bin Abi Laila used to say, And upon us with them. At-Tirmidhi narrated it with this addition. The meaning of their saying, “As for ‘peace be upon you’, we have learned it,” is the one in the tashahhud, which he used to teach them just as he used to teach them a surah from the Qur’an, and in it is, “Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy and blessings of God.” Another Hadith Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Haad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khabab, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri may God be pleased with him, who said: We said, O Messenger of God, this is the greeting, so how should we send blessings upon you? He said, “Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham.” Abu Salih said, on the authority of Al-Layth: On Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham. Ibrahim bin Hamza told us, Ibn Abi Hazim and Al-Dawwardi told us, on the authority of Yazid, meaning Ibn Al-Haad, who said: As You sent blessings upon Abraham, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and the family of Abraham. An-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah included it on the authority of Ibn Al-Haad with this chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: I read on the authority of Abd al-Rahman Malik, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Salim, that he said: Abu Hamid al-Sa’idi informed me that they said: O Messenger of God, how do we send blessings upon you? He said: Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon Abraham, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring as You blessed the family of Abraham, for You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.) The rest of the group, except for al-Tirmidhi, transmitted it from the hadith of Malik with it. Another hadith Muslim said: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi told us: I read to Malik from Nuaym ibn Abdullah al-Mujmir, who told me: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari told me: Abdullah ibn Zayd was the one who saw the call to prayer. He told him from Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us while we were in the assembly of Sa`d ibn `Ubadah. Bashir ibn Sa`d said to him: God has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of God, so how should we send blessings upon you? The Messenger of God remained silent until we wished he had not asked him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed the family of Abraham in the worlds. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. And peace, as you have known. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa`i, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from a hadith of Malik with this chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zayy ibn Abd Rabbih, on the authority of Abu Mas’ud Al-Badri that they said: O Messenger of God, we have known the greeting of peace, but how should we send blessings upon you when we pray in our prayers? “He said: Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad.” He mentioned it and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Abu Hurayrah in a similar manner. From here, Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, went to the view that it is obligatory for the one praying to send blessings upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the final testimony of faith. If he leaves it out, his prayer is invalid. Some of the later Malikis and others began to criticize Imam Al-Shafi’i for stipulating that in prayer, and they claimed that he was the only one who did that. Abu Ja’far Al-Tabari, Al-Tahawi, Al-Khattabi, and others narrated the consensus to the contrary, as Al-Qadi ‘Iyadh narrated from them. This speaker was arbitrary in his refutation of Al-Shafi’i, and he forced himself in his claim of consensus on that, and he said what he did not fully understand. We have narrated the obligation of that and the command to send blessings upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prayer, as is apparent in the verse, and this hadith is explained by a group of the Companions, including Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Mas’ud Al-Badri, and Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, and among the Successors: Al-Sha’bi and Abu Ja’far Al-Baqir. And Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and this is what Al-Shafi’i adopted, there is no disagreement on this from him or among his companions. Imam Ahmad adopted this finally, as narrated by Abu Zur’ah Al-Dimashqi, and it was also said by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and the jurist Imam Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as Ibn Al-Mawaz Al-Maliki may God have mercy on them. Even some of the Hanbali imams made it obligatory to say in sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings be upon him), as he taught them to say when they asked him. Even some of our companions made sending blessings upon his family obligatory, as narrated by Al-Bandaniji, Salim Al-Razi and his companion Nasr ibn Ibrahim Al-Maqdisi. It was narrated by Imam Al-Haramayn and his companion Al-Ghazali as a saying from Al-Shafi’i. The correct view is that the majority disagreed with it, and they narrated a consensus to the contrary. The view that it is obligatory is based on the apparent meanings of the hadith, and God knows best. The point is that Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, says that it is obligatory to pray for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prayer, both before and after, as mentioned above. Praise and thanks be to God. There is no consensus to the contrary on this issue, neither in the past nor in the present. And God knows best. What supports this is another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, and al-Nasa’i, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Hibban in their Sahihs, on the authority of Haywah ibn Shuraih al-Misri, on the authority of Abu Hani’ Hamid ibn Hani’, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik Abu Ali al-Junbi, on the authority of Fadalah ibn Ubayd, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man supplicating in his prayer without glorifying God or sending blessings upon the Prophet. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘This man has been in a hurry.’ Then he called him and said to him or to someone else: ‘When one of you prays, let him begin by glorifying and praising God Almighty, then let him send blessings upon the Prophet, then let him supplicate after that for whatever he wishes.’” Likewise, the hadith narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: ‘There is no prayer for one who does not perform ablution, and there is no ablution for one who does not mention the name of God over it, and there is no prayer for one who does not send blessings upon the Prophet, and there is no prayer for one who does not love the Ansar.’” But this Abd al-Muhaymin is rejected. At-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of his brother Ubayy ibn Abbas, but there is a view on that, and it is only known from the narration of Abdul-Muhaimin, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-A’ma, on the authority of Buraidah, who said: We said, O Messenger of God, we know how to greet you, but how do we pray for you? He said, “Say: O God, place Your prayers, mercy, and blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, just as You placed them upon Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.” Abu Dawud al-A’ma’s name is Nafi’ bin al-Harith, and he is rejected. Another hadith is suspended. We narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Mansour, Yazid bin Harun, and Zaid bin Al-Habbab, all three of them on the authority of Nuh bin Qais: Salamah Al-Kindi told us that Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to teach the people this supplication: O God, the Spreader of the spreads, the Creator of the heavens, and the Compeller of the hearts according to their nature: the wretched and the happy, make the best of Your prayers, the best of Your blessings, and the best of Your favors upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, the opener of what was closed, the seal of what came before, the proclaimer of the truth with the truth, and the destroyer of the armies of falsehood, as he bore it and undertook Your command for Your obedience, striving to please You, not slackening in his footing, nor weakening in his resolve, aware of Your revelation, keeping Your covenant, continuing to implement Your command until it lit a spark for a spark. The favors of God connect their causes to their people. Through it, hearts are guided after the immersion in temptations and sin, and the brightest of the clarifiers of the flags, the luminaries of the rulings, and the illuminators of Islam. He is Your trusted trustee, and the keeper of Your stored knowledge. And your witness on the Day of Judgment, and your messenger is a blessing, and your messenger with the truth is a mercy. O God, make your paradise spacious for him, and reward him with multiples of goodness from your grace, congratulations that are not tarnished, from the success of your permissible reward and your generous, abundant giving. O God, raise the building of the builders’ building above the building of the builders. And honor his abode and his place with you, and complete his light for him and reward him from your sending him with an accepted testimony, pleasing speech, with just logic, a clear plan, and a great argument and proof.
