This is a well-known statement of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Ibn Qutaybah spoke about it in his Mushkil al-Hadith, and so did Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Faris al-Lughawi in a volume he compiled on the virtue of sending prayers upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that there is a problem with its chain of transmission. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: This Salamah al-Kindi is not well-known and did not meet Ali, that is what he said. And the hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated this trace on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayegh on the authority of Saeed ibn Mansur: Nuh ibn Qays told us on the authority of Salamah al-Kindi who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to teach us to pray for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would say: O God, the Spreader of the spreads, and he mentioned it. Another hadith is not authentic. Ibn Majah said: Al-Husayn ibn Bayan told us, Ziyad ibn Abdullah told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Fakhita, on the authority of Al-Aswad ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: When you send blessings upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then send blessings upon him well, for you do not know, perhaps that will be presented to him. They said to him, Teach us. He said, “Say: ‘O God, make Your blessings, mercy, and blessings upon the Master of the Messengers, the Leader of the God-fearing, and the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, the Leader of goodness, the Guide to goodness, and the Messenger of Mercy. O God, raise him to a praiseworthy station that the first and the last will envy. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham, for You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, bless Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham, for You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” This is not authentic. Ismail Al-Qadi narrated something similar to this on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr or Omar, with some doubt about the narrator. Another hadith Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Abu Israel told us on the authority of Yunus bin Khabab, who said: He delivered a sermon to us in Persia and said: “Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation.” He said: Someone who heard Ibn Abbas say informed me: It was revealed thus, so we said: Or they said: O Messenger of God, we have been taught to greet you, but how do we send blessings on you? He said: “O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. Have mercy on Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You had mercy on the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. Bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.” This hadith is used as evidence by those who hold that it is permissible to ask for mercy for the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as is the opinion of the majority. It is supported by the hadith of the Bedouin who said: O God, have mercy on me and Muhammad, and do not have mercy on anyone else with us. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: You have restricted something that is too broad. Judge Iyad reported that the majority of the Malikis forbade it. He said: Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Zayd permitted it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Asim ibn `Ubayd God, who said: I heard `Abdullah ibn `Amir ibn Rabi`ah narrating on the authority of his father, who said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever sends blessings upon me, the angels will continue to send blessings upon him as long as he sends blessings upon me, so let a servant say little of that or do a lot of it.” Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Shu`bah with it. Another hadith Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Bandar told us, Muhammad bin Khalid bin Ashma told us, Musa bin Ya’qub Al-Zuma’i told me, Abdullah bin Kaysan told me that Abdullah bin Shaddad told him on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people closest to me on the Day of Resurrection will be those who send the most prayers upon me.” Al-Tirmidhi, may God have mercy on him, was the only one to narrate it, then he said: This is a good and rare hadith. Another hadith Ismail Al-Qadi said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yaqub bin Zaid bin Talha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Someone from my Lord came to me and said to me: There is no servant who sends blessings upon you except that God sends blessings upon him tenfold.’ A man stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, shall I not dedicate half of my supplication to you?’ He said: ‘If you wish.’ He said: ‘Shall I not dedicate two-thirds of my supplication to you?’ He said: ‘If you wish.’ He said: ‘Shall I not dedicate all of my supplication to you?’ He said: ‘Then God will suffice you from the worries of this world and the worries of the Hereafter.’” Then an old man in Mecca called Mani’ said to Sufyan, on the authority of the one who transmitted it: I do not know. Another hadith Ismail Al-Qadi said: Saeed bin Salam Al-Attar told us, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Abi bin Kaab, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out in the dead of night and say: ‘The first earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what it brings.’ My father said: ‘O Messenger of God, I pray at night. Should I dedicate a third of my prayer to you?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Half.’ He said: ‘Should I dedicate half of my prayer to you?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Two-thirds.’ He said: ‘Should I dedicate all of my prayer to you?’ He said: ‘Then God will forgive all of your sin.’” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in a similar manner, saying: Hannad told us, Qubaysah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of At-Tufayl bin Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of his father, who said: “When two-thirds of the night had passed, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would stand and say: ‘O people, remember God, remember God. The first earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what it brings. Death has come with what it brings.’ My father said: ‘I said, O Messenger of God, I send many prayers upon you, so how much of my prayers should I devote to you?’ He said: ‘Whatever you wish.’ I said: ‘A quarter?’ He said: ‘Whatever you wish, and if you do more, it is better for you.’ I said: ‘Then half?’ He said: ‘Whatever you wish, and if you do more, it is better for you.’ I said: ‘Two-thirds?’ He said: ‘Whatever you wish, and if you do more, it is better for you.’ I said: ‘Should I devote all of my prayers to you?’ He said: ‘Then your worries will be taken care of, and your sins will be forgiven.’” Then he said: This is a hasan hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Tufayl bin Ubayy, on the authority of his father, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think if I make all my prayers upon you? He said: Then God will suffice you in whatever concerns you of this world and the hereafter. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah Mansur bin Salamah Al-Khuza’i and Yunus, who is Ibn Muhammad, told us: Laith told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Haad, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Umar, on the authority of Abu Al-Huwairith, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubayr bin Mut’im, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, so I followed him until he entered a palm grove, and he prostrated and prolonged his prostration until I feared or was afraid that God had taken him or taken him. I came to look and he raised his head and said: What is the matter with you, Abd Al-Rahman? I mentioned that to him and he said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to me: Shall I not give you good report? God, the Almighty, says: Whoever prays upon you, I will pray upon him, and whoever greets you, I will greet him.” Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed, a client of Banu Hashim, told us, Sulayman ibn Bilal told us, Amr ibn Abi Amr ibn Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and headed towards his charity. He entered and faced the qiblah, then fell down in prostration and prolonged the prostration until I thought that God had taken his soul in it. I approached him and sat down, and he raised his head and said: Who is this? I said: Abd al-Rahman. He said: What is the matter with you? I said: O Messenger of God, I prostrated in a prostration in which I feared that God had taken your soul. He said: Gabriel came to me and gave me good report that God, the Almighty, says to you: Whoever prays for you, I pray for him, and whoever greets you, I greet him. So I prostrated to God, the Almighty, in gratitude.” Ismail ibn Ishaq al-Qadi narrated it in his book on the authority of Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid on the authority of al-Darawardi, on the authority of Amr ibn Abd al-Wahid on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf on his authority. He narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of… Abdulrahman. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim ibn Buhair ibn Abdullah ibn Muawiyah ibn Buhair Rayyan told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, Abdullah ibn Umar told me, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Yazid, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out for an errand and did not find anyone following him. Umar was alarmed and brought him a water-tub from behind him. He found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in a drinking place. He moved away from him from behind until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his head. He said: ‘Well done, Umar, when you found me prostrating and moved away from me. Gabriel came to me and said: Whoever from your nation sends blessings upon you once, God will send blessings upon him ten times and raise him ten degrees.’” This hadith was chosen by al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi in his book al-Mustakhraj ‘ala al-Sahihain. Ismail al-Qadi narrated it on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Salamah ibn Wardan, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Umar, in a similar manner. He also narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Hamid, on the authority of Anas ibn Ayyad, on the authority of Salamah bin Wardan, on the authority of Malik bin Aws bin Al-Hadathan, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, with a similar chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit bin Sulayman, the client of Al-Hasan bin Ali, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Talha, on the authority of his father, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came one day and joy was evident on his face. They said: O Messenger of God, we see joy on your face. He said: The angel came to me and said: O Muhammad, is it not pleasing to you that your Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, says: No one from your nation prays for you except that I pray for him ten times, and no one from your nation greets you except that I greet him ten times? I said: Yes.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah with this chain of transmission. Ismail Al-Qadi narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Uways, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Umar, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha, in a similar manner. Another chain of transmission Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Ka`b bin `Ujrah, on the authority of Abu Talha al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up one day in a good mood, and a smile could be seen on his face. They said: O Messenger of God, today I woke up in a good mood, and a smile could be seen on your face. He said: Yes, someone came to me from my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and said: Whoever from your nation sends a prayer upon you, God will write for him ten good deeds, erase ten bad deeds from him, raise him ten degrees, and return the same to him.” This is also a good chain of transmission, but they did not include it. Another Hadith Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ismail bin Ja’far, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever sends blessings upon me once, God will send blessings upon him ten times.’” Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith. There are other narrations on this topic on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf, Amir bin Rabi’ah, Ammar, Abu Talhah, Anas and Ubayy bin Ka’b. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn bin Muhammad narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Ka’b, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “On the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), who said: ‘Send blessings upon me, for it is a purification for you, and ask God to grant me Al-Wasilah, for it is a degree in the highest Paradise, and none will attain it except one man, and I hope that I will be that one.’” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Abu Hurayrah in a similar manner. He said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Bakali told us, Uthman ibn Sa`id told us, Dawud ibn `Ulayyah told us on the authority of Layth on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Pray for me, for it is a purification for you, and ask God for me the highest rank in Paradise.’ So we asked him, or he told us, and he said: ‘It is a rank in the highest part of Paradise, and it belongs to a man, and I hope that I will be that man.’” There are some who have spoken against it in its chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Marih al-Khawlani, I heard Abu Qais, the client of Amr bin al-‘As, I heard Abdullah bin Amr say: Whoever sends blessings upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God and His angels will send blessings upon him seventy times, so let a servant say little of that or say a lot. I heard Abdullah bin Amr say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us one day as if bidding farewell and said: I am Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet - he said it three times - and there is no prophet after me. I have been given the openings, endings, and comprehensive verses of speech, and I have been taught how many are the guardians of Hell and the bearers of the Throne, and through me I have been spared and my nation has been spared, so listen and obey as long as I am among you. But when I go, then adhere to the Book of God, make lawful what He has made lawful and forbid what He has made unlawful.” Another hadith Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Abu Salamah al-Khurasani told us, Abu Ishaq told us on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever mentions me in his presence, let him send blessings upon me, and whoever sends blessings upon me once, God will send blessings upon him ten times. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in Al-Yawm wa al-Laylah from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi on the authority of Abu Salamah, who is al-Mughirah ibn Muslim al-Khurasani, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Amr ibn Abdullah al-Subai’i on the authority of Anas on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Yunus bin Amr told us, meaning Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Burayd bin Abi Maryam, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever sends one prayer upon me, God will send ten prayers upon him, and ten sins will be removed from him.” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Malik bin Amr and Abu Saeed told us, they said: Sulayman bin Bilal told us, on the authority of Amara bin Ghazia, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The miser is the one who is mentioned in my presence and then does not send blessings upon me.” Abu Saeed said: Then he does not send blessings upon me. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman bin Bilal, then he said: This is a good, strange, and authentic hadith. Some of the narrators included it in the Musnad of Al-Hussein bin Ali, and some of them included it in the Musnad of Ali himself. Another hadith Ismail Al-Qadi said: Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ma’bad bin Bilal Al-Anzi, a man from Damascus told us, on the authority of Aouf bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most miserly of people is he who is mentioned in my presence and does not send blessings upon me. Another hadith is not transmitted. Ismail said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, I heard al-Hasan say, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is enough miserliness for a man that if I am mentioned in his presence he does not send blessings upon me.” Another hadith Al-Tirmidhi said: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi told us, Rabi’i bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘May the nose of a man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me be rubbed in the dust. May the nose of a man in whose presence the month of Ramadan comes and then passes before he is forgiven be rubbed in the dust. May the nose of a man in whose presence his parents reach old age and they do not admit him into Paradise be rubbed in the dust.’ Then he said: ‘Good and strange.’” I said: Al-Bukhari narrated it in Al-Adab on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubayd God: Ibn Abi Hazim told us on the authority of Kathir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. We narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with the same chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi said: There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Jabir and Anas. I said: And Ibn Abbas and Ka’b bin Ujrah. I have mentioned the chains of transmission of this hadith at the beginning of the Book of Fasting, when he said: Either one of them or both of them reach old age while you are alive. This hadith and the one before it are evidence of the obligation of sending blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned. It is the view of a group of scholars, including al-Tahawi and al-Halimi. It is strengthened by the other hadith narrated by Ibn Majah: Jabara bin al-Mughlis told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me has missed the path to Paradise.’” Jabara is weak, but Ismail al-Qadi narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali al-Baqir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me has missed the path to Paradise.’” This is a mursal hadith that is strengthened by the one before it, and God knows best. Others said that it is obligatory to pray for him once in a gathering, and then it is not obligatory in the rest of that gathering, rather it is recommended. Al-Tirmidhi transmitted this from some of them, and it is supported by the hadith narrated by Al-Tirmidhi: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salih, the freed slave of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A group of people do not sit in a gathering in which they do not mention God and do not pray for their Prophet except that it will be a cause of regret for them on the Day of Resurrection. If He wills, He will punish them, and if He wills, He will forgive them.” Al-Tirmidhi is the only one to narrate it from this source, and Imam Ahmad narrated it from Hajjaj and Yazid ibn Harun, both of them from Ibn Abi Dhi’b from Salih, the freed slave of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. It has been narrated from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), through more than one chain of transmission. Ismail al-Qadi narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Dhakwan, from Abu Sa'id, who said: "There are no people who sit and then stand without sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), except that it will be a cause of regret for them on the Day of Resurrection, even if they enter Paradise because of what they see of the reward." It has been narrated from some of them that sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is only obligatory once in a lifetime, in compliance with the command of the verse. Then it is recommended in all situations. This is what Qadi 'Iyadh supported after he reported the consensus on the obligation of sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in general. He said: Al-Tabarani reported that the verse is to be interpreted as recommended and claimed consensus on it. He said: Perhaps it is with regard to what is more than once, and what is obligatory in it is once, such as testifying to his prophethood. Whatever is more than that is recommended and encouraged from the traditions of Islam and the symbol of its people. I say This is a strange statement, because the command to send blessings upon him has been mentioned at many times, some of which are obligatory and some of which are recommended, as we will explain. From it, after the call to prayer, according to the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Haywah told us, Ka’b ibn Alqamah told us that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr say: He heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-’As say: “He heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘If you hear the muezzin, then say what he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me, God will send blessings upon him ten times. Then ask God to grant me al-Wasilah, for it is a station in Paradise that is not fitting for anyone but one of God’s servants, and I hope that I am he. Whoever asks God to grant me al-Wasilah, intercession will be granted to him.’” Narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ka’b ibn Alqamah. Another way Ismail Al-Qadi said: Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us, Amr bin Ali bin Abi Bakr Al-Jashmi told us, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks God for intercession for me, my intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection.” Another Hadith Ismail Al-Qadi said: Sulayman bin Harb told us, Saeed bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Pray for me, for your prayers for me are a purification for you, and ask God for me Al-Wasilah.’ He said: ‘Either he tells us or we ask him.’ He said: Al-Wasilah is the highest degree in Paradise, and none will attain it except one man, and I hope that I will be that man.’ Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mu’tamir, on the authority of Laith - who is Ibn Abi Sulaym - with this chain of transmission. And likewise the other Hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Bakr bin Sawadah told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Nu’aym, on the authority of Wafa’ Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Ruwayfi’ bin Thabit Al-Ansari, ‘That the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever sends prayers upon Muhammad and says: O God, place him in a seat close to You on the Day of Resurrection, my intercession is obligatory for him.’” This is a sound chain of transmission, and they did not include it. Another trace - Ismail Al-Qadi said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, Muammar told me, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, I heard Ibn Abbas say: O God, accept the great intercession of Muhammad and raise his status to the highest level, and grant him what he asks for in the Hereafter and in this world, as You gave to Abraham and Moses, peace be upon them. A good, strong, authentic chain of transmission. This includes when entering and exiting the mosque, as narrated by Imam Ahmad: Ismail bin Ibrahim told us, Laith bin Abi Salim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother Fatima bint Al-Hussein, on the authority of his grandmother Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque, he would send prayers upon Muhammad and grant him peace, then say: O God, forgive my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy. And when he left, he would send prayers upon Muhammad and grant him peace, then say: O God, forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your grace.” Ismail Al-Qadi said: Yahya bin Abdul Hamid narrated to us, Sufyan bin Omar Al-Tamimi narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: When you pass by the mosques, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). As for sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings be upon him) in prayer, we have already discussed it in the final tashahhud and those scholars who held this view, including Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him and honor him and Ahmad. As for the first tashahhud, it is not obligatory according to all opinions, and is it recommended? There are two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. Among these is sending blessings upon him (peace and blessings be upon him) in the funeral prayer. The Sunnah is to recite the Opening of the Book in the first takbir, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the second, supplicate for the deceased in the third, and say: O God, do not deprive us of his reward, and do not tempt us after him. Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: Mutraf ibn Mazin narrated to us from Muammar from Az-Zuhri: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunaif informed me that a man from the companions of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) informed him that the Sunnah in the funeral prayer is for the imam to say takbir, then recite Surat Al-Fatihah after the first takbir silently to himself, then send blessings upon the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and devote the supplication to the funeral. In the takbirs, he does not recite anything from them, then he says the taslim silently to himself. An-Nasa’i narrated it from Abu Umamah himself that he said: It is from the Sunnah, and he mentioned it. This from the companion is considered to be marfu’ according to the authentic hadith. Ismail Al-Qadi narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna from Abd Al-A’la from Muammar from Az-Zuhri from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl from Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab that he said: The Sunnah in the funeral prayer, and he mentioned it. And this is what was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Umar and Al-Sha'bi. Among that, regarding the Eid prayer, Ismail Al-Qadi said: Muslim bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Hisham Al-Dastawai narrated to us, Hammad bin Abi Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, that Al-Walid bin Uqbah came out to Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa and Hudhayfah one day before the Eid and said to them: The Eid is approaching, so how should we say Takbir during it? Abdullah said: You begin by saying Takbir to begin the prayer and praise your Lord and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then you supplicate and say Takbir and do the same. Then you say Takbir and do the same. Then you recite and say Takbir and bow. Then you stand and recite and praise your Lord and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then you supplicate and say Takbir and do the same, then you bow. Hudhayfah and Abu Musa said: Abu Abd Al-Rahman spoke the truth. The chain of transmission is sound. It is recommended to end the supplication with prayers upon him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Dawud told us, Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl told us, on the authority of Abu Qurrah Al-Asadi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, who said: The supplication is suspended between the heaven and the earth, and nothing of it ascends until you send prayers upon your Prophet. And Ayoub ibn Musa narrated it likewise, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab. It was narrated by Muadh ibn al-Harith on the authority of Abu Qurrah on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab on the authority of Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Razin ibn Muawiyah also narrated it in his book with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: “The supplication is suspended between the heaven and the earth and does not ascend until blessings are bestowed upon me. Do not make me like the rider’s immersion. Pray for me at the beginning, end, and middle of the supplication.” This addition is narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah in the Musnad of Imam Abd ibn Hamid al-Kashi, where he said: Ja’far ibn Awn told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, who said: Jabir said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: “Do not make me like the rider’s cup. When he gets hung up, he takes his cup and fills it with water. If he needs to perform ablution, he does so. If he needs to drink, he drinks, otherwise he pours out what is in it. Put me at the beginning of the supplication, in the middle of the supplication, and at the end of the supplication.” This is a strange hadith, and Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak in hadith. Among the most emphatic of these is the supplication of Qunut, as narrated by Ahmad, the People of Sunan, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, and Al-Hakim, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me words to say in Witr: ‘O God, guide me among those whom You have guided, grant me well-being among those whom You have granted well-being, take me under Your protection among those whom You have taken under Your protection, bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed. For You decree and none can decree against You. He whom You befriend shall not be humiliated, and he whom You take as an enemy shall not be honored. Blessed are You, our Lord, and exalted.’ Al-Nasa’i added to this in his Sunan, and may God’s prayers and peace be upon Muhammad.” It is recommended to increase your prayers for him on Friday and Friday night. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, on the authority of Abu al-Ash'ath al-San'ani, on the authority of Aws al-Thaqafi may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Among the best of your days is Friday. On it, Adam was created, on it he died, on it the Trumpet will be blown, and on it the Great Calamity will occur. So increase your prayers for me on it, for your prayers are presented to me.” They said: O Messenger of God, how are our prayers presented to you when you have decayed? He said: God has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi. This hadith was classed as saheeh by Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Daraqutni, and al-Nawawi in al-Adhkar. Another hadith Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Amr ibn Sawad al-Misri told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Ayman, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Increase your prayers for me on Friday, for it is witnessed and witnessed by the angels. No one prays for me on it except that his prayer is presented to me until he finishes it.’ I said: ‘And after death?’ He said: ‘God has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets, but God’s prophet is alive and well.’” This hadith is strange from this source, and there is a break in the chain of transmission between Ubadah ibn Nassi and Abu al-Darda’, for he did not meet him. And God knows best. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Abu Umamah and Ibn Mas`ud, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the command to increase prayers upon him on Friday night and day, but their chains of transmission are weak, and God knows best. It was narrated in a mursal form on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: Ismail al-Qadi said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, I heard al-Hasan al-Basri say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The earth will not consume the body of one to whom the Holy Spirit has spoken.’” It is a hasan mursal. Al-Qadi said: Al-Shafi`i said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad told us, Sufyan ibn Sulaym told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When it is Friday and Friday night, increase prayers upon me.’ This is a mursal. Thus, the preacher must send prayers upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on Friday from the pulpit in the two sermons, and the two sermons are not valid without that because it is an act of worship, and mentioning God is a condition for it, so mentioning the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is obligatory in it, like the call to prayer and the prayer. This is the view of al-Shafi`i and Ahmad, may God have mercy on them both. It is recommended to send blessings and peace upon him when visiting his grave (peace and blessings be upon him). Abu Dawud said: Ibn Awf - he is Muhammad - told us: Al-Maqri told us: Haywah told us, on the authority of Abu Sakhr Hamid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘There is none among you who sends peace upon me but that God restores my soul to me so that I may return his greeting.’” This is narrated only by Abu Dawud and authenticated by Al-Nawawi in Al-Adhkar. Then Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Salih told us: I read on the authority of Abdullah ibn Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: ‘Do not make your homes into graves, and do not make my grave a place of celebration. Send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are.’” This is also narrated only by Abu Dawud. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Surayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Nafi’ - he is Al-Sayegh - and Al-Nawawi also authenticated it. It was narrated from another chain of transmission. Judge Ismail bin Ishaq said in his book The Virtue of Sending Blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ismail bin Abi Uways told us, Jaafar bin Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Jaafar bin Abi Talib told us, on the authority of someone from his family who told him, on the authority of Ali bin al-Husayn bin Ali, that a man used to come every morning and visit the grave of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pray for him and do what Ali bin al-Husayn was famous for. Ali bin al-Husayn said to him: What makes you do this? He said: I love to greet the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ali bin al-Husayn said to him: Would you like me to tell you a hadith on the authority of my father? He said: Yes. Ali bin Al-Hussein told him: My father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not make my grave a place of celebration, and do not make your homes graves. Send prayers upon me and greet me wherever you are, for your prayers and greetings will reach me.” In its chain of transmission is an unknown man who was not named. It has been narrated from another source as a mursal. Abd Al-Razzaq said in his Musannaf, on the authority of Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of a man called Suhayl, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Al-Hasan bin Ali, who said: He saw some people at a grave and forbade them, saying: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not make my grave a place of celebration, and do not make your homes graves. Send prayers upon me wherever you are, for your prayers will reach me.” Perhaps he saw them being ill-mannered by raising their voices more than necessary, so he forbade them. It has been narrated that he saw a man visiting a grave and said: O man, you and a man in Andalusia are the same from him, meaning that everyone will receive the prayers and greetings of God be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. Al-Tabarani said in his great dictionary: Ahmad bin Rushdin Al-Masry told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, Hamid bin Abi Zainab told me, on the authority of Hassan bin Hassan bin Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pray for me wherever you are, for your prayers reach me. Then Al-Tabarani said: Al-Abbas bin Hamdan Al-Isfahani told us, Shuaib bin Abdul Hamid Al-Tahhan told us, Yazid bin Harun bin Abi Shaiban told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abdullah bin Khattab, on the authority of Umm Anis bint Al-Hasan bin Ali, on the authority of her father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Have you seen the statement of God Almighty: ‘Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet’? He said: This is among the concealed things, and had you not asked me about it, I would not have told you. God Almighty has assigned two angels to me. If I am mentioned in the presence of a Muslim slave and he sends blessings on me, those two angels say: May God forgive you. And God and His angels say in response to those two angels: Amen. And no one sends blessings on me.” No one but those two angels said: May God forgive you, and God and His angels said in response to those two angels: Amen.” Very strange, and its chain of transmission is very weak. Imam Ahmad said: “Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God has angels who travel around the earth and convey to me the greetings of my nation.”’” This is how al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A’mash, both on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Sa’ib. As for the other hadith, Whoever sends blessings upon me at my grave, I hear him, and whoever sends blessings upon me from afar, I hear him, its chain of transmission is questionable. It was narrated by Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi al-Saghir alone, and he is rejected. It was narrated on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Our companions said: It is recommended for the pilgrim, when he has recited the Talbiyah and finished, to send blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, based on what Al-Shafi’i and Ad-Daraqutni narrated from Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za’idah, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr As-Siddiq, who said: A man was commanded, when he finished his Talbiyah, to send blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in every situation. Ismail Al-Qadi said: Arim ibn Al-Fadl told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Zakariya told us, from Al-Sha’bi, from Wahb ibn Al-Ajda’, who said: I heard Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: When you arrive, circumambulate the House seven times and pray two rak’ahs at the Maqam, then go to Al-Safa and stand on it from where you can see the House and say Allahu Akbar seven times, a takbir between praising and thanking God, sending blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asking for yourself. And on Al-Marwah the same, with a good, good, and strong chain of transmission. They said: It is recommended to send blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, along with mentioning God when slaughtering, and they took as an example the words of God Almighty: And We have raised high for you your fame. Some of the commentators said: God Almighty says: I do not remember except that it is mentioned with me. The majority disagreed with them on this and said: This is a place where mention of God Almighty is singled out, such as when eating, entering, having intercourse, and other things in which the Sunnah did not mention sending blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another hadith Ismail Al-Qadi said: Muhammad bin Abi Bakr Al-Muqaddami told us, Amr bin Harun told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Thabit, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Pray for God’s prophets and messengers, for God sent them as He sent me.’” In its chain of transmission are two weak narrators, namely Amr bin Harun and his sheikh, and God knows best. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Ath-Thawri on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah Al-Rabdhi on his authority. Among the evidence for that is that it is recommended to pray for him when the ear rings, if the report about that is authentic, as Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih and said: Ziyad bin Yahya told us, Muammar bin Muhammad bin Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Rafi’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If the ear of one of you rings, let him remember me and send blessings upon me and say: ‘May God remember whoever remembers me with good.’” Its chain of transmission is strange, but its authenticity is questionable, and God knows best. Question The scribes prefer that the scribe repeats the prayer upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) every time he writes. It was reported in the hadith through Kadah bin Rahmah, on the authority of Nahshal, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever prays upon me in a book, the prayer will continue to be valid for him as long as my name is in that book.’” This hadith is not authentic for many reasons. It was reported on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, but it is also not authentic. Al-Hafiz Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahabi, our Sheikh, said: I think it is fabricated. Something similar was reported on the authority of Abu Bakr and Ibn Abbas, but none of it is authentic, and God knows best. Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi mentioned in his book Al-Jami’ Ladab Al-Rawi Wa Al-Sami’: I saw in the handwriting of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal may God have mercy on him that the name of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was often written without mentioning the prayer upon him in writing. He said: I was informed that he used to pray upon him verbally. Chapter As for praying for other than the prophets, if it is by way of subordination as mentioned in the hadith: O God, bless Muhammad and his family and his wives and his offspring, then this is permissible by consensus. Rather, the dispute arose over whether other than the prophets were singled out for prayer. Some said: This is permissible, and they cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, and His words: On them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and His words: Take alms from their wealth to purify them and sanctify them thereby, and pray for them, and the hadith of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: “When people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with their alms, he would say: O God, pray for them. So my father came to him with his alms, and he said: O God, pray for the family of Abi Awfa.” They included it in the two Sahihs. And the hadith of Jabir, that his wife said: O Messenger of God, pray for me and my husband, and he said: May God bless you and your husband. The majority of scholars said: It is not permissible to single out other than the prophets for prayer, because this has become a slogan for the prophets when they are mentioned, so no one else is included with them, so it is not said: Abu Awfa said: Bakr, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, or Ali, may God bless him and grant him peace, even if the meaning is correct, just as it is not said: Muhammad, the Almighty and Majestic, said, even if he is honorable and noble, because this is a symbol of the remembrance of God, the Almighty and Majestic, and they interpreted what was mentioned in this regard in the Book and Sunnah as a supplication for them, and for this reason it was not proven to be a symbol for the family of Abu Awfa nor for Jabir and his wife, and this is a good approach. Others said: This is not permissible because praying for people other than the prophets has become a symbol of the people of whims. They pray for those they believe in, so they should not be followed in that, and God knows best. Then those who forbid it differed: Is it a matter of prohibition, reprehensibility, or something contrary to what is best? There are three opinions, as reported by Sheikh Abu Zakariya al-Nawawi in his book Al-Adhkar. Then he said: The correct opinion, which is held by the majority, is that it is reprehensible because it is a symbol of the people of innovation, and we have been forbidden from their symbol, and reprehensible is that which has a deliberate prohibition. Our companions said, and the reliance in that is that prayer has become specific in the language of the Salaf to the prophets, just as our saying Glory be to God is specific to God Almighty. Just as you do not say Muhammad even though he is dear and great, you do not say Abu Bakr or Ali (peace be upon them). This is pronounced verbatim. He said: As for peace? Sheikh Abu Muhammad al-Juwayni, one of our companions, said: It is in the meaning of prayer, so it is not used for the absent, nor is it used exclusively for anyone other than the prophets, so it is not said to Ali, peace be upon him, and this is the same in this regard for the living and the dead. As for the present, it is addressed to him, so it is said: Peace be upon you, and peace be upon you, or peace be upon you, or upon you. This is agreed upon. What he mentioned ends. I said This has been prevalent in the expression of many copyists of books, that Ali, may God be pleased with him, is the only one to be called peace be upon him, without the rest of the companions, or may God honor his face. And even though its meaning is correct, the companions should be treated equally in this, because this is a matter of glorification and honor. The two sheikhs and the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman, are more deserving of this than him, may God be pleased with them all. Ismail Al-Qadi said: Abdullah bin Abdul-Wahhab bin Ziyad narrated to us, Uthman bin Hakim bin Ubadah bin Haneef narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: It is not valid to send blessings upon anyone except the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, but one should supplicate for forgiveness for Muslim men and women. He also said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Husayn bin Ali narrated to us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Burqan, who said: Umar bin Abdul-Aziz, may God have mercy on him, wrote: As for what follows, some people have sought this world through the deeds of the Hereafter, and some storytellers have introduced into their prayers for their caliphs and leaders something equal to the prayers for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. So when this letter of mine reaches you, order them to send blessings upon the prophets and their supplications for the Muslims in general, and to leave everything else. A good report. Ismail Al-Qadi said: Muadh bin Asad told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Khalid bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Nabih bin Wahb, that Ka’b entered upon Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and they mentioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ka’b said: There is no dawn except that seventy thousand angels descend until they surround the grave, beating their wings and praying for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seventy thousand at night and seventy thousand during the day, until the earth splits open and he emerges with seventy thousand angels escorting him. Branch Al-Nawawi said: If one prays for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he should combine the prayer and the greeting, and not limit himself to one of them. He should not say: “May God bless him and grant him peace” only, nor “May peace be upon him and grant him peace” only. What he said is taken from this noble verse, which is His statement: “O you who have believed, pray for him and greet him with peace.” So it is better to say: “May God bless him and grant him peace”
33:57: God the Almighty says, threatening and warning those who harm Him by disobeying His commands, committing His prohibitions, persisting in doing so, and harming His Messenger with a defect or shortcoming - may God protect us from that - Ikrimah said regarding the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger it was revealed about the image-makers. In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty says: The son of Adam harms Me, cursing time, and I am time, I alternate its night and day." The meaning of this is that the people of ignorance used to say, What a disappointment! Time has done such and such to us! Thus they would attribute the actions of God the Almighty to time and curse it, while the one who did that is God the Almighty, so He forbade that. This is what al-Shafi'i, Abu Ubaidah, and other scholars, may God have mercy on them, decided. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for marrying him to Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. It appears that the verse is general and includes everyone who harms him in any way, and whoever harms him has harmed God, just as whoever obeys him has obeyed God, as Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us: Ibrahim ibn Sa’d told us, on the authority of Ubaidah ibn Abi Rai’ah al-Hadha’ al-Tamimi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Take care of my companions, do not take them as a target after me. Whoever loves them loves them because of my love, and whoever hates them hates them because of my hatred. Whoever harms them has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed God. Whoever harms God is likely to be seized by Him.’” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ubaidah ibn Abi Rai’ah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal, with this chain of transmission. Then he said: This is a strange hadith, which we do not know except from this source. God the Almighty says: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned meaning, they attribute to them something they are innocent of, which they did not do or commit, they have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin. This is the grave slander, to relate or transmit about believing men and women something they did not do, by way of faultfinding and disparaging them. Those who are most subject to this threat are the disbelievers in God and His Messenger, then the Rafidah, who disparage the Companions and find fault with them for things God has declared them innocent of, and they describe them with the opposite of what God has told us about them. God the Almighty has told us that He was pleased with the Muhajireen and Ansar and praised them, but these ignorant fools slander them, disparage them, and mention things about them that they never did or committed. They are, in reality, people with upturned hearts who criticize those who are praised and praise those who are criticized. Abu Dawud said: Al-Qa'nabi told us: Abdul Aziz, meaning Ibn Muhammad, told us, on the authority of Al-Ala', on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that it was said: O Messenger of God, what is backbiting? He said: It is mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes. It was said: What if what I say is true in my brother? He said: If what you say is true in him, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is not true in him, then you have slandered him. And this is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Ad-Darawardi, who then said: It is hasan saheeh good and authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad Ibn Salamah told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Mu'awiyah Ibn Hisham told us, on the authority of Ammar Ibn Anas, on the authority of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, on the authority of Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: 'Which usury is the greatest usury in the sight of God?' They said: God and His Messenger know best." He said: The greatest usury in the sight of God is making permissible the honor of a Muslim man. Then he recited: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin.

33:59: God the Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command the believing women - especially his wives and daughters because of their honor - to draw their jilbabs over themselves to distinguish themselves from the traits of the women of the Age of Ignorance and the traits of female slaves. The jilbab is the cloak over the khimar, as stated by Ibn Masoud, Ubaidah, Qatadah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and others. It is like the izar today. Al-Jawhari said: The jilbab is the cloak. A woman from the tribe of Hudhayl said, mourning one of her dead men: Eagles walk towards him, heedless, like virgins wearing their robes. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that God commanded the believing women, when they went out of their homes for some need, to cover their faces from above their heads with their jilbabs and to show one eye. Muhammad bin Sirin said that I asked Ubaidah Al-Salmani about the saying of God the Almighty: {and draw their cloaks over their faces} so he covered his face and head and exposed his left eye. Ikrimah said that she covered the opening of her throat with her jilbab, drawing it over it. Ibn Abi Hatim said that Abu Abdullah Al-Tehrani told us in what he wrote to me, that Abdul Razzaq told us, that Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Khaitham, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaiba, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said that when this verse was revealed, {and draw their cloaks over their faces}, the women of the Ansar went out as if there were crows on their heads because of the tranquility, and they were wearing black cloaks. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Saleh told us, Al-Layth told us, Yunus bin Yazid told us. He said: We asked him, meaning Al-Zuhri: Does a slave girl have to wear a khimar, whether she is married or unmarried? He said: She has to wear a khimar if she is married. She is forbidden from wearing a jilbab because it is disliked for them to resemble free, chaste women, and God the Most High said: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri that he said: There is nothing wrong with looking at the adornment of the women of the People of the Covenant. He only forbade that for fear of temptation, not because they are sacred. He provided evidence for that by the words of God the Most High: and the women of the believers and His words: That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused, meaning that if they do that, it will be known that they are free women, not slaves or prostitutes. Al-Suddi said about the verse: “O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That will be more suitable that they will be known and not be abused.” He said: There were some wicked people from the people of Medina who would go out at night when darkness fell into the streets of Medina to harass women, and the dwellings of the people of Medina were cramped. When night fell, the women would go out into the streets to relieve themselves, and those wicked people would seek that from them. If they saw a woman wearing a outer garment, they would say, This is a free woman, so they would refrain from approaching her. If they saw a woman without a outer garment, they would say, This is a slave woman, so they would pounce on her. Mujahid said that they would cover themselves so that it would be known that they were free, so no wicked person would approach them with harm or suspicion. And the Almighty’s saying: And God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning for what happened in the days of ignorance when they did not have knowledge of that. Then the Almighty said, threatening the hypocrites, who are those who show faith but conceal disbelief, and those in whose hearts is disease Ikrimah and others said they are the adulterers here, and the agitators in the city meaning those who say the enemies have come and the wars have come, which is a lie and slander, if they do not desist from that and return to the truth, We will surely tempt you against them Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning we will give you power over them. Qatada said, We will surely stir you up with them. Al-Suddi said, We will teach you about them. “Then they will not be your neighbors therein” meaning in the city except for a little while, cursed is a condition of them during their short stay in the city, expelled and banished. Wherever they are found meaning they are found, they will be seized because of their humiliation and small number and killed in a terrible slaughter. Then the Most High said, The way of God with those who passed on before meaning this is His way with the hypocrites if they rebel against their hypocrisy and disbelief and do not turn back from what they are doing, that the people of faith will prevail over them and subjugate them. And you will not find any change in the way of God meaning the way of God in that is not changed or altered.

Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.”
33:67: God Almighty says, informing His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he has no knowledge of the Hour, even if people ask him about it. He guided him to refer its knowledge to God Almighty, as God Almighty said in Surat Al-A’raf, which is Meccan, and this is Medinan. So the situation of referring its knowledge to the One who establishes it continued, but He informed him that it is near, saying: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near, as God Almighty said: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split, and He said: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away, and He said: The command of God has come, so do not hasten it, then He said: Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers, that is, He has distanced them from His mercy, and has prepared for them a Blaze, that is, in the Hereafter, to abide therein forever, that is, remaining continuously, so they will not leave it or be removed from it. They will find neither protector nor helper, that is, they will have no helper or supporter to save them from what they are in. Then He said: On the Day when their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say, ‘Oh, if only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!’ That is, they will be dragged on their faces into the Fire, and their faces will be twisted in Hellfire. They will say, while they are like this, that they wished that they had been among those who obeyed God and the Messenger in this world, as God has informed us about them in the state of the gathering places, saying: “And on the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying, ‘Oh, would that I had taken with the Messenger a way. Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend. He led me astray from the message after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter.’” And God Almighty has also said: Perhaps those who disbelieve would wish that they had been Muslims. Thus, He has informed us about them in this state, that they wish that they had obeyed God and the Messenger in this world, and they will say, ‘Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the way.’ Tawus said, Our masters means the nobles, and our dignitaries means the scholars. Our Lord, give them double the punishment, meaning because of their disbelief and their misleading us. And curse them with a great curse. Some reciters read it with a unified Ba’, and others read it with a triple Tha’, and both are close in meaning, as in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr that Abu Bakr said, O Messenger of God, teach me a supplication that I may say in my prayer. He said, Say, ‘O God, I have wronged myself greatly, and no one forgives sins except You, so forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me, for You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.’ Both of them were reported in the two Sahihs. It is narrated as much and great, and both have a correct meaning. Some of them preferred that the supplicant combine the two expressions in his supplication, and there is consideration in that. 33:69: Al-Bukhari said in his interpretation of this verse: Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Awf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Muhammad, and Khulas, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses was a modest man, and this is what God Almighty said: ‘O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God.’” This is how he mentioned this hadith here, very abbreviated. He narrated it in the hadiths of the prophets with this same chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses, peace be upon him, was a modest, discreet man, and nothing of his skin was visible out of modesty. Those of the Children of Israel who harmed him harmed him, and they said: He only covers himself this way because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a skin disease. God Almighty wanted to clear them of what they said to Moses, peace be upon him, so he was alone one day and took off his clothes on a stone. Then he washed himself, and when he finished, he went to his clothes to take them, and the stone ran away with his clothes, so Moses took his staff and asked the stone and kept saying: My clothes are a stone, my clothes are a stone, until he reached a group of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, the most beautiful thing that God Almighty created, and he was innocent of what they said. The stone stood up, took his clothes, put them on, and began to strike the stone with his staff. By God, there were scars on the stone from the effect of striking it three, four, or five times. He said: That is what God Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God. This is a good, lengthy context, and this hadith is from the only one narrated by Bukhari, not Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh narrated to us, Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Khalas and Muhammad narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said concerning this verse: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses; but God cleared him of what they said, and he was esteemed in the sight of God. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses was a modest and discreet man. Hardly anything of his skin could be seen out of shyness before him.” Then he cited the hadith as Al-Bukhari narrated it in full. He narrated it on his authority in his Tafsir on the authority of Ruh on the authority of Aouf on his authority. And Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ath-Thawri on the authority of Jabir Al-Ju’fi on the authority of Amir Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. And thus he narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Do not be like those who harmed Moses, he said: His people said to him, You are impure. So he went out one day to wash and placed his clothes on a rock. The rock came out, tying his clothes to it, and he went out following it naked until he took him to the gatherings of the Children of Israel and they saw that he was not impure. So that is what his statement means: So God cleared him of what they said. And thus al-Awfi narrated it from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ruh bin Hatim and Ahmad bin Al-Mu’alla Al-Adami told us: Yahya bin Hammad told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Moses, peace be upon him, was a shy man. He came to the water - I think he said - to bathe, and he placed his clothes on a rock, and his private parts were hardly visible. The Children of Israel said, ‘Moses has a disease or something wrong with him’ - meaning that he did not remove his clothes - so the rock carried his clothes until they were right next to where the Children of Israel were sitting. They looked at Moses as the most handsome of men - or something like that - and that is what His statement means: ‘So God cleared him of what they said, and he was esteemed in the sight of God.’” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, regarding His statement: Then God cleared him of what they said, he said: Moses and Aaron ascended the mountain and Aaron, peace be upon him, died. The Children of Israel said to Moses, peace be upon him: “You killed him. He was kinder to us than you and more modest.” So they hurt him because of that. Then God ordered the angels to carry him and they passed by the gatherings of the Children of Israel. It spoke of his death and no one knew the location of his grave except the marble. God made him deaf and mute. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Musa Al-Tusi, on the authority of Ibad bin Al-Awam, and then he said: It is possible that this is what is meant by the hurt and it is possible that the first is what is meant. There is no more correct statement than God Almighty’s statement: I said. It is possible that all of them are meant or that there is something else with it, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided something one day, and a man from the Ansar said: ‘This division is not for the sake of God.’ I said: ‘O enemy of God, will I not tell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what I have said?’ I mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his face turned red, then he said: ‘May God have mercy on Moses. He was harmed more than this, and he was patient.’” They both included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Sulayman ibn Mihran Al-A’mash. Another chain of transmission - Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, I heard Isra’il ibn Yunus, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, the client of Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Zaid ibn Za’idah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Let no one inform me of anything from any of my companions, for I would like to come out to you with a sound heart. So wealth came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he divided it up. He said: I passed by two men, and one of them was saying to his companion: By God, Muhammad did not intend by his division the face of God or the Hereafter. He said: I checked until I heard what they said, then I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, you told us that no one should inform me of anything from my companions, and I passed by so-and-so and so-and-so, and they were saying such-and-such. The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned red and he was upset, then he said: Leave me alone, for Moses was harmed with more than this, and he was patient. Abu Dawud narrated it in Al-Adab on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Dhuhli on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Faryabi on the authority of Isra’il on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, with this abbreviated version: Let none of my companions convey to me anything from anyone, for I like to come out to you with a pure heart. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way in Al-Manaqib on the authority of Al-Dhuhli, except that he said Zayd ibn Za’idah. He also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Musa and Husayn ibn Muhammad, both of them on the authority of Isra’il on the authority of Al-Suddi on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Abi Hisham, with this also abbreviated version. He added Al-Suddi to its chain of transmission, then he said: It is strange from this source. God the Almighty said: And he was held in high esteem by God meaning he had esteem and prestige with his Lord, the Almighty. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that his supplications were answered by God. Others from the Salaf said that he never asked God for anything except that He gave it to him, but He withheld seeing him as He willed. Some of them said that because of his great esteem with God, he interceded for his brother Aaron that God would send him with him, so God answered his request and said: And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet.
33:70: God the Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him and to worship Him as if He sees them, and to say right words, meaning straight, without crookedness or deviation. He promised them that if they do that, He will reward them for it by making their deeds right, meaning He will guide them to do righteous deeds and forgive them their past sins. He will inspire them to repent for whatever they may do in the future. Then God the Almighty says: And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment, meaning that he will be saved from the fire of Hell and will be granted eternal bliss. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Awf told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the noon prayer. When he finished, he gestured to us with his hand, so we sat down and said: God Almighty has commanded me to command you to fear God and to speak words of right judgment. Then he came to the women and said: God has commanded me to command you to fear God and to speak words of right judgment. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said in Kitab At-Taqwa: Muhammad bin Abbad bin Musa told us, Abdul Aziz bin Imran Al-Zuhri told us, Isa bin Samra told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did not stand on the pulpit except that I heard him say: O you who have believed, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice, the verse. Very strange. It was narrated on the authority of Abdul Rahim bin Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with an interrupted chain of transmission: Whoever wants to be the most honorable of people, let him fear God. Ikrimah said: The appropriate statement is There is no god but God. Another said: The appropriate statement is truthfulness. Mujahid said: It is correctness. Another said: It is the truth, and all of it is true.
