33:72: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What he meant by the trust is obedience, and He offered it to them before offering it to Adam, but they could not bear it. So He said to Adam: I have offered the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they could not bear it. Will you accept what is in it? He said: O Lord, what is in it? He said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. So Adam took it and bore it, and that is what the Almighty said: {And man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The trust is the obligations. God offered it to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. If they fulfill it, He will reward them, and if they neglect it, He will punish them. So they hated that and feared it, without disobeying Him, but out of respect for the religion of God, so that they would not fulfill it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it, and that is what the Almighty said: {And man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} Meaning, he was deceived by the command of God. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bishr told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it. He said: It was offered to Adam and He said: Take it with what is in it. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you. He said: I accept. It was only the time between the afternoon and the night of that day that he committed the sin. Ad-Dahhak narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, but there is some doubt about it and a disconnect between Ad-Dahhak and him, and God knows best. This is what Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: Trust is the obligatory duties. Others said: It is obedience. Al-A`mash said, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka`b said: Part of trust is that a woman is entrusted with her private parts. Qatada said: Trust is religion, obligatory duties, and prescribed punishments. Some of them said it is ritual bathing after sexual impurity. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: Trust is three things: prayer, fasting, and ritual bathing after sexual impurity. All of these sayings do not contradict each other, but rather they are in agreement and go back to the fact that it is an obligation and acceptance of commands and prohibitions with its condition, which is that if he does that, he will be rewarded, and if he leaves it, he will be punished. So man accepts it despite his weakness, ignorance, and injustice, except for the one whom God guides, and with God is help sought. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdul Aziz bin Al-Mughira Al-Basri told us, Hammad bin Waqid - meaning Abu Omar Al-Saffar - told us, I heard Abu Muammar - meaning Awn bin Muammar narrating on the authority of Al-Hasan - meaning Al-Basri - that he recited this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains [Al-Hasan - meaning Al-Basri], he said: He offered it to the seven layers of paths adorned with stars, and the bearers of the Mighty Throne. It was said to them: Will you bear the Trust and what is in it? They said: And what is in it? He said: It was said to them: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. They said: No. Then it was offered to the seven strong earths, which were held down with pegs and made smooth with beds. He said: It was said to them: Will you bear the Trust and what is in it? They said: And what is in it? He said: It was said to them: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. They said: No. Then it was offered to the lofty, high, difficult, and hard mountains. He said: It was said to them: Will you bear the Trust and what is in it? They said: And what is in it? He said to her: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. She said: No. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said that when God created His creation, He gathered together mankind, jinn, the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. He began with the heavens and offered them the trust, which is obedience. He said to them: Will you bear this trust, but with grace, honor, and reward in Paradise? They said: O Lord, we are not able to do this and we do not have the strength, but we are obedient to You. Then He offered the trust to the earths and said to them: Will you bear this trust and accept it from Me, and I will give you grace and honor in this world? They said: We have no patience for this, O Lord, and we cannot bear it, but we are obedient and listen to You. We will not disobey You in anything You command us to do. Then He brought Adam near and said to him: Will you bear this trust and protect it with the care it deserves? Then Adam said: What do I have with You? He said: O Adam, if you do good, obey, and fulfill the trust, then you will have honor, favor, and a good reward in Paradise. But if you disobey, do not fulfill the trust as it should be fulfilled, and do wrong, then I will punish you, chastise you, and send you to Hell. He said: I am satisfied, O Lord, and I will bear it. Then God, the Almighty, said: I have burdened you with it. This is what God, the Almighty, said: {And man bore it.} Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Mujahid said: He presented it to the heavens, and they said: O Lord, the stars and the inhabitants of the heavens bore me, and what was mentioned, and I do not desire any reward, nor do I bear an obligation. He said: He presented it to the earth, and it said: O Lord, I have been planted in the trees, and I have been made to run in the rivers, and the inhabitants of the earth, and what was mentioned, and I do not desire any reward, nor do I bear an obligation. The mountains said the same. God, the Almighty, said: {And man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} concerning the outcome of his affair. Ibn Jurayj said the same. On the authority of Ibn Ashwa’, he said: When God offered them the responsibility of carrying the trust, they cried out to God for three days and nights, and said: Our Lord, we have no strength to work, nor do we want the reward. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Harun bin Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa Al-Mawsili told us, my father told us, Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, regarding this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth (Al-A’raf 2:17), the human being said: Between my ears and my shoulders, and God, the Almighty, said: “I will help you with it. I will help you with your eyes in two layers, so if he urges you to do something you dislike, close them. I will help you with your tongue in two layers, so if he urges you to do something you dislike, close them. I will help you with your private parts in clothing, so do not uncover them to something I dislike.” Then something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Abu Hazim. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God the Most High: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains (al-Baqarah 2:170), he said: God the Most High offered them the Trust, that He would impose upon them the religion and make for them a reward and a punishment, and that He would entrust them with the religion, but they said: “No, we are subject to Your command. We do not want reward or punishment.” He said: And God the Most High offered it to Adam and said: Between my ears and my shoulders. Ibn Zayd said: God the Most High said to him: “As long as you bear this, I will help you. I will make a veil for your sight, so if you fear looking at what is not permissible for you, then lower its veil over it. 33:73: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What he meant by the trust is obedience, and He offered it to them before offering it to Adam, but they could not bear it. So He said to Adam: I have offered the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they could not bear it. Will you accept what is in it? He said: O Lord, what is in it? He said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. So Adam took it and bore it, and that is what the Almighty said: {And man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The trust is the obligations. God offered it to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. If they fulfill it, He will reward them, and if they neglect it, He will punish them. So they hated that and feared it, without disobeying Him, but out of respect for the religion of God, so that they would not fulfill it. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it, and that is what the Almighty said: {And man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.} Meaning, he was deceived by the command of God. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bishr told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning this verse: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it. He said: It was offered to Adam and He said: Take it with what is in it. If you obey, I will forgive you, and if you disobey, I will punish you. He said: I accept. It was only the time between the afternoon and the night of that day that he committed the sin. Ad-Dahhak narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, but there is some doubt about it and a disconnect between Ad-Dahhak and him, and God knows best. This is what Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: Trust is the obligatory duties. Others said: It is obedience. Al-A`mash said, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka`b said: Part of trust is that a woman is entrusted with her private parts. Qatada said: Trust is religion, obligatory duties, and prescribed punishments. Some of them said it is ritual bathing after sexual impurity. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: Trust is three things: prayer, fasting, and ritual bathing after sexual impurity. All of these sayings do not contradict each other, but rather they are in agreement and go back to the fact that it is an obligation and acceptance of commands and prohibitions with its condition, which is that if he does that, he will be rewarded, and if he leaves it, he will be punished. So man accepts it despite his weakness, ignorance, and injustice, except for the one whom God guides, and with God is help sought. He said: It was said to them: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. They said: And what is in it? He said: It was said to them: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. They said: No. Then it was offered to the lofty, high, difficult, and hard mountains. He said: It was said to them: Will you bear the Trust and what is in it? They said: And what is in it? He said to her: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished.
